## DE-PRISM-MOMENTUM-REGISTRY-001 — Technicals momentum family closes the last `_INDICATOR_REGISTRY` gap (2026-07-03)

Branch: `feat/prism-momentum-registry` | Base: `origin/main` d2fff55 (DE-PRISM-NUMERIC-VERIFY-001, PR #90) | HEAD: a621497

### Problem

The 2026-07-03 post-deploy verification of DE-PRISM-NUMERIC-VERIFY-001 (see addendum above) found the numeric verifier's only real-world gap: every `momentum_<TICKER>_20d` citation the council emits resolves `unverifiable` — 4 of 24 real citations that day, 100% of the unverifiable count — because `_INDICATOR_REGISTRY` had no entry for the technicals `momentum` family (only `breadth` was registered from that lens).

### Decision: 10 literal registry entries, absolute tolerance, magnitude derived from live citation precision

`advisors/prism_numeric_verifier.py` gains one named constant (`_MOMENTUM_TOLERANCE = 0.001`) and 10 literal `_INDICATOR_REGISTRY` entries — `momentum_<TICKER>_20d -> ("technicals", "momentum.<TICKER>", "absolute", _MOMENTUM_TOLERANCE)` — one per ticker in `lens_technicals._PROXY_UNIVERSE` (SPY, QQQ, IWM, EFA, AGG, GLD, XLF, XLE, XLV, XLI). Registered as literal keys, not the fundamentals wildcard shape — a ticker outside the fixed proxy universe (e.g. `momentum_TSLA_20d`) stays `unverifiable`, never silently matched. Total diff: 16 lines; `_classify`, `_resolve_dotted_path`, `_lookup_registry_entry` untouched.

**Scope decision (PM, over the recon's narrower default): register all 10 proxy tickers, not just the 4 seen live.** The recon that scoped this cycle found only 4 tickers (SPY/QQQ/XLV/XLF) actually cited in the one verified production run. Registering only those 4 would have left the other 6 proxy-universe tickers silently unverifiable the first time the council happened to cite one of them on a future night. All 10 are registered up front.

**Absolute, not relative, tolerance — same reasoning as `breadth`.** Momentum is a naturally bounded ~+/-0.15 20-day-return fraction that legitimately sits near and crosses zero. A relative tolerance (`_classify()`'s relative branch divides by `|truth|`) would make ordinary rounding noise near zero look like a large relative error — the same category error the fundamentals wildcard deliberately avoids by being relative for the opposite reason (large-magnitude $ figures).

**Tolerance grounding — the adversarial crux mrtest owned.** `0.001` is derived from the live citation precision (~4 decimals, e.g. `-0.0124`), so honest rounding noise tops out at `0.00005` (half the last digit) — `0.001` gives 20x headroom over that floor. Verified against both ends: a correctly-rounded citation of a true value passes; a hallucinated citation representative of the kind the council could plausibly produce (e.g. `-0.02` cited against a true `-0.0124`, diff `0.0076`) lands outside even the `_OVERRIDE_FACTOR`-widened band and is correctly `overridden` — a looser guessed tolerance (e.g. `0.01`) would have wrongly passed that hallucination.

**Ground-truth stability, verified against the data flow (not assumed).** The verifier's ground truth is a post-council re-fetch (`prism_scheduler._fetch_lens_sections()`, prism_scheduler.py:560-657), not the payload the council read at synthesis time. This re-fetch is safe for momentum specifically because momentum and `breadth` come from the same `_build_technicals_section()` call over the same Alpaca daily-bar fetch, and a completed trading day's daily bar is immutable once posted — unlike `tone`, whose rolling GDELT window genuinely drifts between council-time and verify-time (the reason `_TONE_TOLERANCE` is deliberately wider). Momentum's tolerance only has to absorb citation-rounding noise, not re-fetch drift.

### Test-boundary correction found during GREEN (float-precision, not a `_classify()` bug)

The two tolerance-boundary tests (`test_momentum_boundary_exactly_at_tolerance_is_pass`, `test_momentum_boundary_exactly_at_override_factor_is_flagged`) originally used `truth=-0.0124` and constructed `cited` via `truth - offset`, relying on `_classify()`'s internal `abs(cited - truth)` to recover the offset exactly. `_MOMENTUM_TOLERANCE` (0.001) has no exact binary (IEEE-754) representation — unlike VIX's `0.5`, which is dyadic and round-trips exactly — so the override-factor test's subtract-then-resubtract produced a 1-ulp miss (`diff=0.003000000000000001` against a freshly computed `0.003` boundary), misclassifying `overridden` instead of `flagged`. Root cause was the test's boundary construction, not `_classify()` — a real citation is never within 1 ulp of a mathematical boundary — and mrimpl correctly declined to touch the shared classify function for a momentum-only tolerance quirk. Fixed by using `truth=0.0` for both boundary tests: IEEE-754 negation and subtraction-from-zero are exact, so the round-trip is bit-for-bit lossless regardless of the tolerance's binary representability, and `0.0` is itself a plausible flat 20d-return reading.

### Files changed

- `advisors/prism_numeric_verifier.py` — `_MOMENTUM_TOLERANCE` constant + 10 `_INDICATOR_REGISTRY` entries (16 lines, pure data addition)
- `tests/prism/test_prism_numeric_verifier.py` — `TestMomentumRegistryExpansion` (10 new tests: out-of-universe-ticker unmapped, exact registry-size pin at 23 keys, correctly-rounded-citation passes, tolerance/override-factor boundaries, near-miss-hallucination rejected, absolute-not-relative correctness near zero) + the 10 momentum indicators added to the two existing registry-wide parametrized tests (never-unverifiable-when-available, comparison-type-is-absolute) + populated the `_FULL_LENS_SECTIONS` fixture's previously-empty `technicals.momentum` dict with per-ticker truths for all 10 proxy tickers
- `tests/prism/test_prism_numeric_verifier_registry_drift.py` — extended the pre-existing F2 registry-drift guard (from the DE-PRISM-NUMERIC-VERIFY-001 review-fix cycle) with `test_technicals_momentum_resolves_against_real_builder_for_all_proxy_tickers`, resolving all 10 momentum entries against the REAL `_build_technicals_section()` output (network mocked at `lens_technicals._get_bars`, its own documented test-mockable seam)

Result: 92/92 GREEN (`tests/prism`, `-n0 -o addopts=`). AC-5 scope guard held: zero diff on `alpha_bot_execution.py`/`math_engine.py` across the whole cycle (RED `8cd20c3` -> float-boundary fix `f939080` -> GREEN `a621497`).

### Reference

DE-PRISM-MOMENTUM-REGISTRY-001; branch `feat/prism-momentum-registry`; HEAD `a621497`; extends the `_INDICATOR_REGISTRY` established in DE-PRISM-NUMERIC-VERIFY-001; direct empirical trigger was that entry's 2026-07-03 post-deploy-verified addendum.

### `/review` follow-up (PR #91): momentum naming pinned in the producer contract

`/review` found the momentum registry's consumer half (`_INDICATOR_REGISTRY`) had no matching producer-side contract: `.claude/agents/prism-technicals-analyst.md` pinned a concrete worked example for `breadth` but described momentum only in prose ("momentum reading") — the `momentum_<TICKER>_20d` naming had been reverse-engineered from one live council run's incidental choice, never enforced. Since the registry's momentum entries are literal (not wildcard-matched), any producer drift (`momentum_IWM`, `IWM_momentum_20d`, ...) would resolve `unverifiable` forever with no CI signal. Fixed by adding a second concrete worked example to the role file (`{"indicator": "momentum_SPY_20d", "value": -0.0124, "lens": "technicals"}`, with an explicit "use the naming exactly" instruction) — mirroring how macro's example pins `DGS10` and derivatives' pins `VIX`. RED `c7d5800` → GREEN `c3fdaa8`; new `TestTechnicalsAnalystMomentumNamingContract` in `tests/ai_advisor/test_prism_role_files_cited_numbers.py` (19/19 total in that file — corrects this codebase's prior "6 tests" miscount for the same file, which undercounted the parametrization across the 6 role files; see `docs/generated/advisors_prism_numeric_verifier.md`). AC-5 held (zero diff on `alpha_bot_execution.py`/`math_engine.py` across the whole cycle).

## DE-SLEEVES-P1-001 — Managed Sleeves: direct Alpaca trade path approved; safety architecture + culling-integration decisions (2026-07-07)

Branch: feature/managed-sleeves | Base: origin/main `0bcbd1a` | Plan: `feature-plans/managed-sleeves.md` (commit `4f665df`)

### Context

The prior plan (`feature-plans/guard-rules-engine.md`) scoped a rule engine with no order-placing path — the PM's default posture given the standing "dashboard/advisor surfaces never place trades" architecture invariant. The operator overruled that default on 2026-07-07: a managed sleeve's value depends on being able to act on its own rules, not just alert on them, and the plan's safety apparatus (shadow-first arming, an envelope hard box, broker-side stops, a panic-style arming ceremony) exists specifically to make direct order placement safe rather than to avoid building it. `guard-rules-engine.md` is superseded; `managed-sleeves.md` is the single plan artifact going forward — the rule-engine core (schema/senses/conditions/limits/runner) is carried into P2 unchanged.

### Decision: direct Alpaca trade path is in scope, against OUR account, never Composer's

A managed sleeve trades a bounded slice of the operator's own Alpaca account (paper today; live only once the operator provisions live keys). Composer keeps executing symphonies untouched — the two systems share no account identity, so there is no position-attribution ambiguity between what Composer holds and what a sleeve holds. Sleeve capital is a fixed-dollar allocation tracked by an internal cash ledger; a sleeve can never spend beyond its own allocation even if the underlying Alpaca account holds more cash.

### Safety architecture (binding for all P1-P4 phases)

1. **Single order-capable module.** `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py` is the only module permitted to construct Alpaca order requests — raw `requests`, no SDK (matches the rest of the stack; `advisors/composer_backtest_client.py`'s retry/backoff/timeout pattern is the model to copy).
2. **Whole-repo containment invariant.** A new AST-based test scans the entire repo and asserts order-endpoint calls (`POST`/`DELETE /v2/orders`, position-closing endpoints) exist only in that one module, and that the live trading host string appears nowhere outside the gated config. This is additive to, and does not replace, the existing single-file scans `test_m2_no_order_path.py` / `test_dashboard_no_order_path.py`, which stay green unmodified.
3. **Paper-first arming ladder.** Every rule is born in SHADOW (senses and would-have-ordered, executes nothing). SHADOW→PAPER requires at least one recorded shadow evaluation window (no arm-on-faith) and is structurally confined to `paper-api.alpaca.markets`. PAPER→LIVE is impossible unless distinct live-key env vars (`ALPACA_LIVE_KEY`/`ALPACA_LIVE_SECRET`) are present, `SLEEVE_LIVE_EXECUTION` is set, and the operator completes a panic-flow ceremony (session auth + CSRF + exact confirm phrase + audit-always-fires) modeled directly on `app.py:2764-2845`'s 6-gate `sell_account` chain.
4. **Envelope clamp-at-fire, reduce-only.** The envelope (ticker allowlist, max single-position %, per-order dollar cap, max daily turnover, long-only, no margin/shorting) is enforced at the moment an order fires, never earlier. Clamps only ever reduce a proposed order size — never increase it — and a clamp-to-zero is a refusal, not a zero-size order. Every clamp/refusal is logged with its reason. Widening an envelope requires the same ceremony as arming; narrowing takes effect immediately.
5. **Broker-side stops over engine-side.** Every entry defaults to an Alpaca-native bracket order (`order_class=bracket`) or an explicit trailing-stop/stop order, so protective exits live at the broker and survive engine downtime by construction — the soft-stop weakness identified in the source concept doc (`sleeve_guide.pdf`).
6. **Tolerance-based reconciliation.** Before any order, the sleeve's tracked positions/cash are checked against Alpaca account truth within a declared tolerance; a mismatch pauses only that sleeve (`PAUSED_RECONCILIATION`) and blocks new orders — it never mis-trades through a drift. The guide's "books balance exactly" premise is naive (fees, rounding, corporate actions); tolerance + pause-on-breach is the operable version of its conservation check.

### Culling-integration decisions (P4 — gates the LIVE rung only)

- **Class-tiered statistical gates.** Rule class is declared and structurally enforced from its action set: DEFENSIVE (reduce-only: sell/flatten/go-to-cash/stop-tighten/notify) vs. ENTRY (any position-opening action) — a rule cannot claim DEFENSIVE while holding entry actions. ENTRY arming requires full overfitting culling; DEFENSIVE arming requires only parameter sanity bounds, measured shadow/paper cost, and an envelope insurance-budget cap (a drawdown brake need not beat a backtest baseline to earn its keep); NOTIFY requires schema validation only.
- **Integration point is `backtest_gate_engine.evaluate_candidate_batch`, never the autotuner.** The autotuner's search space (`OPTUNA_SEARCH_SPACE_KEYS`) is an NN1-closed 6-dial frozenset whose winner auto-applies to live config with no operator step (`autotuner.py:1857`, `:2803`) — structurally the wrong gate model for operator-authored, order-placing rules. `backtest_gate_engine.evaluate_candidate_batch` (`advisors/backtest_gate_engine.py:525`) is the only decoupled abstraction that accepts arbitrary daily-return candidates through fold-transform + BHY + PBO + the acceptance gate, so it is the sole culling integration point. Sleeve rules are structurally forbidden from both the autotuner search space and its auto-apply path.
- **`pbo=None` fails closed for entry-class arming.** A single-candidate run yields `pbo=None`, which never fires the veto under the engine's current semantics — a vacuous gate for a human-authored rule. Entry verdicts are computed over a perturbation cohort (the rule + parameter-perturbed siblings + a do-nothing baseline), which makes PBO computable and additionally tests neighborhood robustness — a rule that only wins at its exact authored parameters is curve-fit.
- **Rule-authoring churn is counted.** Every culling simulation logs `BACKTEST_SELECTION` rows to the researcher-DOF ledger, so the existing BHY `n_effective` count and the Overfitting Conscience S/N watchdog see operator rule-authoring iteration as search cost, not a free loop.
- **Paper trading is not gated by culling.** Forward-test evidence gathered on the PAPER rung is the one unminable sample and should not wait on P4; only the LIVE rung requires a recorded culling verdict (for ENTRY class) or the sanity/cost/budget checks (for DEFENSIVE class). LIVE stays impossible-by-construction regardless (no live keys + the ceremony above).

### Status

Plan approved 2026-07-07 (`feature-plans/managed-sleeves.md`, commit `4f665df`). Build cycle in progress on `feature/managed-sleeves`: P1 (sleeve infrastructure + order layer — `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py`, `reconciliation.py`, `ledger.py`, `envelope.py`, `sizing.py`, DB migration) RED/GREEN underway. This entry records the approved architecture and decisions as of plan approval; `docs/generated/sleeves.md` (per-module API reference) lands alongside the P1 GREEN commits, once the modules it documents exist.

### Binding rules

1. `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py` is the ONLY module permitted to construct Alpaca order requests — enforced by a new whole-repo AST invariant test, additive to (never replacing) `test_m2_no_order_path.py` / `test_dashboard_no_order_path.py`.
2. Sleeve rules are structurally forbidden from `OPTUNA_SEARCH_SPACE_KEYS` and the autotuner auto-apply path (`autotuner.py:1857`, `:2803`) — `backtest_gate_engine.evaluate_candidate_batch` is the only culling integration point.
3. LIVE arming is impossible without distinct live-key env vars present, `SLEEVE_LIVE_EXECUTION` set, and the panic-flow ceremony modeled on `app.py:2764-2845`.
4. A rule cannot claim DEFENSIVE class while holding entry actions — schema-level enforced.
5. A sleeve trades OUR Alpaca account; Composer continues executing symphonies untouched — no shared position/account identity between the two.

### Reference

Supersedes `feature-plans/guard-rules-engine.md` (rule-engine core carried into P2 unchanged — a single plan artifact prevents divergent plans feeding the TDD skills). See `feature-plans/managed-sleeves.md` for the full acceptance criteria (AC-1..AC-24), architecture, edge cases, and testing strategy.

### Addendum (2026-07-07): `sleeve_rule_fires` deferred to a P2 migration

Migration 033 (commit `7126eb7`, shipped) creates five tables — `sleeves`, `sleeve_rules`, `sleeve_orders`, `sleeve_fills`, `sleeve_runtime` — not the six originally sketched in the plan's Architecture section. `sleeve_rule_fires` is DEFERRED from P1 to a P2 migration (034): additive-first migration discipline makes the deferral free (no P1 code path writes fires), and the fires row shape (sensed snapshot, episode semantics) is better designed against the real P2 rule-runner than guessed at now. `feature-plans/managed-sleeves.md`'s Architecture DB line and Decisions table are updated to match the shipped migration.

## DE-SLEEVES-P2-001 — Managed Sleeves P2: rule engine core (schema/senses/conditions/limits/runner) (2026-07-08, cycle in progress)

Branch: `feature/managed-sleeves` | Base: origin/main `0bcbd1a` (carried from P1) | Plan: `feature-plans/managed-sleeves.md` §"P2 — Rule engine core" | Predecessor: `DE-SLEEVES-P1-001`

### Context

P1 shipped the order-capable infrastructure (`sleeves/alpaca_orders.py`, `reconciliation.py`, `envelope.py`, `sizing.py`, `ledger.py` + migration 033) with zero production callers — `sleeve_rules` schema-ready but unread by any P1 code path, and `sleeve_rule_fires` explicitly deferred (see the P1 addendum above). P2 builds the rule engine itself — `sleeves/rules/` (schema validation, senses, condition-tree evaluation, pacing/limits, the runner) plus a migration 034 shipping `sleeve_rule_fires` — carrying the v1 `guard-rules-engine.md` rule-engine design verbatim per AC-4/AC-5/AC-6. Every rule is born in SHADOW (AC-6), and P2 ships SHADOW fires end-to-end (sensed snapshot + the envelope-clamped order the rule would have placed), executing nothing. The runner/actions layer built this phase is not itself SHADOW-restricted, though: it structurally supports a non-SHADOW (PAPER/LIVE-mode rule) path that reaches P1's `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py` — but only through `envelope.clamp`, never around it, extending P1's own containment invariant. What is genuinely P3-only is *production reachability*: no route, arming ceremony, or `alpha_bot_execution.main()` integration exists yet to ever create, arm, or invoke a PAPER/LIVE rule in production — the capability is being built this cycle, but nothing calls it non-SHADOW outside the test suite until P3 (see Decisions below).

### Status

Migration 034 (`c1047c1`), the P2 RED suite (`817df3e`, revised `6872d40`/`f883059`/`ab4ea8a`), the P2 GREEN (`7e0efe1`, 314 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped across `tests/sleeves/`), the entry-requires-explicit-stop RED/GREEN (`e3819f9`/`083526f`, 337 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped), and s2-review's first BLOCK finding's RED/GREEN response (`07c07ca`/`df47c84`/`ef34848`, 363 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped: cash-safety + reservation wiring, market_hours_only restriction) have all landed on `feature/managed-sleeves`. **s2-review's re-verdict at `ef34848` is APPROVE** (both original BLOCK findings closed; independently re-verified 449 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped across `tests/sleeves` + all 5 P1 containment canary files, ruff clean). One non-blocking tracked follow-up came with that approval — see the Known limitation note below. This entry is finalized as of this commit.

### Scope carried from the plan (AC-4, AC-5, AC-6)

- **Rule schema:** `when/if/then/limits`; size/depth/enum-closed validation; field-level errors; no code strings (no `eval`).
- **Senses:** symphony state, portfolio state, daily-bar indicators (SMA/EMA/RSI/momentum/realized vol/drawdown-from-high), time-of-day/day-of-week (ET, XNYS-holiday-aware per `market_calendar.py` — never hours-only), cached FRED series. Missing/stale sense data is fail-safe: not-fireable, logged deduped — never a crash, never a silent skip that looks like "no signal."
- **Condition-tree evaluation** over those senses.
- **Pacing/limits** (cooldown_sec, max_fires_per_day, episode latch, churn-brake state) persisted in `sleeve_runtime` across the fresh-subprocess-per-minute engine model (app.py:572-587,697) — proven by a test simulating consecutive one-shot engine invocations.
- **Migration 034:** `sleeve_rule_fires` (sensed snapshot + the exact envelope-clamped order a SHADOW rule would have produced) — resolves the P1 deferral; see the Addendum below once shipped.
- **Capability vs. production reachability:** the runner/actions modules structurally support an armed (PAPER/LIVE-mode rule) path — order construction reaches `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py` only through `envelope.clamp` (never around it), pinned by a RED test asserting non-bypassability. What's P3-only is the *production caller*: no route/ceremony/`alpha_bot_execution.main()` wiring exists yet to arm a rule or ever invoke `evaluate_rules()` non-SHADOW in production — every rule that can exist in production this phase is still SHADOW, by absence of any arming path, not because the runner code is incapable of more.

### Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Runner/actions build full SHADOW+armed capability in P2; only production *reachability* (routes/ceremony/`alpha_bot_execution.main()` wiring) is P3-gated | Resolved 2026-07-08 (s2-test-writer flagged a contradiction between this skeleton's original "SHADOW-only" framing and both the kickoff brief's armed-path RED-test requirement and migration 034's `order_id` column, which exists for PAPER/LIVE fires per its own header comment). Landed: RED (`817df3e`, revised `6872d40`/`f883059`/`ab4ea8a`) then GREEN (`7e0efe1`) — `sleeves/rules/actions.py`'s `dispatch_action` structurally routes `buy`/`sell`/`go_to_cash` through `sleeves.sizing.size_order` then `sleeves.envelope.clamp_order`, reaching `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py` only with the clamped qty and only when `shadow=False`; a capability, not a production hole, since no route/ceremony/`main()` integration exists yet to ever create, arm, or invoke a PAPER/LIVE rule in production until P3. |

| Entry actions require explicit exit parameters (`stop_loss_pct` or `trailing_stop_pct`; `take_profit_pct` optional) in the rule document — a `buy` with no declared stop is a schema error, not a silent engine default | **Resolved:** RED `e3819f9` (s2-test-writer) then GREEN `083526f` (s2-rules-impl). Credit to s2-rules-impl, who surfaced this in the `7e0efe1` commit body rather than silently deciding (naming `_DEFAULT_BRACKET_STOP_LOSS_PCT`/`_DEFAULT_BRACKET_TAKE_PROFIT_PCT` explicitly as "NOT a tuned risk parameter, flagged as an open design point"). `sizing.py`'s `risk_pct` mode already requires a stop distance to compute qty, so an entry action's definition is incomplete without one; AC-7 makes the exit part of the entry, owned by the rule author, never a silently-applied engine constant; a hardcoded default stop would couple an untested constant into real position sizing. `schema.py`'s `_validate_buy_exit_fields` now requires `stop_loss_pct` or `trailing_stop_pct` (each bounded `0 < pct < 1`); the old bracket-default constants are gone entirely (enforced absent by a module-source-inspection test). `take_profit_pct` stays optional; when absent, `actions.py` derives the take-profit distance as a fixed `_TAKE_PROFIT_REWARD_RISK_RATIO = 2.0` multiple of the rule's *own* declared stop distance, never an independent percentage. **This ratio is a deliberate, tunable default, not the only option:** it embeds an upside opinion (every entry's take-profit is capped at exactly 2x its stop distance), and the recorded alternative is a stop-only entry (Alpaca's `OTO` order class, no take-profit leg, upside uncapped) — not built, a candidate P3+/operator decision. The current default is the honest middle: safe (protective floor intact, scales with the author's declared risk, test-pinned) but not neutral, and surfaced rather than buried. Verified: `tests/sleeves` 337 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped at `083526f`. |

| Armed-path dispatch enforces cash-safety and durably records the P1 invariant #6 reservation sequence for every order-placing action; `market_hours_only=False` is restricted to pure-notify rules | **s2-review BLOCK finding at `083526f`, PM ruling, resolved:** RED (`07c07ca`, fixture fix `df47c84`) then GREEN (`ef34848`). The gap: the armed path placed real broker orders with zero cash-safety enforcement and no durable reservation row — wiring the existing P1 primitives into the armed dispatch path immediately (this cycle), not a deferral guard, since a real-money gap is not something P2 can ship and defer. New `sleeves.ledger.reconstruct_from_history(capital_usd, order_history)` (pure fold over `database.get_sleeve_order_history`'s output using the existing `reserve`/`apply_fill`/`release` transitions, reusing `get_daily_turnover_usd`'s exact terminal-status denylist so an unrecognized/future order status fails closed — stays reserved, the conservative direction). `_dispatch_buy` reconstructs real ledger state and attempts `reserve()` in BOTH shadow and armed mode (so a SHADOW fire's snapshot reflects the true would-have-been outcome, not an optimistic one) — insufficient cash refuses with zero broker calls and zero DB writes either way. Every order-placing action (buy/sell/go_to_cash/set_stop) now mints a `client_order_id` and inserts a `RESERVED` `sleeve_orders` row before the broker call, attaches the broker's own order id on ack, and marks the row terminal on rejection (the release mechanism, since `LedgerState` is never itself persisted, only reconstructed) — `ActionResult.order_id` threads through to the fire row for AC-19's trade-to-fire-to-order trace. Second, independent ruling in the same commit: `market_hours_only=False` was an unrestricted override (drift from the plan's market-hours-only-evaluation v1 posture) — now schema-rejected unless the rule's entire `then` action set is pure-`notify` (any order-placing action, entry or defensive, forbids the override regardless of the flag). Verified: `tests/sleeves` 363 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped at `ef34848`, ruff clean. |

(Resolved design points, per the GREEN `7e0efe1`: the condition-tree is a plain nested-dict `{"op": "compare"|"AND"|"OR"|"NOT", ...}` structure (see `sleeves/rules/schema.py` / `conditions.py`); the sense fail-safe uses no separate dedup key at the condition-eval layer itself (`conditions.evaluate_condition` returns a bare `sense_missing:<key>` reason per evaluation; the plan's "logged deduped" framing is a P3/runner-integration-time dashboard/Discord concern, not a P2 mechanism, and stays an open point for that phase); the `sleeve_runtime` KV scheme is 5 string-valued keys per rule_id (`last_fire_ts`/`fires_today_date`/`fires_today_count`/`episode_latched`/`consecutive_false_count`), all read/written through the existing P1 `get_sleeve_runtime`/`set_sleeve_runtime` accessors, zero in-process cache.)

### Known limitation: reservations don't yet self-release (tracked, non-blocking)

Flagged by s2-review as a non-blocking follow-up alongside their APPROVE verdict at `ef34848` (independently confirmed by reading `_place_order_with_reservation` and `reconstruct_from_history` directly): fill-polling is entirely unwired in P2 (AC-9/P3 scope) — `_place_order_with_reservation` attaches only the broker's `alpaca_order_id` on ack, never a status transition, so an acked `sleeve_orders` row stays literally `'RESERVED'` forever in P2's current code; nothing anywhere in `sleeves/` ever calls `database.insert_sleeve_fill` or advances a row's status past `'RESERVED'` except on rejection (`'rejected'`). Since `reconstruct_from_history`'s `release()` only fires when an order's status is in the terminal-status denylist, a successfully-placed order's cash reservation never naturally releases until P3's reconciliation/fill-polling loop lands and records a real fill or terminal status. **This is the safe direction** — it over-reserves cash headroom, never under-reserves it, so `ledger.reserve()`'s `InsufficientCashError` can only be more conservative than the sleeve's true available cash, never less — but reservations will visibly accumulate once real (armed) order flow starts in P3, and that accumulation should not be mistaken for a bug when first observed. Tracked here so P3's fill-polling wiring closes it, not silently discovered later.

## DE-SLEEVES-P3-001 — Managed Sleeves P3: wiring + surfaces (2026-07-08, cycle complete — real paper-account smoke PASSED after 3 done-bar fixes)

Branch: `feature/managed-sleeves` | Base: origin/main `0bcbd1a` (carried from P1/P2) | Plan: `feature-plans/managed-sleeves.md` §"P3 — Wiring + surfaces" | Predecessor: `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001`

### Context

P1 shipped the order-capable infrastructure; P2 shipped the rule engine itself (`sleeves/rules/`) with full SHADOW+armed dispatch capability, but zero production reachability — no route, ceremony, or `alpha_bot_execution.main()` wiring exists to ever create, arm, or invoke a PAPER/LIVE rule (see `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001`). P3 closes that gap: hooking the P2 runner into the live engine tick, building the Flask route surface + dashboard panel + replay endpoint + Discord digest extension, and building the two arming ceremonies (SHADOW→PAPER, PAPER→LIVE) that are the only way a rule can ever leave SHADOW in production.

This entry started as a skeleton at cycle start (drafted before any P3 code had landed, when branch tip was still `758a577`, P2's last gate-finding commit) and has since been extended in place — Decisions/Status filled in as `s3-engine`/`s3-dashboard`/`s3-test-writer` landed RED/GREEN commits, never rewritten. It records the scope carried from the plan below; see Status for what has actually shipped.

### Scope carried from the plan (AC-9, AC-10, AC-13, AC-14, AC-15, AC-16, AC-17, AC-18, AC-19)

- **Engine hook:** `sleeves.rules.runner.evaluate_rules` called from `alpha_bot_execution.main()`, placed AFTER the existing exit machine (absolute precedence preserved — the plan is explicit this ordering is non-negotiable), via the lazy-import convention already used for `ai_advisor.py` (import inside `main()`, never module-level).
- **Reconciliation wiring:** pre-trade and post-fill broker-truth reconciliation (AC-9) — P2 left fill-polling and reservation release entirely unwired (see `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001`'s "Known limitation" note); P3 is where a `sleeve_orders` row advances past `RESERVED` for a real fill, and where `sleeves.reconciliation.reconcile_sleeve` actually gets called against live broker state and can set a sleeve to `PAUSED_RECONCILIATION`.
- **Route surface:** `GET/POST /api/sleeves`, `POST /api/sleeves/<id>/arm-paper|arm-live|disarm|delete`, `GET/POST /api/sleeves/<id>/rules`, `POST .../rules/<id>/arm|disarm|delete`, `GET .../rules/<id>/replay` — CSRF pattern from `POST /api/settings`.
- **Ceremony gates:** SHADOW→PAPER requires a recorded shadow-evaluation-window minimum (AC-13, no arm-on-faith); PAPER→LIVE replicates the `sell_account` 6-gate chain (AC-14) and additionally requires a recorded culling verdict for ENTRY-class rules (AC-21/23 — P4 scope, but the arming route's *check* for a verdict is P3's to build even before P4 ships the verdict producer).
- **Whole-repo invariant extension:** AC-15's containment scan must keep passing once a real production caller exists — this is the point where "no production caller" (P2's own docs note) becomes false, and the scan needs to prove the *new* caller still only reaches the broker through `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py` and only via `envelope.clamp`.
- **Dashboard panel + Atlas badge:** AC-16 (sleeve status, cash ledger vs. broker truth, per-rule fire/P&L attribution, arm/disarm controls, Atlas cache-health badge).
- **Discord + digest:** AC-17 (fires, fills, clamps/refusals, reconciliation pauses, churn-bench events; EOD digest extension; dedup to one alert/day for repeated identical conditions).
- **Replay endpoint:** AC-18 (`GET .../replay?days=N`, N≤60, diagnostics-only — condition-replay, never an arming input per the plan's explicit decision).
- **Trade traceability:** AC-19 (every trade traces rule→fire→order→fill; every sleeve/rule/envelope mutation in the config-audit pattern) — P2 built the fire→order half of this trace (`ActionResult.order_id`); P3 is where a real armed fire actually produces one in production.

A THIRD BLOCK-level gap (shared-account reconciliation semantics, task #31) surfaced afterward from `s3-ux`'s live 7-sleeve visual-gate testing — RED at `c5a78bc`, fixed at `c178ee2` (retired the per-sleeve `reconcile_sleeve_or_pause`, replaced with aggregate cash/position checks computed once per broker-host group; 28/28 `test_reconciliation.py` + 21/21 `test_tick_orchestrator.py`, full regression 547 passed / 0 failed in-scope, ruff clean; see Decisions below), and `s3-review`'s full re-verification of that fix pinned one further open design point as a real test rather than leave it an unverified assumption (`6eec056`, no behavior change). All BLOCK findings raised against the RED/GREEN/review cycle are now resolved. **The PM then ran a real paper-account smoke test** (a default sleeve attempting to place a genuine order) and found three further gaps the review cycle's mocked/fixture-based tests couldn't have caught, since each only manifests against real bar data or the real broker: (1) `closes_by_symbol`/`fred_cache` were hardcoded empty dicts, so every entry's price computed to `0.0` and every sizing attempt refused — fixed at `d62348a`/`a80d2c3` by wiring `synthetic_history.fetch_bars` + cached FRED into the tick, once per tick (task #33 — the epic's done-bar blocker; this is the fix that made direct trading functionally real, not just structurally present); (2) an empty/absent envelope allowlist read as "confined to nothing" rather than "unconfined," so a default sleeve with no allowlist populated could never buy its own rule's symbol — fixed at `2c8fcb5` (task #34); (3) unrounded bracket-leg prices from risk-sizing math (e.g. `14.839`) triggered a real Alpaca `HTTP 422` sub-penny rejection on every bracket entry — fixed at `dfbaa4a` by rounding to Alpaca's documented equity tick at the `alpaca_orders.py` boundary (task #35). **The smoke re-ran after all three fixes and PASSED**: a default sleeve placed a real broker-accepted paper order. The only remaining item is the non-blocking `arm_sleeve_live` open point below (operator/PM ruling, not a defect).

### Decisions

| Decision | Rationale |
|----------|-----------|
| Disarm route (`disarm_sleeve`) is SYNCHRONOUS/DB-only; actual broker cancellation of a disarmed sleeve's open orders happens on the engine's next tick instead | The disarm route was initially written to call `sleeves.alpaca_orders.cancel_order` directly, which would have tripped the pre-existing whole-repo containment invariant (`tests/app/test_dashboard_no_order_path.py`, which denylists `cancel_order` in every route except `sell_account`). Caught pre-emptively by `s3-dashboard` before any GREEN landed; `s3-test-writer` revised the RED contract at `9acc53e` to move cancellation to `sleeves/tick_orchestrator.py`'s new `cancel_open_orders_for_shadow_sleeve` (called by the engine tick for every SHADOW-status sleeve). The route itself only reverts `sleeve`/`sleeve_rules` status/mode to `SHADOW`; positions and broker-side stops are never touched either way (AC-12's non-destructive-kill contract). |
| SHADOW-status sleeves get fill-polling and reconciliation too, not just order cancellation (s3-review BLOCK 1, resolved) | As first committed (`d7c8bb5`), `poll_and_apply_fills`/`reconcile_sleeve_or_pause` only ran for non-SHADOW sleeves — a disarmed sleeve stays SHADOW permanently until re-armed, so real broker-side exposure from a TOCTOU fill (between the disarm click and the tick's cancel attempt) or a residual position could drift forever uncaught. `s3-review`'s post-GREEN pass flagged this as BLOCK; RED at `f4e496a`, fixed at `9d8e46c` — both functions now run for every sleeve regardless of status, gated only on "already `PAUSED_RECONCILIATION` coming into this tick." A SHADOW sleeve that breaches reconciliation now pauses exactly like any other status. Verified: `tests/sleeves/test_tick_orchestrator.py` 19/19 passed; full regression 477 passed / 0 failed, ruff clean. |
| Broker errors on fill-polling and order cancellation are logged at WARNING; a cancel failure during disarm additionally posts a Discord alert (s3-review BLOCK 2, resolved) | `sleeves/alpaca_orders.py` never logs internally by its own never-raises contract, so a persistent broker outage/auth failure on the fill-polling or SHADOW-cancel path was invisible anywhere in the stack. Fixed at `9d8e46c` alongside BLOCK 1: `poll_and_apply_fills`/`cancel_open_orders_for_shadow_sleeve` now log `WARNING` on any `OrderResult.error`; `cancel_open_orders_for_shadow_sleeve` additionally posts a best-effort Discord alert on a cancel failure specifically — an operator who clicked disarm must never be left believing an order is cancelled when the broker actually rejected it. |
| **RESOLVED: `reconcile_sleeve_or_pause` retired; replaced by an aggregate cash/position check computed once per broker-host group, not per sleeve** | As first committed (`9d8e46c`), the function passed one sleeve's own `ledger_state.cash_usd` against `alpaca_orders.get_account`'s account-level `"cash"` field — correct only by coincidence when exactly one sleeve exists; found broken by `s3-ux`'s live 7-sleeve visual-gate testing (task #25, not the original RED/GREEN cycle): every sleeve paused within one tick. **PM ruling, implemented:** `sleeves/reconciliation.py` gained two one-sided pure functions — `reconcile_aggregate_cash` (breaches iff `Σ(sleeve.cash_usd + sleeve.reserved_usd)` across every checked sleeve exceeds `broker_cash_usd + tolerance`; broker cash exceeding the combined claim is explicitly fine) and `reconcile_aggregate_position` (per-symbol, breaches iff sleeves' combined qty for a symbol exceeds the broker's own qty for it + tolerance; a broker-only position in an untracked symbol is ignored entirely). `sleeves/tick_orchestrator.py`'s new `_run_aggregate_reconciliation` calls `get_account`/`get_positions` exactly once per resolved-broker-host group (never per sleeve) and applies both checks; a cash breach pauses every sleeve in the group (blame is unattributable across virtual slices of one account), a position breach pauses only the sleeves holding that symbol. `run_sleeve_tick_for_all_sleeves` was restructured into three phases (per-sleeve SHADOW-cleanup + fill-poll, once-per-host-group aggregate reconciliation, per-sleeve rule evaluation) to keep the existing one-sleeve's-exception-never-blocks-another contract. RED at `c5a78bc` (`s3-test-writer`), GREEN at `c178ee2` (`s3-engine`, task #31). Verified: `tests/sleeves/test_reconciliation.py` 28/28 passed, `tests/sleeves/test_tick_orchestrator.py` 21/21 passed; full regression 547 passed / 0 failed in this file's scope (8 unrelated pre-existing failures in `tests/app/test_sleeves_panel_render.py` are task #32's panel-rendering BLOCK, untouched by this fix), ruff clean. |
| **RESOLVED (task #32): AC-16 panel-rendering gaps** — status-badge color-collapse, disabled-button styling, a missing delete control, missing cash-ledger/per-rule-P&L display | Found by `s3-ux`'s live 7-sleeve visual-gate pass (task #25). Fixed at `821b385`: (1) all 6 named statuses now map to their own visually-distinct status-pill class via `_sleeve_status_badge_class`/`_SLEEVE_STATUS_BADGE_CLASSES`, replacing a 3-way `if`/`elif` that collapsed 4 statuses into one look; (2) a new `data-testid="sleeve-delete-control"` wired to a new `POST /api/sleeves/<id>/delete` route + `database.delete_sleeve()`; (3)/(4) the panel now renders real per-sleeve ledger cash and per-rule realized P&L, both derived with zero new schema via `sleeves.ledger.reconstruct_from_history` folds over existing order/fill history (not fabricated placeholders); (5) a `.control-disabled` class dims the Disarm button when the sleeve is SHADOW; (6) every panel flex row gained `flex-wrap`+`gap` for mobile 375px (CSS-only, not RED-encoded). RED at `2d5dcae`, GREEN at `821b385` — 19/19 passed in `test_sleeves_panel_render.py`, full regression 1189 passed / 0 failed, ruff + `node --check` clean. |
| **RESOLVED: disabled Disarm button's cursor didn't change to `not-allowed` — CSS specificity** | `s3-ux`'s re-render confirmed all 6 findings above pass, with one trivial residual: opacity correctly dropped to `0.4` but the cursor stayed `pointer`, because the button's own inline style set `cursor: pointer` unconditionally and a class selector alone can never out-specificity an inline style. Fixed at `cd9a970` by adding `!important` to `.control-disabled`'s `cursor` property. Pure CSS fix, no test/behavior change (19/19 still passing). |
| **RESOLVED (s3-review's last BLOCK on this cycle): the new delete route only checked open positions, not non-terminal orders** | A position is only ever created by `ledger.apply_fill()`, so an order the broker has accepted but not yet filled (or a still-`RESERVED` pre-ack row) produced zero positions and read as falsely flat at `821b385` — even though it's a live, unrecoverable broker exposure: once the sleeve row is deleted, `database.get_all_sleeves()` never includes it again, so nothing would ever poll/cancel/reconcile that order again for the rest of the process's life (worse than the disarm route's already-handled TOCTOU gap, since a disarmed sleeve's row survives and is revisited every engine tick). RED at `a7e57b4`, fixed at `f8ca848`: the route now additionally refuses if any of the sleeve's orders has a status outside the terminal-status set (`filled`/`canceled`/`expired`/`replaced`/`done_for_day`/`rejected` — the same tuple `get_daily_turnover_usd`/`tick_orchestrator.py` already use); `"RESERVED"`'s correct absence from that tuple means the one check covers both the accepted-but-unfilled and still-`RESERVED` cases with no separate branch. Verified: 21/21 passed in `test_sleeves_panel_render.py`; full regression 1191 passed / 0 failed, ruff clean. |
| **RESOLVED (epic done-bar blocker, PM's real paper-account smoke): the engine tick wired hardcoded empty bar/FRED dicts, so every entry's price computed to `0.0` and every sizing attempt refused** | `run_sleeve_tick_for_all_sleeves` passed `closes_by_symbol={}`/`fred_cache={}` literals to `evaluate_rules`; `runner.py`'s own `price = closes[-1] if closes else 0.0` always yielded `0.0`, so `sizing.size_order` refused every entry with `error="invalid_price"` — safe (fails closed) but non-functional: an armed sleeve could never genuinely trade, making the whole direct-trade epic structurally present but not actually working. Fixed at `d62348a` (task #33): the tick now collects every symbol referenced by an enabled rule across every evaluable sleeve and fetches daily closes for that whole set via `synthetic_history.fetch_bars` (the same daily-bar path P1/P2 already use, never a second HTTP client) exactly ONCE per tick, plus cached FRED observations from `database.get_latest_market_lens_cache()`'s nightly `"macro"` lens block (cache-only, D-1, matching `ai_advisor.py`'s own cache-serve precedent) — never a live FRED call from the tick. A symbol with no bars, or a fetch failure, degrades through the pre-existing `sleeves.rules.senses`/`conditions` fail-safe contract (not fireable, no fire recorded), never a crash or a fabricated price. Follow-up at `a80d2c3` (`s3-review`, non-blocking): fixed a docstring citation to the wrong `ai_advisor.py` function name, and excluded FRED's own `"."` missing-observation sentinel from `fred_cache` (it would otherwise reach `conditions.py`'s numeric comparator as a bare string and raise `TypeError` instead of failing safe). Verified: `tests/sleeves/test_tick_bars_price_feed.py` 6/6 then 7/7 passed; full regression 543 passed / 0 failed at `d62348a`, `tests/sleeves/` full tree 403 passed / 0 failed at `a80d2c3`, ruff clean both. |
| **RESOLVED (PM's real paper-account smoke): empty/absent envelope allowlist meant "confined to nothing," not "unconfined," contradicting AC-2** | `sleeves/envelope.py`'s `clamp_order` treated an empty or absent `allowlist` as confinement to the empty set — refusing EVERY buy with `REASON_NOT_IN_ALLOWLIST`, so a default sleeve whose operator never populated an allowlist could never trade its own rule's symbol. **PM ruling:** empty/absent allowlist means NO ticker confinement — the rule's own `when.symbol` plus the dollar/position/turnover caps are the real money-safety bounds; a genuinely non-empty allowlist continues to confine exactly as before. Fixed at `2c8fcb5` (task #34): the allowlist gate in `clamp_order` is now skipped entirely when the allowlist is empty/absent. `is_envelope_widened` was also rewritten in the same commit — its subset-based allowlist check assumed the old "empty = deny-all" semantics and would have mis-flagged this fix's own narrowing direction (empty/absent → populated) as a widen while failing to flag the real extreme case (clearing a populated allowlist down to empty/absent, i.e. confined → the whole universe) at all; now matches the None/absent-means-unlimited pattern already used for every other cap. Verified: `tests/sleeves/test_envelope_clamp.py` 51/51 passed (both new test classes green, zero regressions in the pre-existing widen-detection classes), ruff clean. |
| **RESOLVED (PM's direct Alpaca repro): unrounded bracket-leg prices triggered a real HTTP 422 sub-penny rejection on every bracket entry** | `submit_bracket_order` sent raw, unrounded float leg prices (e.g. `take_profit=14.839`, `stop_loss=12.8155`, straight out of risk-sizing math) via `str(price)`; Alpaca returned `HTTP 422` code `42210000` ("sub-penny increment does not fulfill minimum pricing criteria") — every real bracket entry was rejected at the broker, even though sizing/envelope/reservation logic upstream had already approved it. Fixed at `dfbaa4a` (task #35): new `_round_to_equity_tick(price, *, rounding)` quantizes via `decimal.Decimal` (never raw float floor/round — `495.00 / 0.01 == 49499.999999999993` in IEEE-754, which would silently floor an already-tick-valid price down a full cent) to Alpaca's documented equity tick size (2 decimals at/above `$1.00`, 4 decimals below). `stop_loss_price` rounds `ROUND_FLOOR` (a long's protective stop must never tighten closer to entry than sizing intended); `take_profit_price` rounds `ROUND_HALF_UP` to the nearest tick (not a protective boundary in the same sense, so either direction is correct). Rounding happens only at the `alpaca_orders.py` boundary — `sleeves/rules/actions.py`'s sizing/price math stays pure and unrounded. Verified: `tests/sleeves/test_alpaca_orders_lifecycle.py` 43/43 passed (all 5 new rounding tests green on first attempt); full regression (combined with the #34 fix in the same verification pass) 561 passed / 0 failed, ruff clean. |
| **Documented (known behavior, not a defect): a `sleeve_orders` row stays `'RESERVED'` locally for up to ~60s after a genuine broker ack, until the next fill-poll tick syncs its status** | `_place_order_with_reservation` attaches only `alpaca_order_id` at ack time; the row's status advances to the broker's own native status string only when `poll_and_apply_fills` next polls that order (the engine tick runs once a minute). Confirmed as expected during the PM's real paper-account smoke — recorded here so this bounded eventual-consistency window is never mistaken for a bug when observed (e.g. by an operator watching the panel or database immediately after an order is placed). No code change; a documentation-only clarification of already-shipped, already-tested behavior (see `docs/generated/sleeves.md`'s architecture invariant 6). |

### Carried forward from P2 (one resolved, one still open)

- **Reservation self-release — RESOLVED.** `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001`'s "Known limitation" note — an acked order's `sleeve_orders` row stayed `'RESERVED'` forever without fill-polling — is closed by `sleeves/tick_orchestrator.py`'s `poll_and_apply_fills` (commit `d7c8bb5`): every engine tick polls broker-truth status for each non-terminal, post-ack order, records any newly-filled quantity as a real `sleeve_fills` row, and advances the order's status to the broker's own status string verbatim — so `reconstruct_from_history`'s next fold sees the real fills and correctly releases any true unfilled remainder once the order reaches a terminal status. Both `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001` and `docs/generated/sleeves.md`'s `reconstruct_from_history` section have been corrected in place (not rewritten) to reflect this.
- **Take-profit reward:risk default — still OPEN.** `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001`'s entry-exit-fields decision flagged the stop-only `OTO`-order-class alternative to the hardcoded 2:1 default as "a candidate P3+/operator decision, surfaced here rather than buried." This stays an **open operator decision** for PR review — not something the doc-writer resolves unilaterally, and P3 introduced no new information bearing on it.

### Open point (non-blocking): `arm_sleeve_live` has no prior-PAPER/track-record check before allowing LIVE

Raised by `s3-review`'s pass over the route surface (`0efe45c`), routed here explicitly rather than encoded as RED — review did not block on it. **This is a recorded open point for the operator/PM to rule on, not a doc-writer verdict.**

The `arm_sleeve_live` route (`POST /api/sleeves/<id>/arm-live`) never checks whether the sleeve — or any of its rules — has ever actually been armed to PAPER, or has any paper track record at all. A sleeve can go straight from freshly-created SHADOW to LIVE as long as the 6 ceremony gates pass (confirm id + exact phrase, then live keys + `SLEEVE_LIVE_EXECUTION`). AC-14's literal text doesn't require a prior-PAPER check, and AC-21's culling-verdict gate is explicit P4 scope — so review didn't block on it. But the plan's own P3 Architecture line reads: "PAPER→LIVE gate: culling verdict... **+ paper track-record minimum** + ceremony" — and no concrete track-record check exists anywhere in the shipped code.

Two ways this could go, neither decided here:
1. **Deliberate P3 deferral to P4** — paper-track-record enforcement gets bundled with the culling-verdict gate when P4 ships (both are prerequisites for the LIVE rung per the plan's own phrasing), so building it now would be partial/premature.
2. **A real scope gap worth closing sooner** — LIVE arming is "impossible by construction" only with respect to *credentials*; nothing today prevents an operator (or a bug) from live-arming a sleeve with zero forward-test evidence, which is arguably a bigger gap than the credential gates address.

Recorded here so it's visible for a ruling rather than discovered later at PR review. See `docs/generated/sleeves.md`'s `arm_sleeve_live` section for the same note.

### Operator questions for PR review (3 items — legitimate design choices, not defects or unaddressed debt)

None of these are resolved here; each is recorded so the operator can weigh it explicitly at PR review rather than discover it later. Team-lead instruction (2026-07-08): each item is a scope/design choice the operator should decide on its merits, not a TODO implying something was left undone.

1. **Entry-time `trailing_stop_pct` produces a FIXED bracket stop, not a live Alpaca-native trailing-stop leg.** A rule author who declares `trailing_stop_pct` (rather than `stop_loss_pct`) on a `buy` action gets `_dispatch_buy` deriving a **fixed** `stop_loss_price` at that distance for the bracket order's stop leg — not an actual trailing-stop order that adjusts as price moves favorably. A real Alpaca-native trailing-stop order is `set_stop`'s domain, for protecting an *already-open* position, not an entry's own bracket. This is arguably surprising given the field's name; the alternative (arming a genuine trailing-stop leg at entry) isn't supported by Alpaca's `bracket` order class and would need a different order-construction path. See `docs/generated/sleeves.md`'s `actions.py` section (`_dispatch_buy`) for the exact mechanism.
2. **Take-profit default is a fixed 2:1 reward:risk ratio, vs. a stop-only `OTO`-order-class alternative.** Carried from `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001`'s entry-exit-fields decision — see that entry and `docs/generated/sleeves.md`'s `actions.py` "Design note" for full detail. Not re-litigated here.
3. **Sleeves panel/digest cash figures are per-sleeve ledger-only; a genuinely fuller ACCOUNT-LEVEL line is possible but requires new persistence.** Raised by `s3-test-writer` (task #29's panel-data scope call, approved by team-lead): the panel currently shows each sleeve's own ledger cash plus its `PAUSED_RECONCILIATION` status signal, and per-rule P&L via the `rule_id` fold — all derivable from data already persisted. A fuller display — **"Σ sleeve cash vs. account cash (as of last tick)"** — would show the operator how much of the real Alpaca account's cash the sleeves collectively claim versus what's actually there. Building it requires the engine tick to persist a broker-account cash snapshot somewhere durable (a new column or table, written at tick time) — today's `_run_aggregate_reconciliation` computes this comparison in-memory every tick but never stores it, so there is nothing for the panel to read after the fact without new persistence. This is a real migration cost (schema change + a new tick-time write path), not a small addition — recorded as an operator-facing scope decision for PR review, not built in P3.

### Reference

See `feature-plans/managed-sleeves.md` §"P3 — Wiring + surfaces" and AC-9/10/13/14/15/16/17/18/19. Predecessor: `DE-SLEEVES-P2-001`. Docs: `docs/generated/sleeves.md`'s P3 section lands alongside P3 GREEN commits.

## DE-SLEEVES-FIX-001 — Managed Sleeves branch-accuracy audit + fix cycle (2026-07-09, cycle in progress)

Branch: `feature/managed-sleeves` | Base: `origin/main` (carried from P1/P2/P3) | Predecessor: `DE-SLEEVES-P3-001` | Audit: `VERDICT-branch.md` (ba-lead synthesis of ba-math/ba-output/ba-flow, 2026-07-09)

### Context

`DE-SLEEVES-P3-001` closed as "cycle complete — real paper-account smoke PASSED." That framing is **corrected here, not retracted wholesale** — the P1/P2 core machinery it verified (ledger conservation, envelope reduce-only clamping, sizing formulas, tick rounding, fill-poll write ordering/idempotency) held up independently under this audit's own fuzz/repro re-verification and stays accurate. What the audit disproves is the P3 wiring layer's claim to be *functionally reachable in production*: a dedicated three-auditor pass (math/output/real-time-flow), including a live paper-account smoke test independent of the PM's earlier one, found the rule engine is **100% inert via the actual production create-rule path** — every rule created through the real route crashes with a `KeyError` on its first fireable tick, forever, silently. The PM's prior smoke test that "passed" exercised the engine with hand-seeded state that bypassed this path; it could not have caught the defect because it never drove a rule through `create_sleeve_rule_route` the way an operator actually would. Full findings, live-smoke transcripts, and fuzz repros are in `VERDICT-branch.md` and its sibling artifacts (this audit's scratchpad directory, not committed to this branch).

**Executive verdict from the audit (quoted for the record):** "The branch is NOT done. Do not arm anything on it." Two CRITICALs on one line (`tick_orchestrator.py:471`): the rule-dict merge omits `sleeve_id` (KeyError, swallowed, zero fires ever) and lets a client-supplied `"mode"` override the row's forced-SHADOW mode (a crafted doc could trade with no arming ceremony). Independently, no production route could ever promote a sleeve's status to PAPER, so a paper-armed rule always lived inside a SHADOW-status sleeve whose step-0 cleanup canceled its orders every tick — live-observed **destroying a real FILLED bracket order** (fill lost, reservation released, both protective legs canceled, resulting naked position invisible to reconciliation).

### Fix-cycle team and process

Composition: sf-test (RED, cycle lead) + sf-eng (engine-layer GREEN) + sf-dash (route/panel/digest-layer GREEN) + sf-review + sf-doc (this entry). RED lands per audit-finding batch; GREEN follows citing the finding number(s) it closes. This entry is extended in place as each fix's GREEN lands — never rewritten — matching `DE-SLEEVES-P3-001`'s own convention.

**Why route-shaped test fixtures are now mandatory (`tests/sleeves/_route_shaped.py`):** the audit's root-cause for why 1200+ pre-existing green tests missed both CRITICALs is that every runner-driving test built its rule dict via `tests/sleeves/rules/conftest.py`'s `make_stored_rule`, which bakes in `sleeve_id`/`mode` — a shape the real `POST /api/sleeves/<id>/rules` route never produces (it stores the raw client payload verbatim; `sleeve_id` lives only in the URL and the `sleeve_rules.sleeve_id` column). `_route_shaped.py` is new test-support (not a test module) whose fixtures drive the actual Flask routes (`create_sleeve_via_route`, `create_rule_via_route`) with a payload shaped exactly like a real operator's POST body — no `sleeve_id`/`mode`/`id` key, ever; the module's own docstring calls adding one of those keys "FORBIDDEN" since it would defeat the cycle's purpose. Existing route-shaped CRUD tests (`tests/app/test_sleeves_routes_crud.py`) never drove the engine, which is why they didn't catch this either — the gap was specifically "route-shaped state" crossed with "reaches a real tick," and no existing test combined both.

### Status (updated as each finding's GREEN lands)

**Finding #3 (HIGH) — RESOLVED at `4abfaf6`.** Sleeve status "PAPER" is now reachable: `arm_sleeve_rule` (`POST /api/sleeves/<id>/rules/<rule_id>/arm`), after its existing AC-13 shadow-fire gate passes, promotes the owning sleeve's status `SHADOW`→`PAPER` — but only from `SHADOW` (a `LIVE` sleeve is never demoted by arming one more rule) — and additionally now refuses arming outright with `409` while the sleeve is `PAUSED_RECONCILIATION` (arming must never clear a money-truth pause as a side effect). This closes the specific failure mode the audit live-observed: sleeve status is what the tick's step-0 cleanup, the panel status badge, and the Disarm control all key off, so a paper-armed rule sitting inside a SHADOW-status sleeve had its resting orders canceled every tick while the panel showed a calm "standby" badge with Disarm disabled. `disarm_sleeve` is unchanged (it already demoted sleeve+rules to SHADOW). RED at `c300034` (`TestArmRoutePromotesSleeveStatus`, `TestPaperSleeveTickCoherence`, `TestPanelBadgeCoherence`, `TestFullLadderEndToEnd` in `tests/sleeves/test_paper_arm_status_promotion.py`), GREEN at `4abfaf6` — 5 of the file's 6 tests pass; the sixth (`TestFullLadderEndToEnd::test_create_shadow_fire_arm_paper_order_and_survival_end_to_end`, the full production-path capstone) stays RED, deliberately, until finding #1's `sleeve_id` engine fix lands (sf-eng task #52) — the capstone drives a rule through the real create route end-to-end, which still crashes on finding #1 independent of this fix. 52/52 pre-existing sleeve route/panel tests pass alongside. **Not yet RED-pinned (flagged by sf-eng, tracked here rather than silently assumed):** the `409`-while-paused branch and the "LIVE is never demoted" branch are both implemented and agreed contract, but have no dedicated regression test yet.

On fold failure both the per-rule and new sleeve-level `realized_pnl_usd` render `None` → `"n/a"` on the panel, never a fabricated `$0.00`. `reporting.py`'s `_build_sleeve_digest_summaries` now derives from the SAME fold — the stale "no fill-attribution wired yet" docstring (finding #8, `reporting.py:196-199`, already false once the panel wired attribution) is corrected, and the digest renders `"n/a"` rather than a hardcoded `realized $+0.00`. **Fix (verified against source, `sleeves/rules/runner.py`):** the compensation criterion is now grounded in DB truth instead of runner-local containers. Before dispatch, the runner captures a baseline of this rule's existing `sleeve_orders` row ids. On a zero-outcome crash (no fire recorded, no `ActionResult` carrying an order), it compensates (restores the pacing episode) ONLY if querying `sleeve_orders` again shows no row for this rule beyond that baseline. This works because the RESERVED insert precedes every broker submit, so the row survives a crash anywhere in the submit/ack/attach window — DB evidence covers the crash window that runner-local evidence cannot. **Fails closed on the baseline re-query itself failing:** if that query raises, `order_path_started` is set `True` (i.e. "assume an order may have started"), so the episode is kept latched rather than restored — an unknowable state never gets treated as "safe to re-fire." The pre-row crash class (finding #9's original scenario — a sizing/`KeyError` before any DB insert) still compensates correctly, unchanged, pinned by the pre-existing `TestPacingLatchSurvivesDispatchCrash`.

## DE-ATLAS-SLOW-QUERY-001 — Atlas community-strategies fetch, unindexed sort eliminated (2026-07-11)

Branch: `fix/atlas-fetch-slow-query` | Base: `origin/main` b7e61b6 | HEAD: eb53a19

### Problem

Every live Atlas pull in `advisors/community_strats.py::load_community_strategies` timed out with `reason="AtlasFetchTimeout"`, so `captplanet.strategies` candidates were never cached and the Strategy Builder's community-suggested path silently degraded to built-new-only on every run. `_fetch_fn` issued a single `find()` with a server-side `sort=[("oos_metrics.sharpe", DESCENDING)]` over a projection that included `edn_string` (a multi-KB field per doc). `oos_metrics.sharpe` has no index on the live collection (only `_id_` is indexed), so this sorted the full ~11,227-doc corpus, at full document size, unindexed, on disk -- observed to take ~50 s in production, exceeding `_ATLAS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S` (45 s) on every call.

### First attempt (commit b2afe1b) and why it was insufficient

The initial fix split the query in two: a lightweight, `edn_string`-free selection query carrying the sort + `.limit(_MAX_FETCH_DOCS)`, followed by an indexed `_id: {"$in": ...}` full-document fetch with no sort. The theory: sorting small documents (two fields) would be cheap even though `oos_metrics.sharpe` stays unindexed.

The PM's live-Atlas gate against this version failed: **45.03 s timeout, 0 candidates returned.** Direct Mongo reads during diagnosis found the real cause -- `captplanet.strategies` has no usable index besides `_id`. A server-side sort is an unindexed COLLSCAN regardless of projection size; shrinking the projection reduces disk I/O per document but does not touch the (dominant) unindexed-sort cost across all ~11,227 docs.

### Fix (commit dd1406e): eliminate server-side sorting entirely

`_fetch_fn` was restructured into three steps, with no `sort=` anywhere in the Mongo query:

1. **Lightweight, unsorted, uncapped selection** -- `collection.find({}, {"_id": 1, "oos_metrics.Sharpe": 1})` over the whole collection. No `sort=`, no `.limit()`.
2. **Client-side rank + bound** -- the selection docs are parsed and sorted descending in Python (`selection_docs.sort(key=_oos_sharpe, reverse=True)`), then sliced to the top `_MAX_FETCH_DOCS` ids.
3. **Targeted full-document fetch** -- `collection.find({"_id": {"$in": top_ids}}, _PROJECTION)`, an indexed `_id` lookup requiring no sort.

Moving the sort into Python is safe here because step 1 only transfers two small fields per document (cheap even unindexed); the ranking cost that was dominating the timeout moves to an in-memory Python sort of a small list.

### `_MAX_FETCH_DOCS` retuned for live timing (500 -> 100 -> 50)

Even with the sort eliminated, `edn_string` averages ~153 KB/doc live -- an indexed `_id` fetch of too many full documents dominates the 45 s budget on its own. `_MAX_FETCH_DOCS` was reduced 500 -> 100 in the same commit as the query restructure (still 5x headroom over `MAX_COMMUNITY_CANDIDATES_PER_RUN=20`), then tightened 100 -> 50 (commit eb53a19) after the PM's live gate against the 100-cap version passed but at 33.95 s -- only ~11 s headroom under the 45 s bound, judged insufficient margin for the droplet's slower 2 vCPU single-thread parse. The public `limit` parameter (post-fetch, post-dedup, caller-level) is unaffected -- a separate, independent control.

### Result (PM-verified live, not self-reported)

## DE-ATLAS-SHARPE-FIELD-001 -- Community-strategies Sharpe field correction: sharpe -> Sharpe (2026-07-11)

Branch: `fix/atlas-fetch-slow-query` | HEAD: eb53a19

### Problem (pre-existing, cycle-independent -- found while diagnosing DE-ATLAS-SLOW-QUERY-001's live-gate failure)

Direct Mongo reads against the live `captplanet.strategies` collection, taken while diagnosing the timeout above, found a second, unrelated defect: all three Sharpe-consumption sites in `advisors/community_strats.py` (client-side selection ranking, the dedup tie-break, and the `min_oos_sharpe` filter) read `oos_metrics['sharpe']` (lowercase) -- a key present on **0 of 11,227** live docs. The real field is `oos_metrics['Sharpe']` (capital S), **string-valued**, present on **10,067 of 11,227** docs. Every community candidate was being ranked, deduped, and filtered as if it had no Sharpe at all -- the sharpe-based selection was effectively a no-op ordering (all docs tied at `-inf`), silently degrading candidate quality without any error, exception, or D-1 signal.

### Fix

A single shared helper, `_parse_sharpe(oos_metrics) -> float | None`, now backs every consumption site:

- Reads the corrected `oos_metrics['Sharpe']` key.
- Defensively parses to `float`, returning `None` (never raising) for: missing field, non-numeric string (`"N/A"`), percent-formatted string (`"12.3%"`), or `"nan"`/`"inf"` -- Python's bare `float()` accepts the latter two as valid floats, but neither is a valid Sharpe ratio, so both are explicitly rejected via `math.isnan`/`math.isinf`.

`_oos_sharpe(doc)` wraps `_parse_sharpe(doc.get("oos_metrics"))`, returning `float("-inf")` on `None` -- preserving the pre-existing "missing/unparseable sharpe never wins a tie, never gets excluded by `min_oos_sharpe`" contract, now pointed at a field that actually has data.

### Invariants preserved

- D-1 never-raises: `_parse_sharpe` never raises regardless of input shape.
- `min_oos_sharpe` keep-rule unchanged: docs lacking a genuinely-parseable Sharpe are always kept, never excluded by the floor.
- No change to `_PROJECTION`, `_bounded_fetch_fn`, or the validate/dedup/filter/limit pipeline structure -- only the field path + parsing.

### Files changed

- `advisors/community_strats.py` -- new `_parse_sharpe()` helper (adds `import math`); `_oos_sharpe()` rewritten to use it; `min_oos_sharpe` filter in `load_community_strategies` rewritten to use it.
- `tests/advisors/test_community_strats_sharpe_field.py` (new) -- `TestRealSharpeFieldPath` (ranking/filtering/dedup actually select on the real field), `TestDefensiveSharpeParsing` (malformed variants sort to bottom, never raise; numeric-string comparison correctness).
- `tests/advisors/test_community_strats.py` -- sibling assertions re-pointed to the corrected field where they had encoded the stale `sharpe` key.

### Reference

DE-ATLAS-SHARPE-FIELD-001; branch `fix/atlas-fetch-slow-query`; HEAD `eb53a19`; found and fixed in the same cycle as `DE-ATLAS-SLOW-QUERY-001` above; see `docs/generated/advisors_community_strats.md` for the current field-parsing reference.

## DE-ATLAS-STAT-FIELD-001 + DE-ATLAS-DEEP-TREE-001 -- Community-candidate ranking field-path bug generalized + deep-tree exception containment (2026-07-11)

Branch: `fix/atlas-fetch-slow-query` | HEAD: 6894afd

### AC-F1 [HIGH] -- `advisors/build_plan_generator.py::admit_community_candidates` / `_stat` -- Sharpe field-path bug generalizes to objective ranking

The field-path bug fixed in `community_strats._parse_sharpe` (`DE-ATLAS-SHARPE-FIELD-001`) generalized one layer up: `admit_community_candidates`'s internal `_stat()` ranking helper read lowercase keys that exist on 0 live `captplanet.strategies` docs --

- `cut_drawdown` wanted `'max_drawdown'` (real key: `'Max Drawdown'`)
- `volatility_mitigation` wanted `'volatility'` (real key: `'Volatility (ann.)'`)
- `lift_risk_adjusted` wanted `'sharpe'` (real key: `'Sharpe'`)

-- so every doc looked stat-missing for 3 of 4 objectives, and the ranking silently fell back to arbitrary insertion-order rather than the documented per-objective stat.

**Fix:** `_stat()` now reads the real title-case `oos_metrics` keys. It strips a trailing `%` before `float()` for the two percentage-based metrics -- `Max Drawdown` and `Volatility (ann.)` are `%`-string-valued on real docs; `Sharpe` is plain-decimal and is NOT stripped, matching `community_strats._parse_sharpe`'s parse contract exactly. `nan`/`inf` values (which pass Python's bare `float()` but are not valid metric values) are rejected post-parse. Missing/unparseable stats still sort last (`float(-inf)`/`float(+inf)` sentinel per objective direction), and `_stat()` never raises.

### AC-F2 [MEDIUM] -- `advisors/community_strats.py` per-doc loop composition-hash step -- deep-tree exception containment

`_strip_ids` (the first step of `_composition_hash`) is recursive -- unlike `symphony_schema`'s deliberately iterative traversal -- and can raise `RecursionError` on a pathologically deep (but structurally valid) tree at roughly 500 nesting levels. The composition-hash call site had no `try`/`except`, unlike the other 3 steps in the same per-doc loop (`json.loads`, `validate_tree`, `extract_tickers` each already had their own). One pathological doc could therefore propagate an uncaught exception out of `load_community_strategies`, violating the D-1 never-raising contract and losing the *entire* batch, not just the one bad doc.

**Fix:** wrapped the composition-hash step in its own `try`/`except`, matching the existing per-step containment pattern -- any exception there (`RecursionError`, `MemoryError`, or otherwise) now increments `parse_failed` and drops only that one doc; the loop continues. `_strip_ids` itself is intentionally left recursive (PM-approved minimal fix) -- a rare deep doc dropping is acceptable latent-risk containment, not observed live data loss.

### Invariants preserved

- Both modules remain off-execution-path, advisory-only -- no live Mongo/network/HTTP calls in tests, no `is_live` propagation, no retry-policy change.
- D-1 never-raises contract unchanged and, for AC-F2, actively strengthened (a class of previously-uncaught batch-aborting exception is now contained per-doc).

### Files changed

- `advisors/build_plan_generator.py` -- `_stat()` rewritten to read the real title-case keys with `%`-strip + nan/inf-reject parsing.
- `advisors/community_strats.py` -- composition-hash step wrapped in `try`/`except` (accounted as `parse_failed`).
- `tests/advisors/test_build_plan_atlas_admission.py` -- 8 fixtures re-pointed to real title-case/%-string field shapes + 1 new malformed-value test.
- `tests/advisors/test_community_strats_deep_tree_robustness.py` (new) -- a real depth-700 structurally-valid tree + a `MemoryError` monkeypatch seam.

## DE-ATLAS-STAT-FIELD-002 -- Key-union for real %-suffix/bare stat field forms (2026-07-11)

Branch: `fix/atlas-fetch-slow-query` | HEAD: 81a8d46

### Problem

The PM's live gate against `DE-ATLAS-STAT-FIELD-001` (commit 6894afd) found `Sharpe` ranking correct (10/10) but `cut_drawdown` and `volatility_mitigation` came back all-`None`. Direct inspection of the real `captplanet.strategies` collection found it raw-data-inconsistent: docs carry EITHER a `%`-suffixed key form (`'Max Drawdown %'`, `'Volatility (ann.) %'` -- the dominant real form) OR the bare form (`'Max Drawdown'`, `'Volatility (ann.)'`), both `%`-string-valued. `community_strats` passes `oos_metrics` through verbatim with no key normalization, so both forms genuinely coexist in the source collection. `Sharpe` is unaffected -- a single key form (`'Sharpe'`) across all live docs.

### Fix

`_stat()` generalized to accept a candidate **key-union list** rather than a single key: it tries each key in order, and the first key that yields a genuinely **parseable** value wins -- a present-but-unparseable value at one key falls through to the next candidate key rather than short-circuiting to `None`.

- `cut_drawdown` now reads `['Max Drawdown %', 'Max Drawdown']`.
- `volatility_mitigation` now reads `['Volatility (ann.) %', 'Volatility (ann.)']`.
- `lift_risk_adjusted` stays single-key `['Sharpe']`.

No known doc carries both forms of a pair, so precedence on a genuine collision is unspecified but deterministic (list order) -- not something any real doc exercises. The `%`-strip-then-`float()` + nan/inf-reject parse logic per key is unchanged from `DE-ATLAS-STAT-FIELD-001`.

### Result (PM-verified live gate)

All 3 numeric-stat objectives (`cut_drawdown`, `volatility_mitigation`, `lift_risk_adjusted`) rank correctly on real cached data, 10/10 candidates each. `-n0` targeted suite: 112 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed.

### Invariants preserved

- Off-execution-path, advisory-only -- no live Mongo/network/HTTP calls in tests, no `is_live` propagation, no retry-policy change.
- `diversify`'s Jaccard-overlap ranking and the `CandidateInfo` admission/tagging logic are unchanged.

### Files changed

- `advisors/build_plan_generator.py` -- `_stat()` generalized to accept a key-union list; the three per-objective call sites updated to pass their key-union.
- `tests/advisors/test_build_plan_atlas_admission.py` -- 4 fixtures re-pointed to the `%`-suffix form as primary + 2 new decisive tests mixing both key forms in one ranking call each.

### Known deferred follow-up (not part of this fix, flagged for a future cycle)

`admit_community_candidates`'s `diversify` branch calls `_extract_tickers_from_tree` on every still-`remaining` candidate on every outer greedy-loop iteration -- O(n^2) total tree-walk work in the candidate-pool size. Bounded today by `_MAX_FETCH_DOCS=50`, so not currently a live-timing problem; cheap fix is a precomputed `{sid: tickers}` map before the loop. Non-blocking; not required for this cycle's gate.
