## DE-GUARD-ALPHA-PRECONDITIONS-001 — Guard-Alpha stop-justification preconditions: Kaminski & Lo (2014) per-symphony measurement (2026-07-23)

Branch: feat/guard-alpha-preconditions | Base: `0c5d3e86` | HEAD: `fa16ca84` (3-round cycle -- see Live-Gate Correction section below for rounds 2-3)

### Summary

Guard Alpha's expected-return case rests on a conditional theorem that had never been measured per symphony against data the system already collects (identified as gap 5 of the R&D methodology external-validation report, `docs/research/methodology-validation-2026-07.md` §2.5/§4, provenance for this cycle). This feature computes, per symphony, the lag-1 autocorrelation (ρ̂) of the if-held daily return series and compares it against the daily (non-annualized) Sharpe ratio (SR̂) — the sufficient condition Kaminski & Lo (2014) identify for a trailing-stop overlay to add expected-return value under momentum, as opposed to the always-negative case under random-walk returns. Advisory display only: one new module (`guard_preconditions.py`), one new read-only GET route, one new Performance-tab panel. No engine behavior change, no automatic enable/disable of Guard Alpha.

### Citation (binding)

Kaminski, K.M. & Lo, A.W. (2014), "When Do Stop-Loss Rules Stop Losses?", *Journal of Financial Markets* 18, 234-254. DOI 10.1016/j.finmar.2013.07.001 (SSRN 968338 for the working-paper version). **Never cite the `alo.mit.edu` mirror — it is a dead link (404).** During RED-writing, an early draft of `guard_preconditions.py`'s citation comment cited the wrong paper title/page range ("An Analysis of Trailing Stop-Loss Strategies", pp. 108-125) — corrected before implementation and regression-guarded by `tests/guard_preconditions/test_classify_stop_justification.py::TestCitation` (4 sub-tests: correct DOI present, correct title present, wrong title absent, dead `alo.mit.edu` string absent). A self-inflicted near-miss during RED-writing is worth recording: the test-writer's own "NOT this URL" aside in a draft citation comment briefly contained the literal forbidden substring `alo.mit.edu`, silently failing its own regression test from the first RED run without being noticed until a later pass — caught and fixed before handoff.

### Sample design (AC-5, amended from the original feature plan)

The plan's original AC-5 wording specified "daily diffs of `shadow_history.current_return`" for the secondary/live sample and left the primary/replay accessor unspecified beyond "reuse the existing replay seam." Both were corrected by PM ruling after two independent recon findings, and the plan was amended in commit `b1d97b36` before RED work began:

1. **Primary sample is NOT `autotuner._collect_sim_returns`.** That function returns the sparse per-TRIGGERED-day guard-alpha delta series — the wrong quantity for a persistence/Sharpe measurement over the full if-held trajectory. The correct accessor, `collect_if_held_daily_returns` (new, `autotuner.py`), reads `ticks[-1]["return"]` for EVERY date in the replay's `history_data`, unconditionally. Pinned by `tests/autotuner/test_collect_if_held_daily_returns.py::TestOutputIsNotTheGuardAlphaSeries`, which monkeypatches `_replay_exit_tick` to never trigger and confirms `_collect_sim_returns` legitimately returns `[]` on the same data while the new function returns every day.
2. **Secondary sample is raw per-day `shadow_history.current_return`, never differenced.** `current_return` is already a per-day return, not cumulative — proven empirically against production data (project memory `project_shadow_return_per_day_proven_empirically.md`). The plan's original "daily diffs" wording would have differenced an already-per-day series, a return-of-a-return error. `analytics.get_shadow_current_return_daily_series` (new) returns the raw values, EOD-row-only (last row per `trading_day` by `ts_utc` — an intraday-frequency-contamination addendum ruled at the same time: a mid-day row would silently change the sampling frequency), **concatenated across ALL position epochs, no epoch filter** (CORRECTED 2026-07-24 at the PM's live gate -- this supersedes the epoch-scoping half of what this AC-5 amendment originally specified; full account in the Live-Gate Correction section below). Pinned by `TestRawPerDayPassThroughNotDiffed` (using the exact oscillating production pattern from the memory: +1.68, +2.17, -5.50, +2.26, +1.0) and `TestEodOnlySelection` (3 intraday rows on one day, only the 19:00 EOD row must contribute).

**Why the replay sample is primary:** N≈250 (the autotuner's walk-forward window) vs. the ~90-day pruned `shadow_history` retention window gives ρ̂ stderr ≈ ±0.06 vs. ±0.11 — meaningfully tighter, with no new data infrastructure required. When the two samples disagree on verdict class, both are shown with their own N (AC-8) — the route never silently prefers one.

### Cache-hit-only constraint on the replay sample (hard contract, not a default; bounded backward probe added 2026-07-24, see Live-Gate Correction below)

`autotuner.build_if_held_replay_series(symphony_id)` — the route-facing orchestration seam — may read `synthetic_history`'s existing file cache (via `get_cached_synthetic_history_only`, which as of the R2 live-gate fix probes UP TO `AUTOTUNE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_TRADING_DAYS=10` NYSE trading days backward from today rather than checking only the exact current date — see the Live-Gate Correction section below) but **must never trigger a live fetch** (`synthetic_history.fetch_bars`, or `generate_synthetic_history`'s fetch-on-miss fallback). Exhausting the entire backward window without a hit returns `None`; it never falls through to fetching. The route renders the honest degraded state for that sample and falls back to a shadow-only row per AC-8.

This was flagged as a non-blocking open question during RED-writing (the plan's "read-only SQLite" Architecture line didn't obviously cover the expensive 250-day replay-history assembly, and an earlier "synchronous on-demand, matches other advisory routes" framing was floated) and the PM ruled it definitively as a hard contract: **Architecture Constraint 5** (the dashboard/UI never reruns the engine — assembling 250-day history on request is engine machinery, not a read), **request latency** (a cold fetch can take minutes inside a dashboard GET), and the standing **bill-protection directive** (a dashboard refresh must never be able to drive Alpaca fetch volume). Pinned by `tests/autotuner/test_build_if_held_replay_series.py::TestCacheMissNeverFetches` (accessor-level) and `tests/app/test_guard_alpha_preconditions_route.py::TestColdCacheNeverFetchesEndToEnd` (route-level, deliberately exercising the REAL `build_if_held_replay_series`, not mocked, unlike every other route test).

The cache-key derivation this reader depends on was extracted into a shared single source of truth, `synthetic_history._resolve_history_cache_key` (PM hard DRY requirement) — both `generate_synthetic_history` (the network-capable writer) and `get_cached_synthetic_history_only` (the new cache-only reader) call this one function rather than each deriving the tickers → holdings-hash → versioned-filename key independently, closing a drift risk where a mirrored re-implementation could silently miss a genuine same-day, same-holdings cache hit. Date resolution uses `synthetic_history.utc_to_eastern` (the same DST-aware conversion `generate_synthetic_history` itself uses) rather than `alpha_bot_execution.get_current_et`, which pulls a heavy production import graph and reads several credentials at import time — unnecessary weight for a date string on an advisory dashboard GET.

### Live-gate correction (R3, 2026-07-24): epoch-scope reversal + backward cache probe

The PM's live functional gate — read-only SQL run directly against a fresh droplet database snapshot — falsified two assumptions baked into the spec above and blocked cycle-complete for a third round. Recorded here as this entry's own tests-green-never-sufficient exhibit: 160/160 tests were GREEN and two prior sufficiency reviews had already passed before this gate ran.

**R1 — epoch scoping was wrong, not merely incomplete.** `position_epoch` is a UUID that churns every 1-2 trading days in production (14-18 distinct epochs per symphony observed over 23 retained trading days). The original current-epoch-scoped query (mirroring `_get_shadow_cumulative_trajectory`'s epoch-additive pattern) capped every symphony's shadow `n_obs` at 1-2 — permanently `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` in production despite 23 real trading days of history existing. Fix: `get_shadow_current_return_daily_series` now concatenates ALL position epochs with no epoch filter at all — epoch-column presence is no longer even checked, and the legacy (pre-migration, no-`position_epoch`-column) code path and the migrated-schema path collapsed into one identical query. **Why this does not contradict the epoch-additive rule used elsewhere:** that rule protects `_get_shadow_cumulative_trajectory`'s CUMULATIVE $-saved level — chaining a prior epoch's absolute level into a new position would fabricate phantom returns, so that function stays epoch-scoped and is UNCHANGED by this fix (confirmed untouched in the diff). A per-day `current_return`, by contrast, is that day's own independent if-held observation regardless of which epoch it fell in — concatenating independent daily observations across epochs is statistically valid; chaining a cumulative level across a position reset is not. This is the load-bearing distinction, not an exception carved into the rule.

**R2 — the replay cache was cold by construction on most days.** `get_cached_synthetic_history_only` originally keyed on exactly today's date, so it only hit on the one day per week the autotune actually ran; the droplet's newest cache file was 6 calendar days stale at gate time. Fix: a new named constant `AUTOTUNE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_TRADING_DAYS=10` (source: weekly autotune cadence plus a buffer for a missed/aborted run), and the reader now walks backward through up to that many NYSE trading days — via `market_calendar.is_trading_day`, this project's single source of truth for trading-day determination, never a re-derived weekday proxy — re-deriving the cache key via the same shared `_resolve_history_cache_key` at EACH candidate date for the CURRENT holdings. Newest-hit-wins: today (offset 0) is checked first and returned immediately on a hit, falling out of the loop order rather than requiring a separate sort step. A holdings change since an aged file was written naturally degrades to a miss for that candidate — the aged file's embedded holdings-hash simply won't match a freshly computed hash for current holdings, no special-casing required. The CACHE-HIT-ONLY / zero-network guarantee is unchanged and was explicitly re-verified, not assumed to still hold: `tests/synthetic_history/test_autotune_cache_backward_probe.py` confirms zero `fetch_bars` calls anywhere across the backward walk.

**Retention interaction (honest disclosure, not fixed this round):** the droplet's `shadow_history` table retains ~23 trading days, below `N_MIN_OBS=40`. Even with the R1 fix, shadow verdicts will therefore practically render `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` in production until the operator extends retention — a known product-level knob (surfaced separately in the PM's ship report), not a defect this cycle introduces or is scoped to fix. `N_MIN_OBS=40` itself is unchanged and stays principled. R2's backward probe partially offsets this on the replay side only (the replay sample is now warm across up to 10 trading days of staleness instead of same-day-only, meaningfully improving the "how often is this actually useful" picture from what was true at the original cycle-complete) — it does not touch the shadow-side retention ceiling.

**Verification.** Ga-tw's independent sufficiency review (not implementer self-report) at HEAD `fa16ca84`: `pytest -n0` on the 2 round-3 target files — 16/16 GREEN; full feature-scope re-run (9 files, the entire guard-alpha-preconditions surface) — 175/175 GREEN, 0 errors. Adversarial read of the actual diff (not just the commit message) confirmed the R1 fix is a pure deletion (the epoch-filtered query and its `has_epoch_column` branch are gone; the one surviving query is byte-identical to the old legacy-schema branch: `MAX(ts_utc)`-per-`trading_day` EOD selection, `current_return` column, `trading_day ASC` order, no epoch predicate) and confirmed the R2 backward-probe loop is boundary-inclusive (checks offsets 0 through 10 for the constant's value of 10), holdings-hash-sensitive by construction, and contains zero references to `fetch_bars` anywhere in the function body. Independently re-verified by this doc-writer, not merely quoting ga-tw's numbers: same 175/175 at HEAD `fa16ca84` on a clean working tree, `ruff check`/`ruff format --check` clean on `analytics.py` and `synthetic_history.py`.

### Verdict classification (AC-3): ordered priority chain, not independent checks

`guard_preconditions.classify_stop_justification` resolves to exactly 5 classes via an ORDERED priority chain, PM-ruled (this ordering, and the ambiguous-region resolution below, is the interpretation ruling for AC-3's under-specified region):

1. `insufficient_reason is not None` → `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`
2. `elif sharpe_daily <= 0` → `NEGATIVE_EDGE`
3. `elif rho - rho_ci - sharpe_daily >= -ε` → `SUFFICIENT_MET`
4. `elif rho - sharpe_daily >= -ε` → `SUFFICIENT_LIKELY`
5. `else` (includes the ambiguous region: ρ̂ < SR̂ but ρ̂+CI ≥ SR̂) → `NOT_MET`

Step 2 must gate before any ρ-vs-SR comparison — a negative or zero Sharpe is trivially "cleared" by any real ρ, so checking ρ first would wrongly classify a stop as justified when the underlying edge is negative (an explicit adversarial trap in the test suite, `test_classify_stop_justification.py`). The under-specified ambiguous region resolves to `NOT_MET`, worded strictly as an **evidence statement**, never a settled fact: `NOT_MET`'s copy reads "this evidence does not demonstrate that observed return persistence clears the daily Sharpe ratio bar... not disproven either; an evidence finding, not a settled fact" — the K&L random-walk-drag theorem is presented as the conditional theorem it is (a "conditional theorem is not itself confirmed or refuted here"), never as a claim proven true for that specific symphony. This prevents negative-direction overclaiming: a naive implementation could have worded `NOT_MET` as "stop is unjustified," which would misstate the theorem as confirmed. No verdict copy, across all 5 classes, ever renders "stop unjustified." `NOT_MET`'s copy additionally states that variance/drawdown reduction can survive under an IID return process, independent of this precondition — the CRRA-EU objective legitimately values that.

A separate float-precision fix, `_BOUNDARY_EPS = 1e-9`, absorbs float64 subtraction noise at exact-by-construction boundaries (e.g. `0.30 - 0.10 == 0.19999999999999998` in IEEE 754 binary64) on both inclusive comparisons above, without blurring the test suite's much larger intentional distinctions (`1e-7`). This fix originated in the implementer's (ga-impl) WIP — a real float64 precision issue the test-writer's exact-equality boundary tests exposed but had not anticipated needing a fix for — and was pinned with a dedicated regression test (`TestBoundaryEpsilonTolerance`, 3 tests) after the fact, at the implementer's own request.

### Response schema: symmetric full-object degradation

`GET /api/guard-alpha-preconditions`'s per-symphony `{replay, shadow}` samples are ALWAYS a complete 6-field object — `{rho, rho_ci, sharpe_daily, n_obs, verdict, sample_source}` — never bare `null`. An unavailable sample (cold/missing replay cache, or a symphony with no `shadow_history` rows yet) degrades to `{rho: null, rho_ci: null, sharpe_daily: null, n_obs: 0, verdict: "INSUFFICIENT_DATA", sample_source: <stable id>}` — the same 5-class vocabulary a genuinely-thin real sample would produce, so callers never null-check a sample before reading its fields. `sample_source` is ALWAYS the stable sample-family identifier (`"if_held_replay"` / `"shadow_history"`), never a reason string — AC-8's two-sample-disagreement display keys on this stable identity.

**Provenance (credit attribution, requested explicitly by the test-writer for this entry, per the PM's honesty directive — attributed accurately, not defaulted to the test-writer):** this uniform contract originated in the implementer's (ga-flask) route WIP, not the test-writer's original RED tests, which had assumed an asymmetric replay-null/shadow-null shape. The test-writer adopted and symmetrically extended the contract after reviewing the implementation (commit `f8d5ca29`), and the PM blessed it as superseding the earlier null-shadow-shaped pin.

A related fix, also route-side: a `_json_safe_float()` guard sanitizes `NaN`/`Infinity` to `None` strictly at the JSON-serialization boundary inside `_sample_row()`. `compute_persistence_stats` legitimately returns `math.nan` on a genuinely flat (zero-variance) series — correct math-layer behavior — but Python's `json` module serializes that as the bare, RFC-8259-invalid tokens `NaN`/`Infinity`, which a real browser's `response.json()` rejects, silently breaking the WHOLE panel for every symphony via `static/performance.js`'s catch-all `.catch()`. Verdict classification still runs against the original, unsanitized `PersistenceStats` object — only the JSON-facing float fields are sanitized, never the classification logic. **Found by the test-writer running the live route during sufficiency review (not by inspection alone), fixed by the implementer** at HEAD `49aba17c` — this is the fix this cycle's final commit ships.

### Deferred scope boundary: regime-switching test

Kaminski & Lo's third precondition — two-state regime-switching value existing only when the low-regime equity mean sits below the risk-free rate (μ₂ < rf) — is explicitly OUT of this cycle. It requires regime-model estimation that would dominate the cycle on its own; noted in the feature plan's Scope Boundaries as a deferred follow-on, not a silently dropped gap. If pursued, it is a separate cycle.

## DE-EXIT-FRICTION-REALIZED-001 -- Exit-tuning friction term + realized-basis $-saved + turnover surfacing (2026-07-24)

Branch: `feat/exit-friction-realized-savings` | Base: `ccda9abe` | HEAD (feature-complete): `8418f55b`

### Summary

Closes the transaction-cost gap identified in `docs/research/methodology-validation-2026-07.md` (internal audit, §3: the Optuna exit-tuning replay was "100% gross-of-cost"; the live Guard-Alpha $-saved headline was decision-time-snapshot based; turnover was unquantified despite `exit_triggers` holding the data since migration 005). Three additive parts, one cycle, no live-engine decision-path changes anywhere:

1. A named, non-tunable friction constant (`SIM_EXIT_FRICTION_PCT`, `autotuner.py`) applied at all three replay-layer exit-accounting sites so the CRRA-EU objective, the PBO veto, and the OOS-alpha acceptance gate all evaluate net-of-friction guard alpha.
2. A realized-basis $-saved figure (`reporting.py` Stage 2, `app.py`'s `GET /api/guard-alpha-summary`) computed from the first post-rebalance observed `shadow_history` value, reported ADDITIVELY alongside (never replacing) the existing snapshot basis.
3. Read-only per-symphony exit-turnover stats (`database.py`, new `GET /api/exit-turnover`) with a retention-honest `coverage_days` field and an estimated annual friction-drag percentage.

Production commits: `d7a036dd` (autotuner.py/reporting.py/database.py -- the three friction sites, Stage-2 realized fields, turnover query layer), `0c87670b` (app.py routes + templates/static JS -- dual-basis headline, exit-turnover panel), `06f08c61`+`8418f55b` (RED/GREEN for a review-found forward-looking gap, see "Incumbent-Score Tripwire" below).

### AC-1 / Finding E -- units correction: `SIM_EXIT_FRICTION_PCT = 0.5`, not `0.005`

The feature plan's original text proposed `0.005` `[PM-ASSUMED]`, sourced directly from `composer_backtest_client._DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_PERCENT` (`composer_backtest_client.py:71`). Pre-RED recon (ga2-tw) caught that this literal is a DECIMAL FRACTION (`0.005 = 0.5%`, per its own docstring) while the replay subtraction sites operate in PERCENT-POINT space (`tick['return']`, the sibling `-0.20` deviation-penalty fallback, `RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION = 100.0`). Copying `0.005` verbatim into a percent-point-scaled subtraction would have applied 100x too little friction -- 0.005 percentage points instead of the intended 0.5 -- silently defeating the whole feature while every test built against the same (wrong) unit convention would still pass. PM-ruled correction, frozen before RED work began: `SIM_EXIT_FRICTION_PCT = 0.5`, with the derivation (`_DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_PERCENT * RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION`) shown explicitly in the constant's source comment rather than silently absorbed. Same defect class as the project's standing unit-comparability memory (`feedback_verify_unit_comparability_on_threshold_constants`) -- verified independently by this doc-writer before recording: `RETURN_PCT_TO_FRACTION = 100.0` at `autotuner.py:727` and `_DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_PERCENT = 0.005` at `composer_backtest_client.py:71` both confirmed real.

### AC-2v2 -- friction applied at ALL THREE replay-layer exit-accounting sites (ga2-opt pre-RED recon)

The original plan text (AC-2) scoped the friction subtraction to `_collect_sim_returns` only. ga2-opt's pre-RED recon found this insufficient and the PM froze the amendment (AC-2v2) before RED work began: the subtraction is applied identically at `_collect_sim_returns` (`autotuner.py:1523-1526`), `_collect_sim_returns_dated` (`autotuner.py:1717-1720`), and `run_simulation` (`autotuner.py:1984-1987`) -- each as `triggered_return = tick.get("return", 0.0) + penalty - SIM_EXIT_FRICTION_PCT`, a distinct term from the sibling `-0.20` deviation-dict `penalty` (different semantics: modeling-uncertainty haircut vs. trading friction; folding them together would destroy the audit trail of both).

**Why three sites, not one:** `_collect_sim_returns_dated` feeds `cscv_date_returns` into `math_engine.compute_pbo` (the Phase-3 PBO overfitting veto); `run_simulation` computes `oos_alpha`/`fallback_oos_alpha`/`default_oos_alpha` consumed by the acceptance-gate accept/reject cascade. Single-site application (only `_collect_sim_returns`, which `run_simulation_crra_eu` calls for the trial objective) would have left the PBO veto and the OOS-alpha acceptance gate evaluating gross-of-friction guard alpha while the trial objective itself went net-of-friction -- reintroducing the exact gross-vs-net inconsistency this feature exists to close, just relocated from the objective to the gate. A dedicated blast-radius test (`tests/autotuner/test_exit_friction_blast_radius.py`, AC-10) pins zero references to `SIM_EXIT_FRICTION_PCT` outside the replay/reporting/analytics surfaces -- specifically confirming zero references from `alpha_bot_execution.py`/`math_engine.py`'s live decision functions.

### AC-5/AC-6 -- Ruling A: realized-basis sourcing, never `bot_state` (ga2-tw pre-RED recon)

Stage 2's realized-basis $-saved fields source EXCLUSIVELY from `database.load_latest_shadow_row(sym_id, current_date_str, et_cutoff=None)` -- the SAME accessor Stage 1 uses, called with no cutoff (Stage 1 restricts to at/before `STAGE1_SNAPSHOT_CUTOFF_ET`; Stage 2 wants the latest AVAILABLE post-rebalance row, the opposite constraint). **The plan's original wording did not explicitly forbid `bot_state`'s live `current_return`** -- ga2-tw's recon flagged that using it would silently reintroduce the exact `DE-GUARD-ALPHA-SAVED-001`/PR-#80 defect class this project already paid to fix once: the action phase clobbers `bot_state[sym_id]["current_return"]` every cycle with a frozen-basket reconstruction, and 7 of 11 audited production days were sign-flipped before that fix shipped. PM ruled the sourcing rule frozen before RED work began: `shadow_history` only, no fallback tier (unlike Stage 1's three-tier lookup) -- absent data means the three new fields (`realized_observed_return`/`realized_source`/`saved_dollars_realized`) are simply ABSENT from the trigger entry, never fabricated, never substituted with the snapshot value. No new external API call -- this reuses the `shadow_history` table Stage 1 already reads.

**Honesty addendum (marks basis, not fill-level):** the realized figure captures post-snapshot PRICE DRIFT through the actual rebalance window, NOT fill-level execution slippage -- true fill reconciliation would require new Composer/Alpaca API integration and stays explicitly out of scope (Decisions table, `feature-plans/exit-friction-realized-savings.md`). Every consumer-facing label says "marks basis"/"realized (marks)" -- the dashboard caption is a STATIC string in `templates/index.html`, deliberately never JS-injected, so it cannot be silently dropped by a future JS bug the way a dynamically-rendered label could.

### AC-6/AC-7 -- dual-basis $-saved design, snapshot semantics preserved verbatim

`GET /api/guard-alpha-summary` now returns BOTH `cumulative_saved_dollars` (unchanged snapshot-basis math -- `DE-GUARD-ALPHA-SAVED-001` semantics preserved byte-for-byte, zero diff to that code path) and the new `saved_dollars_realized` + `realized_coverage: {with_data, total}`. Coverage accounting (AC-7): an entry missing realized data is EXCLUDED from the realized sum, COUNTED in `total`, never counted in `with_data`, never silently substituted with the snapshot value -- `realized_coverage.with_data === 0` renders "no realized data yet" on the dashboard, never a bare $0.00 (a real-looking zero would misrepresent "we have no data" as "we measured zero"). This dual-basis design was a deliberate PM decision (Decisions table): the snapshot basis has shipped semantics operators already trust; dual display is honest and preserves comparability rather than silently redefining what $-saved means.

### AC-8 -- Ruling C: turnover `coverage_days` honesty + operator knobs (ga2-tw pre-RED recon)

`database.get_exit_turnover_stats` reports per-symphony exit counts over trailing 30/90/365-day windows from `exit_triggers`. The plan's original wording risked a bare 365-day count implying a full year of coverage. ga2-tw's recon flagged that `exit_triggers` is pruned daily via `prune_old_triggers`/`TRIGGER_TELEMETRY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 90 days, `app.py:788`, operator-configurable) -- the 365-day window cannot structurally back a true year of history under the default retention setting. PM ruled every window carries an honest `coverage_days` field (`min(window, actual_retained_days)`) alongside its count, and the UI renders both together (`static/performance.js`'s `turnoverWindowCell`: `"N (Xd retained)"`, never a bare count under a "365d" header).

**This is OPERATOR KNOB #2**, alongside `SHADOW_HISTORY_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 180, `app.py:793`) which gates the Kaminski-Lo stop-justification precondition sample size (`N_MIN_OBS=40`, `DE-GUARD-ALPHA-PRECONDITIONS-001`) -- both retention knobs belong on the operator's radar as one decision surface, not two unrelated settings. `compute_est_annual_friction_drag_pct` scales the 365-day window's `exit_count` by `365 / coverage_days` to correct for retention-capped under-counting, returning `0.0` (never dividing by zero) when `coverage_days` is 0.

**Exit-leg-only (documented limitation, not a bug):** `exit_triggers` only ever records exit events; re-entry is implicit in Composer's daily rebalance and not discretely logged. Inferring round-trips from `bot_state["triggered"]` state transitions is explicitly deferred (Scope Boundaries) -- a candidate follow-on if the exit-leg-only estimate proves materially different from true round-trip turnover.

## DE-INCUBATION-GATE-001 — Strategy Incubation Gate: forward paper-tracking ledger between the backtest gate and operator recommendation (2026-07-25)

Branch: `feat/strategy-incubation-gate` | Base: `a91718ea` (#113) | HEAD (docs-pass): `386b3f0a`

### Summary

Closes recommendation 3 of `docs/research/methodology-validation-2026-07.md` (the R&D methodology external-validation report, § 4) — the third and final graduated gate in the confidence program. Before this cycle, a Strategy Builder candidate that cleared the Harvey-Liu BHY FDR + PBO + SPY-OOS backtest gate (`advisors/backtest_gate_engine.py`) surfaced immediately as an operator recommendation. That gate is entirely retrospective, and the candidate tree itself is LLM-generated (`advisors/build_plan_generator.py`) — a structural risk no backtest-only gate can rule out: the model may be pattern-matching training-era market history rather than discovering genuine edge. This cycle adds a mandatory forward-tracking stage: every gate-survivor is registered into a new ledger as `INCUBATING` and tracked on real forward daily returns (paper — zero capital, zero execution) for a minimum window; only candidates that clear an honest forward bar against SPY are `PROMOTED` to recommendation status. Advisory-only end to end; zero live-execution surface; zero change to the 1-minute engine decision path (structurally enforced blast-radius guard, `tests/advisors/test_incubation_blast_radius.py`).

New module `advisors/incubation.py`; new migration 037 (`strategy_incubation` + `incubation_daily` tables, additive-only); Step 4b wired into `advisors/strategy_builder_engine.propose_strategies`; new read-only `GET /api/incubation`; a 03:30 daily off-hours tick; a 4-state status chip on the Strategy Builder tab. See `docs/generated/advisors_incubation.md`, `docs/generated/database.md`, `docs/generated/app.md`, `docs/generated/static_ai_advisor_js.md`, `docs/generated/advisors_strategy_builder_engine.md`, and `docs/generated/advisors_strategy_builder_scheduler.md` for the full technical record; this entry records the design rulings and their provenance.

Team: `ga3-tw` (test-writer/coordinator), `ga3-db` (database), `ga3-adv` (advisors engine), `ga3-flask`/`ga3-flask2` (dashboard — see "Team composition note" below), `ga3-rev` (reviewer), `ga3-doc` (this doc-writer). PM (main session) is team lead.

### Named constants — all operator knobs, `[PM-ASSUMED]`, never Optuna/advisor-tunable

| Constant | Value | Home | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `INCUBATION_WINDOW_TRADING_DAYS` | `63` | `advisors/incubation.py` | Minimum forward trading days observed before promotion is possible (~3 months). The methodology-validation report cites ≥ 6-month allocator practice for genuine out-of-sample incubation; 63 trading days is the named, trivially-raised retail-pragmatic floor that still delivers a memorization-free signal — not a claim that 3 months matches institutional practice. |
| `INCUBATION_MDD_BREACH_MULT` | `1.5` | `advisors/incubation.py` | Forward max-drawdown (positive pct magnitude) must stay ≤ this × the candidate's stored backtest MDD before an early fail fires, at ANY day count — a candidate does not need to wait out the full window to fail on a genuine drawdown blowup. |
| `INCUBATION_MAX_FETCH_FAILURES` | `5` | `advisors/incubation.py` | Consecutive daily-tick Composer fetch failures for one candidate before `EXPIRED`. |
| `MAX_INCUBATING` | `20` | `database.py` | Cap on concurrently-`INCUBATING` rows. Beyond the cap, the lowest-gate-time-`oos_alpha` candidates are not admitted (caller sorts descending before calling `admit_candidate`), logged honestly, never silently dropped. |
| `INCUBATION_REFRACTORY_DAYS` | `90` | `database.py` | A `FAILED`/`EXPIRED` candidate hash cannot be re-admitted for this many days — prevents re-generation from laundering a candidate past its own history. |

**Layering rule behind the constant split (a cross-cycle principle, not incubation-specific):** `database.py` never imports FROM `advisors.*`. Because `register_incubation_candidate`'s cap-and-refractory enforcement runs inside `database.py`, its two constants live there; the other three (tick/promotion-only) live in `advisors/incubation.py`. Caught during recon before any RED test was written — the original handoff draft had placed all five constants in `advisors/incubation.py`, which would have made `database.py` either duplicate them or reach up into `advisors.*` to read them, a backwards-layering violation. Same house convention as `math_engine.py`'s no-magic-numbers rule, applied cross-module for the first time this cycle.

### The memorization-free rationale (AC-8)

Forward data collected after a candidate's admission timestamp did not exist yet when the generating LLM's training data was assembled — it post-dates the model's training cutoff **by construction**. This makes the promotion decision in `evaluate_promotion()` the first signal anywhere in the Strategy Builder pipeline that cannot be explained by the model having memorized or pattern-matched the evaluation data; a candidate can look arbitrarily good on its backtest and still fail here. The rationale is documented as a comment at the promotion-decision code site (`advisors/incubation.py`, `evaluate_promotion`'s "AC-8 lookahead-bias rationale" comment, immediately above the `alpha = candidate_cum - spy_cum` computation) per the plan's explicit requirement, and cites `docs/research/methodology-validation-2026-07.md`'s parametric-lookahead finding.

### Bill-bounding and idempotency

**Bill-bounded:** ≤ `MAX_INCUBATING + 1` Composer calls per daily tick (one shared SPY-benchmark call plus one call per `INCUBATING` candidate, bounded because `get_incubating()`'s result set is itself capped at `MAX_INCUBATING`). An empty ledger makes **zero** Composer calls, not even the shared SPY call.

**Idempotency (admission):** a re-generated identical tree while `INCUBATING`/`PROMOTED` is a permanent no-op, clock never resets (`reason="already_tracked"`); `FAILED`/`EXPIRED` within the refractory window is refused (`reason="refractory_window"`); past the window, re-admission is a cap-checked UPDATE-in-place with a genuinely reset clock (`reason="refractory_reentry"`). `EXPIRED` is treated identically to `FAILED` for the refractory window — a `ga3-tw` coordination decision, not verbatim in the plan text: both represent "this hash didn't make it," and the refractory rule's stated purpose applies equally to either.

**Idempotency (daily tick) — promoted by review to a hard, structural requirement.** `ga3-rev`'s review flagged that the tick's own loop-selection logic ("only append dates strictly after the last recorded `trading_day`") is not, by itself, a sufficient duplicate-prevention guarantee — an out-of-order response reprocess or a full-history resend after a restart could still double-insert if that application-level logic were ever wrong. The PM promoted this to a hard requirement: `incubation_daily`'s `UNIQUE(candidate_hash, trading_day)` constraint plus `append_incubation_day`'s `INSERT OR IGNORE` write must guarantee zero duplicates at the DB layer regardless of loop-selection correctness. Pinned by a dedicated RED test (`tests/advisors/test_incubation_tick.py::TestNormalTick::test_rerunning_the_same_tick_response_twice_inserts_zero_duplicates`), which calls `run_incubation_tick()` twice against the identical mock response and asserts `days_observed` is unchanged after the second call.

### The five `ga3-tw` recon findings + the AC-5 amendment (credited, PM-ruled ACCEPTED before any RED test was written)

The original plan text (`feature-plans/strategy-incubation-gate.md`, first commit `f3f208c7`) contained five items `ga3-tw` flagged during pre-RED recon, plus one additional finding of its own (AC-5's badge-honesty gap). All six were ruled ACCEPTED by the PM and frozen into `.claude/tdd-handoff.md` before implementation began — none of this lives only in chat.

**(a) Daemon scheduling slot, confirmed at 03:30.** The plan's original text left the daily-tick scheduling slot as `[PM-ASSUMED — recon decides]`. Recon confirmed `app.py`'s `run_scheduler()` already runs `_run_lens_pipeline()` at 03:00; the incubation tick registers at **03:30**, staggered by 30 minutes so the two off-hours jobs never contend for the same minute, via the identical CC-2 lazy-import-inside-a-daemon-thread wrapper pattern `_run_lens_pipeline`/`_lens_pipeline_worker` already establish. No standalone systemd timer.

**(b) Single admission wiring seam, not two — closes a genuine double-admission risk.** The plan's original architecture text described the admission adapter as "called from `strategy_builder_engine.propose_strategies` persistence path + the weekly scheduler," which reads as two separate wiring points. Since the weekly scheduler (`advisors/strategy_builder_scheduler.py`) itself calls `propose_strategies`, wiring admission at both sites would have double-admitted every scheduler-sourced survivor — once via the scheduler's own call, once via `propose_strategies`'s internal one. `ga3-tw`'s recon caught this before any RED test was written; the PM ruled a single wiring seam inside `propose_strategies`'s existing Step-5 survivor-persist loop (documented as "Step 4b" in `docs/generated/advisors_strategy_builder_engine.md`), with a source-guard RED test (`tests/advisors/test_incubation_admission.py`) asserting `admit_candidate`/`register_incubation_candidate` are referenced from exactly one production call site.

**(c) AC-3 corrected — Composer has no windowed backtest API.** The plan's original text described the daily tick as fetching "the day's new segment" via a windowed `run_backtest` call. Recon found `composer_backtest_client.run_backtest()` takes no start/end date parameter at all — every call returns the candidate's FULL-history `daily_returns` series. The corrected design: each tick re-fetches the full-history response for every `INCUBATING` candidate and extracts every ISO date key strictly after that candidate's most-recently-recorded `trading_day`, filtered through `market_calendar.is_trading_day`. This is not a workaround — it is what makes daemon-down gap catch-up free at zero extra Composer-call cost (a daemon down for N days simply yields N new date keys in the next tick's one response) while staying within the original ≤ `MAX_INCUBATING + 1` calls/tick bill bound.

**(d) Migration numbering + test-file naming convention** — approved as proposed (`migrations/037_strategy_incubation.sql`, `tests/database/test_037_strategy_incubation.py`, matching house convention).

**(e) Day-zero admissible survivors from pre-existing `advisor_observations` rows — ruled moot.** Backfilling forward data for pre-feature survivors is explicitly OUT of scope (Scope Boundaries); the PM's live functional gate probes real post-deploy admission instead of a backfill.

**AC-5 amendment (`ga3-tw`'s own additional finding, not in the original five) — the entry's best honest-design exhibit.** The plan's original AC-5 text called for the weekly scheduler's persisted advisory observations to gain "an additive `incubation_status` field." Recon found this cannot work: `advisor_observations` rows are append-only/immutable (no update/delete accessor exists at all — `database.py`'s own docstring states this design invariant). A status value frozen into `raw_response` at persist time would always read the admission-moment value — a candidate promoted or failed weeks later would still display `INCUBATING` on its original observation forever, an honest-looking badge that would in fact be lying. The corrected design, ruled by the PM before any RED test existed: `_persist_survivor` gains exactly ONE new additive key, `"candidate_hash"` (immutable, always correct — the same additive-blob precedent as the shipped `run_id`/`invocation_source`/`evidence_injected` keys). Status is instead computed LIVE, at render/API time, by joining that `candidate_hash` against the incubation ledger (`database.get_incubation_overview()`) — both `GET /api/incubation` and `app.py`'s `ai_advisor_tab()` badge stamping share one `_incubation_badge()` helper so wording never drifts between the two render sites. This is the structural reason incubation status can never silently go stale on the dashboard: there is no frozen field to go stale in the first place.

### Two same-cycle schema-gap addenda, found by the implementer, PM-ruled

Both landed as additive migration-037 amendments (never a new migration 038 — "037 amended in place" was an explicit PM ruling, since neither addendum shipped to any environment between the original 037 commit and these follow-ups).

**Fetch-failure counter (`fetch_failure_count` column + `record_incubation_fetch_outcome` accessor).** `ga3-adv` found while starting GREEN that the handoff's original policy — "derive the consecutive-fetch-failure count from `incubation_daily` gaps" — does not actually work: a genuine fetch failure produces ZERO `incubation_daily` rows for that tick, so there is no data trail to derive a count from. `ga3-tw`'s same-day first-pass ruling added a raw column (`consecutive_fetch_failures`, no new accessor, direct SQL from `advisors/incubation.py` via `database.get_connection()`). The PM overruled this same day: state-DB writes go through named `database.py` accessors, never raw SQL from a caller module — the same layering principle already established by the constants split above. Final design: `fetch_failure_count` column + a new `record_incubation_fetch_outcome(candidate_hash, ok) -> int` accessor (the only sanctioned writer of that column), returning the resulting count so the caller can compare it against `INCUBATION_MAX_FETCH_FAILURES` in the same call. A dedicated RED test simulated a process restart (module eviction from `sys.modules` + re-import between tick calls) specifically to catch an in-memory-only implementation, which would have passed a same-process test while silently resetting on every real `app.py` restart.

**`get_incubation_daily_series` accessor.** `ga3-adv` found a second real gap while implementing `run_incubation_tick()`: none of the originally-pinned accessors return the actual ordered `incubation_daily` values a candidate needs — `get_incubation_overview()` only provides a `days_observed` COUNT, and `evaluate_promotion()` (a deliberately pure, DB-free function) cannot run without the real per-day series. `ga3-adv` proposed a named accessor from the start this time (having learned from the PM's raw-SQL correction above) — `get_incubation_daily_series(candidate_hash) -> tuple[list[float], list[float | None]]`, shaped to drop directly into `evaluate_promotion`'s first two positional args. Ruled ACCEPTED as proposed, architecturally consistent, non-controversial.

### `ga3-rev`'s review-promoted findings (hard requirements before implementation, not optional suggestions)

Beyond the structural tick-idempotency requirement above, `ga3-rev`'s review promoted two more findings to hard RED-test requirements: (1) a **non-tautological** `candidate_hash` correctness test — the cross-module equality check (`incubation.candidate_hash(t) == community_strats._composition_hash(t)`) is satisfied trivially if `candidate_hash()` simply delegates to `community_strats._composition_hash()`, which is exactly what was recommended; a second, independent test (`test_candidate_hash_matches_an_independently_computed_reference_value`) recomputes the expected hash inline using only stdlib `json`/`hashlib` (no import of `community_strats` at all), proving the underlying algorithm itself is correct, not merely that two functions happen to agree; (2) a no-stale-caching route test (`TestIncubationRouteNoStaleCaching::test_status_change_between_two_requests_is_reflected_on_the_second`) — two `GET /api/incubation` requests with a real `set_incubation_status` transition in between must return different values, closing off any future temptation to memoize the route.

### A genuine floating-point bug found and fixed during implementation

`ga3-adv` found a real boundary bug while implementing `evaluate_promotion`'s MDD-breach comparison: quantstats' `max_drawdown` is pandas/numpy float64 arithmetic that can land a fraction of a ULP away from an exact decimal boundary (empirically ~1.8e-15 off a -15.0%-exactly scenario), which without a tolerance could spuriously trip the strict `>` breach comparison on a mathematically-exact non-breach. Fixed with `_MDD_BREACH_EPSILON = 1e-9` — the identical value and rationale as the shipped `guard_preconditions.py`'s `_BOUNDARY_EPS` precedent (`DE-GUARD-ALPHA-PRECONDITIONS-001`), applied only on the non-breach side of the comparison so it can never mask a genuine breach.

### WIRE1-3 test-fixture bug (two root causes, `ga3-tw` fix, zero production code touched)

`ga3-adv` reported all three `TestAdmissionWiringEndToEnd` tests failing with `screened_survivors=[]`, `rejection_reason='below_spy_alpha'` against their real, already-committed implementation. `ga3-tw` root-caused this to two independent test-fixture defects in its own test file (routed per the house "root cause determines the role" convention — this was never an engine bug):

1. The fixture's mock `run_backtest` router returned the byte-identical fake series for EVERY call, including `propose_strategies`'s own internal SPY-benchmark call (Step 2a) — producing an exact `oos_alpha` tie, and the gate's non-strict `<=` comparison classifies a tie as NOT beating SPY. Fixed via tree-name dispatch (mirroring `test_incubation_tick.py`'s existing `_run_backtest_router` pattern): the SPY-benchmark tree now gets a clearly worse series, the candidate a clearly better one.
2. Fixing (1) alone still failed, now on `rejection_reason='fdr_not_winner'` with `winner_p_adj=0.5` (the "empty validation fold" sentinel) — an all-positive return series has zero down-days, which breaks the Sortino t-statistic the BHY/FDR gate scores on regardless of how large `oos_alpha` is. Fixed by switching both series to a mixed-sign factor cycle (~80% up-days) with strongly separated net drift.

All 9 tests in the file verified passing against `ga3-adv`'s unmodified, already-committed implementation once both fixture defects were corrected — no rework requested of `ga3-adv`.

### The WIRE3 vacuity finding and the unconditional non-vacuity standard

`ga3-tw` initially argued the WIRE3 fix (`3fe8c460`, an `assert mock_register.called` addition) was "mechanically obvious, no rerun needed." The PM rejected this: WIRE3's ORIGINAL form also looked obviously correct by direct reasoning, and only empirical execution had exposed it as vacuous — the standard for proving a test can genuinely fail is unconditional, not effort-weighted or reasoning-exempted. `ga3-tw` then did the required construction: a detached scratch worktree at `3fe8c460`, with `advisors/strategy_builder_engine.py` checked out back to its pre-wiring state (`32eaa486`, confirmed via grep: 0 hits for `candidate_hash`/`admit_candidate`/`register_incubation_candidate` vs 11 before the checkout). Ran the full `TestAdmissionWiringEndToEnd` class there: WIRE3 failed exactly on the intended assertion (register was never called); WIRE1/WIRE2 also failed, on their own real behavioral assertions (not `ModuleNotFoundError`, since `advisors/incubation.py` genuinely exists in that scratch state) — confirming all three tests depend on the actual Step-5 wiring, not merely the module's existence. This closed the cycle's third and final vacuity instance (alongside the `ecedeecb` born-green batch, verified non-vacuous the same way against a separate scratch worktree at `ecedeecb`, and the WIRE1-3 fixture bug above) — the general lesson (unconditional non-vacuity, "obvious by reasoning" is never an exemption) is now a standing project practice, not a one-off.

### Shared-worktree provenance note (`d214c7f4`)

`ga3-adv`'s task #41 commit (`d214c7f4`, engine + Step-5 admission wiring + daily tick) additionally carries `ga3-flask`'s final `/api/incubation` route + `_incubation_badge` + `ai_advisor_tab()` stamping hunks (task #42) inside the same `app.py` diff — a shared-file union, not intentional scope creep. Both lanes had uncommitted, intermixed edits in the same shared worktree file; `ga3-adv` checked `git status`/`git diff --cached --stat` (file-level) before committing but not per-hunk content, and did not realize the file carried both lanes' work until the PM's coordination message (requiring a joint pre-commit confirmation for any shared-file union commit going forward) arrived after the commit was already made. Verified no functional harm: `tests/app/test_incubation_route.py` (13/13) passed against the committed state, and `ga3-flask` confirmed their edits landed as intended; `ga3-adv` messaged `ga3-flask` directly so no duplicate/conflicting `app.py` commit was attempted. This incident is the origin of a new standing shared-worktree rule (recorded in the PM's operating ledger): content-level `git diff --cached -- <file>` plus explicit cross-lane final-confirmation is now required for any file more than one lane touches — a file-level stat check is structurally blind to interleaved hunks.

### Team composition note — `ga3-flask` / `ga3-flask2`

The dashboard lane's task #42 work (the `GET /api/incubation` route, `_incubation_badge()`, `ai_advisor_tab()` stamping, `templates/ai_advisor.html`'s chip CSS/markup, and `static/ai_advisor.js`'s `refreshIncubationChips()`) was authored by the `ga3-flask` teammate, as recorded in `ga3-flask`'s own status-log entry in `.claude/tdd-handoff.md` (23/23 tests passing, ruff clean). `ga3-flask` was subsequently rescinded from the team roster before it committed its own remaining exclusive files (`templates/ai_advisor.html` + `static/ai_advisor.js`, the portion not already captured inside `d214c7f4`'s shared-file union above); a replacement teammate, `ga3-flask2`, verified that authored work and committed it as `386b3f0a` (`"task #42 exclusive files (authored by ga3-flask lane, verified+committed by ga3-flask2)"`). No functional rework was needed — `ga3-flask2`'s role was verification and commit of already-authored, already-tested work, not re-implementation. This doc-writer did not independently observe the reason for `ga3-flask`'s rescission; it is recorded here only as verified commit provenance, not as an incident root-cause account.

### Frontrunner Builder queuing is unaffected

`strategy_builder_engine._persist_survivor`'s pre-existing, unconditional `insert_frontrunner_proposal` call (the AC-10 retrofit, `DE-FRONTRUNNER-001`) still fires for every non-rejected candidate regardless of incubation status. This cycle changed neither the Frontrunner Builder's separate operator-approval-to-Composer-create queue nor its trigger condition — Step 4b only gates the Strategy Builder tab's own recommendation badge. The two surfaces (incubation ledger, Frontrunner Builder proposal queue) are independent by design.

### `ga3-rev`'s post-GREEN review — Findings 1 and 2 (fixed, `250f044a` / `210b62fc` / `7173d269`)

`ga3-rev`'s independent 8-gate review of the completed GREEN implementation (against merge-base `a91718ea`) found two findings, both routed back through the Toxic Pair and fixed before this doc-writer's finalization pass:

**Finding 2 — non-tunability regression trio (`250f044a`).** The five incubation constants (`MAX_INCUBATING`, `INCUBATION_REFRACTORY_DAYS`, `INCUBATION_WINDOW_TRADING_DAYS`, `INCUBATION_MDD_BREACH_MULT`, `INCUBATION_MAX_FETCH_FAILURES`) had no standing regression guard proving they stay non-tunable — the plan's own "never Optuna/advisor-tunable" requirement was documented but not tested. `ga3-tw` added `tests/advisors/test_incubation_constants_non_tunable.py` (7 tests), mirroring the existing `tests/autotuner/test_exit_friction_constant.py::AC-3` pattern exactly: each constant is asserted absent from `OPTUNA_SEARCH_SPACE_KEYS`, absent from the AI Advisor's suggestible allowlist, and never read from a per-trial params dict or the environment. Non-vacuity was independently demonstrated (not merely asserted): the AST/string dict-and-env-access scan was run against a temporary source copy with a violation deliberately planted into it, proving the scan mechanism can actually catch a real violation rather than trivially finding nothing on already-clean source.

**Finding 1 — MDD-baseline coercion, initially reported, then reachability-falsified and re-graded (`210b62fc` RED, `7173d269` GREEN).** The original Step 4b code coerced a `None` backtest `max_drawdown` to a `0.0` baseline, with an inline comment calling this "a conservative choice." `ga3-rev` correctly flagged this as backwards: a `0.0` baseline is not conservative, it fabricates a result — `evaluate_promotion`'s early-fail check would trip an `mdd_breach` verdict the first time the candidate showed ANY nonzero forward drawdown, misreporting missing data as a risk-exceeded finding rather than "erring safe." Before writing the fix, `ga3-tw` performed adversarial reachability verification and found the finding's real-world severity was substantially lower than "reported" framing implied: a candidate whose `info.metrics["max_drawdown"]` is `None` **cannot reach Step 4b at all** via the real `propose_strategies()` call path today — `_passes_screens` already fails closed on any `None` metric earlier in the pipeline, unconditionally, independently confirmed GREEN by the pre-existing `tests/advisors/test_strategy_builder_engine.py::TestAdversarialCycle3::test_passes_screens_returns_false_when_max_drawdown_is_none`. The finding is real (the coercion logic was genuinely wrong) but was **never a live production bug** — it was unreachable dead code under the current call graph.

**Fixed shape, per the PM's ruling on severity wording (binding for every doc surface, including CLAUDE.md):** `ga3-adv` extracted a pure seam, `_resolve_admission_mdd_baseline(raw_mdd: float | None) -> float | None` (`advisors/strategy_builder_engine.py`) — `None` in returns `None` (a decline-admission signal), a real value converts via the unchanged `abs(raw_mdd) * 100.0`. Step 4b now declines admission entirely (logs the reason, never calls `admit_candidate`) when the seam returns `None`, with an honest source comment documenting the reachability finding so no future reader infers a live bug from the fix's mere existence. `evaluate_promotion` is byte-unchanged. **The correct, mandatory severity characterization for this fix, everywhere it is described, is "defensive-code correctness, unreachable under current call graph, second-layer defense" — never "declined admission closes a live bug" or any wording implying a real production gap existed.** See `docs/generated/advisors_strategy_builder_engine.md`'s `_resolve_admission_mdd_baseline` section and `docs/generated/advisors_incubation.md`'s admission section (both reconciled to this same wording in this doc-writer's finalization pass) for the full technical account.

## DE-HYGIENE-R1-001 -- Guard-Alpha-preconditions phantom-key filter + synthetic_history cache-miss log honesty (2026-07-25)

**Problem.** Two small, independently-found hygiene defects in EXISTING codepaths, both surfaced during the PM's live probing of the guard-alpha-preconditions feature on 2026-07-24 (`DE-GUARD-ALPHA-PRECONDITIONS-001`):

(a) `GET /api/guard-alpha-preconditions` (`app.py::guard_alpha_preconditions()`) iterated every top-level key of `bot_state` as if it were a symphony. `bot_state`'s top level actually mixes real per-symphony sub-dicts with 5 portfolio-level metadata keys (`date`, `last_execution_mode`, `last_market_close_snapshot`, `last_successful_cycle_at`, `post_mortem_run`), so all 5 rendered as phantom `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` "symphony" rows -- 16 served on the droplet against 11 real symphonies.

(b) `synthetic_history.get_cached_synthetic_history_only`'s bounded 10-trading-day backward cache-probe walk (`AUTOTUNE_CACHE_MAX_AGE_TRADING_DAYS=10`, see `DE-GUARD-ALPHA-PRECONDITIONS-001` R2) called `load_cached_history` unconditionally for every candidate date, which raises `FileNotFoundError` internally and logs a per-file `WARNING "corrupt or unreadable cache file"` on a plain missing file -- the EXPECTED case under the weekly autotune cache cadence, not a corruption signal. A single route call could emit up to 11 misleading WARNING lines.

**Fix (a) -- structural discriminator, not a name denylist (AC-2).** New `app.py::_is_symphony_state_entry(value) -> bool` = `isinstance(value, dict) and "name" in value` (`app.py:3114`) -- the SAME structural shape check already used at 7 other `app.py` call sites (`app.py:1205, 1214, 1320, 1363, 1504, 2760, 3012`), reused rather than reinvented. Every real symphony entry is unconditionally stamped with `"name"` each cycle by the engine (`alpha_bot_execution.py:1633`) as soon as it is created; no top-level metadata value (plain `str`/`bool` scalars, or the differently-shaped `last_market_close_snapshot` dict) ever carries that key. Wired at the route's single iteration site (`app.py:3218`, `for sym_id, sym_data in bot_state_dict.items():` with a `continue`-on-exclude guard, replacing a bare `for sym_id in bot_state_dict:`). A future top-level metadata key is excluded automatically without a code change, as long as it isn't itself a dict carrying `"name"` -- the anti-rot property AC-2 required. `guard_preconditions.py`, `alpha_bot_execution.py`, and `math_engine.py` carry zero diff.

**Fix (b) -- miss-vs-corruption log split (AC-5/AC-6).** `synthetic_history.py` gains `_log_cache_miss_summary(missed_dates, current_date_str)` (`synthetic_history.py:548`); `get_cached_synthetic_history_only` (`synthetic_history.py:577`) now checks `os.path.exists(cache_file)` BEFORE calling `load_cached_history` at all -- a missing file is collected into a local `missed_dates` accumulator instead of reaching `load_cached_history`, and never raises. At most ONE aggregate `logging.info` line is emitted per call (on a hit, or on walk-back exhaustion), naming the miss count and date range and stating explicitly that it is "expected under the weekly cache cadence, not an anomaly." `load_cached_history` itself is byte-unchanged -- it is only ever called for a candidate whose file already exists on disk, so its existing per-file WARNING path/wording still fires verbatim (and unmodified) for a genuinely corrupt/unreadable file, and its OTHER caller (`generate_synthetic_history`) is unaffected by construction (this fix touches only `get_cached_synthetic_history_only`'s own call site). Walk-back depth, candidate date stepping (via `market_calendar.is_trading_day`), and every return value are unchanged.

**Both are hygiene fixes to existing codepaths, not new codepaths -- no TDD Toxic Pair required** (project CLAUDE.md exception class), but both behavior changes are pinned by tests ahead of implementation (RED-then-GREEN, `a6aaa7ed` -> `ef81c55a`/`39147312`) and the full PR gate (`/review`, PM live functional test, CI, merge-to-origin) still applies per the Merge & PR Workflow hard requirement -- this decision entry does not itself constitute that gate passing.

**Edge cases confirmed (per the plan's Edge Cases section):**
- A `bot_state` blob containing ONLY the 5 metadata keys renders the route's existing honest empty state (`{"symphonies": {}}`, HTTP 200) -- AC-4, never an error.
- A real-but-thin symphony sub-dict that still carries `"name"` (degenerate/missing sub-data) still passes the discriminator and appears with its existing honest degraded verdicts -- AC-3, no-self-regression; the filter only ever excludes, never additionally degrades, a real entry.
- Day-0 cache hit in the backward walk emits zero miss lines (`missed_dates` stays empty, `_log_cache_miss_summary` no-ops).
- A mixed walk-back (some days miss, an older day hits) still emits at most one aggregate summary, and the hit's return value is unaffected.
- A file that exists but fails to parse mid-walk-back still produces the pre-existing per-file WARNING, with the walk-back continuing past it exactly as before.

**Test coverage.** `tests/app/test_guard_alpha_preconditions_route.py` (extended) -- phantom-key exclusion (AC-1), metadata-only honest empty state (AC-4), degenerate-real-symphony no-self-regression (AC-3), and a novel-metadata-key anti-rot proof that a name-denylist implementation would fail (AC-2), plus a unit-test class for `_is_symphony_state_entry` directly. `tests/synthetic_history/test_autotune_cache_backward_probe.py` (extended) -- caplog-based classification: all-miss and mixed-miss-then-hit walk-backs collapse to at most one INFO "miss" record instead of one-per-candidate WARNING "corrupt" record; day-0 hit and genuine mid-walkback corruption (file exists, unparseable) are pinned as regression guards for behavior the fix must not disturb. `a6aaa7ed`'s own non-vacuity verification: 18 of the 20 new tests failed for a clean reason against pre-fix HEAD (`AttributeError` on the not-yet-implemented helper, or the literal pre-fix behavior -- e.g. 11 WARNING records instead of <=1 on an all-miss walk-back); the other 2 are intentional pass-now regression guards for behavior the fix must not disturb.

**Fresh authoritative test count (this doc-writer's own run, not a propagated tally), HEAD `39147312`:** `python -m pytest -n0` targeting both cycle test files directly -- **38 passed / 0 failed / 0 errors**. `hc-tw`'s task-48 sufficiency pass completed with no separate commit or numeric report to cite; this doc-writer's own fresh run is therefore the authoritative count for this entry, per house convention (mirroring `DE-INCUBATION-GATE-001`'s "fresh authoritative recount" precedent above).

**Reference:** `feature-plans/preconditions-phantom-keys-and-cache-log-noise.md`; branch `fix/route-phantom-keys-log-noise`; worktree `.claude/worktrees/hygiene-cycle`. Commit chain: `daea9b8d` (plan) -> `a6aaa7ed` (RED, both test files, `hc-tw`) -> `ef81c55a` (GREEN, `synthetic_history.py`, `hc-sh`) -> `39147312` (GREEN, `app.py`, `hc-flask`) -> docs finalization (`hc-doc`, this entry). The PM's live functional gate (merge workflow step 4, per house convention re-running the K-L probe -- expect `symphony_count` to drop 16 -> 11 with the 5 phantoms gone and all real verdicts byte-identical) has not yet run as of this entry; a subsequent PR/merge record carries that outcome.

## DE-GAS-COHERENCE-001 — Guard-Alpha $-Saved Display Coherence: Sign Convention + Windowing (2026-07-29)

**Operator-locked convention:** every guard-alpha/P&L dollar figure in the app renders the **ABS magnitude with NO sign character** (not even a redundant `+` on a winning figure) — direction is conveyed by COLOR plus a trailing WORD instead (the positive word, default `"saved"`, for `value >= 0` including exactly `0.0`; the negative word, default `"lost"`, for `value < 0`). Separately: **"same range" must mean "same number."** For a shared nominal window token (e.g. "1Y"), every surface computing a $-saved figure over that window must resolve to the identical day-count and therefore a byte-comparable number — and every windowed surface must disclose which window backs the figure on screen.

### Why this shipped

Nine concrete defects were found across the dashboard, History tab, and Discord/QuickChart producer surfaces, all sharing one of two root causes:

1. **No shared dollar-formatting implementation existed anywhere.** Every surface (the dashboard $-saved panel, History's hero/by-reason cards, the Managed Sleeves EOD digest, the Discord EOD embed) hand-rolled its own sign handling — which is why the SAME bug (a forced/naked sign character rendered under an unconditional "saved"/"Total Saved" label, e.g. `"Total Saved: $-50.00"`) was independently present in at least five places, plus a sixth defect class where a figure was colored green (`--studio-pos`) UNCONDITIONALLY regardless of its actual sign (History's `val-total-saved`), and a seventh where a signed guard-alpha percentage (History's Detail column) was colored neutral gray regardless of sign, and an eighth where a chart's per-day bars all shared one hardcoded color regardless of that day's sign (QuickChart's "Daily Saved ($)" dataset).
2. **The dashboard's $-saved panel (`GET /api/guard-alpha-summary`) was ALWAYS the all-time cumulative sum, while History's own $-saved (`analytics.get_history_summary`) was calendar-windowed from the SAME `saved_dollars` field in the SAME `post_mortem_*.json` files** — for a given nominal window there was no shared token and no way to reconcile the two numbers. Compounding this, History's own "1Y"/"5Y" window-picker buttons sent literal calendar-day counts `252`/`1260` (a 252-trading-days/year artifact) while the app-wide `1y` token (`analytics._WINDOW_TRAILING_DAYS["1y"] == 365`) meant 365 calendar days everywhere else — so "1 year" meant two different, unreconcilable spans depending which surface you were on, even before the windowing gap above.

### The fix

**AC-1 (shared Python formatter).** New `analytics.format_dollar_saved(value: float, *, positive_word: str = "saved", negative_word: str = "lost") -> str`:
```python
word = positive_word if value >= 0 else negative_word
return f"${abs(value):,.2f} {word}"
```
The single Python-side source of truth for this convention, keyword-only word params (a positional third argument raises `TypeError`), thousands-separator formatting.

**AC-2 (Python callers route through AC-1).** `reporting.build_sleeves_digest_section`'s `realized_pnl_usd` line (`positive_word="gain"`, `negative_word="loss"` — a generic per-rule realized P&L figure, not a guard-alpha savings figure, hence the different word pair; the pre-existing `None`/non-numeric → `"n/a"` degrade is unchanged) and `reporting.send_eod_discord_post`'s Discord "Total Saved" embed line (default words; the label itself shortened from "Total Saved:" to "Total:" since the rendered value already carries "saved"/"lost") both now call `analytics.format_dollar_saved` instead of a hand-rolled `f"...{:+,.2f}"` format spec.

**AC-3 (QuickChart bar coloring by sign).** The "Daily Saved ($)" dataset's `backgroundColor` is now a per-index list (`"#10b981"` emerald for `v >= 0`, `"#f43f5e"` rose for `v < 0`) parallel to `data`, replacing a single hardcoded `"rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.5)"` amber string applied to every bar regardless of that day's sign.

**AC-4/AC-5 (windowed `GET /api/guard-alpha-summary` + byte-parity).** The route gains an optional `?window=<token>` query param using the SAME token vocabulary `/api/strip/<window>` accepts (`_STRIP_WINDOW_TOKENS`), resolved via the SAME `analytics._window_cutoff_date` the strip route already uses — never a new cutoff scheme. Each `post_mortem_<date>.json` file's embedded date is compared against the resolved cutoff BEFORE its triggers are folded into the sum, so an out-of-window file is excluded entirely (not just its dollar contribution — its dates never enter `date_range` either). Response gains `window` (echoes the resolved token, mirroring `/api/strip/<window>`'s own echo-back pattern) and a `date_range` that brackets ONLY the in-window files' own dates. Omitting `window`, or passing an unrecognized token, resolves to `"all"` — byte-identical to the pre-cycle default (regression guard for existing all-time callers, e.g. the Discord aggregation context). **The byte-parity proof:** for any shared day-count token, this windowed sum equals `analytics.get_history_summary(days=N)["total_saved"]` computed over the identical post-mortem files, to the cent — both routes sum the identical `saved_dollars` field through the identical `is_valid_post_mortem_entry` gate and the identical cutoff arithmetic. This holds AT `1y` specifically only because of the next fix.

**Revise 2 (gas-review sufficiency finding, same day):** the day-1 `exit_triggers` fallback originally gated on the WINDOW-FILTERED `dates` list being empty — but `dates` comes back empty in two genuinely different situations: no post-mortem files exist at all (the true day-1 case), OR real files exist but none fall inside the selected window (every file hit the cutoff `continue` before contributing a date). The second case was wrongly falling through to the day-1 fallback, flipping `source` to `"exit_triggers_intraday"` and `basis_label` to `"no guard events yet"` — dishonestly implying no guard event has EVER occurred when a real one exists just outside the window. Fixed: the day-1 fallback now gates on the UNFILTERED `files` glob, not the window-filtered `dates` list; the window-exists-but-empty case now returns an honest `basis_label="no guard events in this window"` with a zeroed `cumulative_saved_dollars`/`guard_event_count` — extending the byte-parity proof to the zero case (matches `get_history_summary`'s own honest 0.0 on the identical fixture).

**AC-6 (History's 1Y/5Y day-counts corrected).** `templates/history.html`'s "1Y" button now sends `data-window="365"` (was `"252"`) and "5Y" sends `data-window="1825"` (5×365, was `"1260"`, 252×5) — the legacy trading-day-shaped values are removed from both the template and `static/history.js` (no residual literal). **`analytics.get_history_summary`'s own calendar-day arithmetic (`end_date - timedelta(days=days)`) is BYTE-UNCHANGED** — it was always arithmetically identical to `_window_cutoff_date`'s bare-int branch; the divergence lived entirely in the template's mislabeled button VALUES, never in two different date-math implementations. Rewiring `get_history_summary` to call `_window_cutoff_date` was considered and rejected as a no-op refactor carrying real risk to a working function's calling contract for zero behavior gain.

**AC-7/8/9 (History tab sign coherence).** `static/history.js`'s `renderHero()` now colors `val-total-saved` by sign (`--studio-pos`/`--studio-neg`, was hardcoded `--studio-pos` unconditionally) and applies `Math.abs()` to its formatted value (was a naked-minus leak). `renderReasonCards()`'s by-reason dollar caption applies `Math.abs(s.dollars)` and swaps its trailing word `"saved"`/`"lost"` by sign in the SAME string-concatenation expression (was an uncolored, unconditional literal `"saved"` with no abs-magnitude handling, rendering the malformed `"$-500.00 saved"` for a loss). `renderTriggers()`'s Detail column (a signed guard-alpha %) now colors `--studio-pos`/`--studio-neg` by the sign of `rec.detail` (was hardcoded `--studio-ink-dim` regardless of sign).

**AC-10/11 (dashboard panel: verb elements + windowing wiring).** `templates/index.html` gains `#dollar-saved-verb` (snapshot headline) and `#dollar-saved-realized-verb` (realized-basis headline) — dedicated elements so JS can swap `"saved"`/`"lost"` independently of each headline's static "across"/"realized" caption text. `static/index.js`'s `fetchGuardAlphaSummary()` sets each verb element by its own figure's sign and never prepends a literal `-$` for either headline (was `(saved < 0 ? '-$' : '$') + Math.abs(saved).toFixed(2)` under a static, unconditional "saved"/"realized" caption — the exact naked-minus-under-a-saved-label pattern this convention forbids). The function also gained a `windowToken` parameter, included as `window=<token>` in its fetch URL; the existing hero window-picker click handler (which already re-fetches `/api/hero-chart` + the windowed strip) now ALSO calls `fetchGuardAlphaSummary(token)` on the same click, so the $-saved panel re-windows in lockstep with the rest of the hero instead of always showing all-time. `_heroWindow`'s initial value changed from the bare number `30` to the string `'30d'` to match the shape the click handler always assigns.

**AC-12 (no-regression).** Existing all-time-only callers of `GET /api/guard-alpha-summary` keep the all-time sum when `window` is omitted; History's 30/60/90/125/ytd buttons and `get_history_summary`'s calendar-day arithmetic are otherwise byte-unchanged; `analytics._window_cutoff_date` is REUSED, never forked; the actual `saved_dollars`/`realized_pnl_usd` VALUE computations (`reporting.py`) and every PERCENTAGE-figure surface (Avg Guard Alpha, `total_alpha`, the windowed `guard-alpha-headline`) are untouched — the no-naked-sign convention governs DOLLAR figures only, per an explicit team-lead ruling.

**AC-13 (JS contract-identity, no shared JS module — a mid-cycle ruling, not the original plan).** The cycle's original directive called for ONE shared `static/format_saved.js` module consumed by both `index.js` and `history.js`. This was RELAXED by the team lead after the doc-writer flagged a real tension: gas-test's RED tests assert literal tokens (`'lost'`, `Math.abs`) are present INSIDE each calling function's own source-text window (this repo's no-jsdom testing idiom extracts function bodies via brace-matching, not cross-file call graphs) — a shared module would hide those tokens at the call site the tests inspect. **Final ruling:** `index.js` and `history.js` each keep a PER-FILE-LOCAL dollar-format implementation with an IDENTICAL contract (abs magnitude + no sign char + sign-conditional word + sign→color), enforced by the parallel body-extraction tests already committed (`test_dollar_saved_panel_sign_coherence.py` for `index.js`, the `test_cycle_5_history.py` extensions for `history.js`) — no RED rewrite was needed. The DRY invariant for JS is contract-IDENTITY across the two files, proven by parallel tests, not a single shared module; Python keeps ONE shared `analytics.format_dollar_saved` since no such call-site-visibility tension exists there.

### `applyHeroWindow()` token-parsing fix (Revise, same day — NOT deferred, corrected from an earlier draft of this entry)

This cycle's own AC-11 change to `_heroWindow`'s initial value (bare number `30` -> string token `'30d'`) exposed a pre-existing type mismatch in `static/index.js`'s `applyHeroWindow(days)`: its non-`'ytd'` branch did `dates.slice(-days)`, which requires a NUMERIC `days`, but `_heroWindow` (and every value the window-picker click handler assigns to it) has always been a STRING token. `dates.slice(-'30d')` coerced to `dates.slice(NaN)`, which `Array.prototype.slice` treats as `slice(0)` — the FULL array, not the intended window. Because `applyHeroWindow(_heroWindow)` fires on every chart render including the very first, this cycle's own `_heroWindow` fix would have regressed the hero chart's default page-load view from a 30-day window to the entire lifetime history. Caught by gas-test's own sufficiency review (RED at `622da235`) BEFORE merge — never shipped as a live regression. **Fixed (`67b66b7e`):** the branch now parses the `'<N>d'` token shape via `parseInt` (preserving bare-number compatibility), special-cases `'1y'` to `365` (the SAME app-wide `analytics._WINDOW_TRAILING_DAYS['1y']` day-count the server-side AC-2 fix already established — so the hero chart and the windowed $-saved/strip values now agree on `'1y'`'s meaning too), and makes `'all'` an explicit lifetime branch (previously an accidental byproduct of the same NaN-slice bug). `'ytd'` handling is unchanged. See `docs/generated/static_index_js.md`.

### Process note (plan reconciliation)

The doc-writer's first feature-plan draft (`a2ab0805`) scoped the fix to the History tab only, narrower than the operator-locked contract; gas-review correctly held the gate. The plan was reconciled twice: once against the team lead's explicit punch-list (dashboard panel windowing, both `index.js` headlines, a shared formatter — commit `937e5d6e`), and once more against the finalized per-file-local JS ruling above (commit `ee6f726f`) — each revision built directly from gas-test's own committed RED tests as the authoritative contract, not a re-guess from the one-line relay. The reconciled plan also surfaced (confirmed by the team lead as already part of their original scope, not new) three surfaces beyond the initial punch-list: History's Detail-column sign coloring, the Discord "Total Saved" line, and the QuickChart bar coloring.

**Reference:** `feature-plans/guard-alpha-saved-coherence.md` (Status: ready, revised twice); branch `fix/guard-alpha-saved-coherence`; worktree `.claude/worktrees/gas-coherence`. Commit chain: `a2ab0805` (plan draft) → `937e5d6e` (plan reconciled to full contract) → `ee6f726f` (plan: JS-helper shape finalized) → `4268444f` (RED, all 6 test files) → `e4e66186` (GREEN — `analytics.py`, `app.py`, `reporting.py`, `static/history.js`, `static/index.js`, `templates/history.html`, `templates/index.html`) → `dba627fe` (RED, Revise 2 — windowed-empty-fallback sufficiency finding) → `90ab8986` (GREEN, Revise 2 — `app.py`, 11 lines) → docs finalization (this entry).
