### Reconciles a stale claim

`DE-AUDIT-BL9-001`'s `current_return_is_reconstructed` marker was shipped 2026-08-05 documented as having "zero consumers" (by design at the time — a discoverability hardening with no reader yet). This cycle creates the marker's first and, as of this entry, only real consumer (`analytics.get_symphony_today_change`). **[Revise 1 note]** the specific "via the 2 threading sites above" mechanism was superseded by F4's `bot_state_entry`-primary pivot (see "Revise 1" below) — the marker is still consumed by the same function, just resolved differently. See the annotation added to `DE-AUDIT-BL9-001`'s entry above (dated, not rewritten) and the corrected living-doc claim in `docs/generated/alpha_bot_execution.md`.

### Revise 1 (PR #125 review findings, 2026-08-13)

**Trigger.** The Merge & PR Workflow's mandatory `/review` skill gate on PR #125 (the original cycle's PR) returned 14 adjudicated findings (`.claude/pr125-review-findings.json`, F1-F14). Branch frozen, merge held, freeze lifted by the team lead with a scope ruling: F1-F9, F13, F14 fixed in this same PR; F10-F12 tracked for a future cycle. AC-7 (zero diff to `alpha_bot_execution.py`, `math_engine.py`, `reporting.py`) stayed inviolate throughout — none of F1-F14 touch those three files.

**F4 — design pivot (the implementation vehicle for F1/F3/F5(c)).** The original cycle's Option-B design read the reconstruction marker from `sym_dict` only, requiring per-caller opt-in threading — which is exactly how F1 and F3 (below) happened: two of app.py's six hand-built `sym_dict` construction sites were threaded, the other four were not. The revise supersedes this with marker resolution primary-sourced from `bot_state_entry` (a parameter every real call site already passes): if `bot_state_entry` is a `dict` AND `"current_return_is_reconstructed"` is PRESENT in it (a key-presence check, not a truthiness check — an explicit `False` is authoritative and must win over a stale/absent `sym_dict` value; `bot_state_entry.get(...) or sym_dict.get(...)` would be WRONG, since it silently falls through on a real `False`), that value is used; only when `bot_state_entry` is `None`, not a `dict`, or lacks the key does resolution fall back to `sym_dict.get("current_return_is_reconstructed")`. Verified independently against source (not just the commit message): `app.py:1229` (`dashboard()`'s per-card `_tc` build) calls `analytics.get_symphony_today_change(_sym_dict, _s, ...)` where `_s` is the literal loop variable over `bot_state`'s real symphony entries — confirms F3 is fixed by construction. This pivot fixes F1 (`/api/strip`'s `compute_windowed_portfolio_strip` path), F3 (dashboard SSR card), and the frozen per-symphony card loop (F5(c)) with ZERO `app.py` diff at those 3 sites — the marker was already threaded through the existing `bot_state_entry` parameter, just previously ignored. The 2 sites the original cycle DID thread (`_compute_portfolio_strip`'s `symphonies_list` build, `get_state()`'s live-poll card build) are now redundant by construction and were REMOVED — the "Marker threading — 2 sites, not the audit's loosely-cited 4" paragraph above describes the original cycle's shipped design, now superseded; see the correction immediately below and `docs/generated/analytics.md`/`docs/generated/app.md` for the current mechanism.

**F1 (HIGH) — a fifth, never-enumerated consumer.** `GET /api/strip/<window>` (`app.py:3043` → `compute_windowed_portfolio_strip`) builds its own `sym_dict`s from `bot_state`, which the original cycle's audit-derived "four callers" enumeration and this entry's own "2 sites, not 4" analysis both missed — under the original sym_dict-only design, this route never received the marker, so a triggered symphony's Today row would render the corrected Held value on `/api/state` but revert to the reconstructed value (and the ~2x-overstated delta) the moment the operator clicked any hero window button, visibly oscillating on the next poll. Fixed by F4 — `bot_state` is already threaded into this path's `bot_state_entry` parameter.

**[CORRECTION] The "structurally immune" claim about `app.py:2169` is weakened.** The paragraph above states the frozen/closed-market snapshot "can structurally never carry a live mid-day reconstruction" because the EOD reset loop (`alpha_bot_execution.py:1037-1058`) always clears the marker before the snapshot builder (`:1119-1127`/`:1153`) runs. This is TRUE only when both loops iterate the identical symphony set — they do not. The reset loop (`:1037`) iterates `symphony_data_cache` (this cycle's freshly-fetched Composer data); the snapshot builder's symphony list, `symphony_keys_eod` (`:1066`, reused at `:1120`), iterates `[k for k in bot_state if isinstance(bot_state[k], dict)]` — ALL of `bot_state`, independent of whether this cycle's Composer fetch succeeded for that symphony. **Verified directly against source, not just the finding's claim:** a symphony whose Composer fetch fails at the 16:00-16:05 ET EOD run is absent from `symphony_data_cache`, so the reset loop's `if s_id in bot_state:` guard never reaches it (`:1040`) — but `symphony_keys_eod`'s membership test (`isinstance(bot_state[k], dict)`) does not check `symphony_data_cache` at all, so that symphony's STALE `bot_state` entry (potentially still carrying `current_return_is_reconstructed=True` and the reconstructed value from an earlier intraday cycle) is spread verbatim into `_eod_accounts_map` (`:1127`) and written into `last_market_close_snapshot.accounts_map` (`:1153`). This is a real, reachable gap (F5(d)) — not the "structurally never" claim as originally written.

**The render-layer defense that now covers it (F5(d)'s resolution — zero diff to `alpha_bot_execution.py`).** This finding is explicitly render-layer-only per the team-lead's scope ruling and AC-7 stays inviolate: `alpha_bot_execution.py` is NOT the fix locus. Before this revise, the frozen render path (F5(b)/(c), below) ignored the marker entirely regardless of what the snapshot carried — so a fetch-failure symphony's stale reconstruction was invisible either way (silently wrong, not silently safe). After F4 + F5(b)/(c), the frozen render path now HONESTLY reads whatever marker value the snapshot actually carries — closing the SILENT SWALLOW, not the underlying data gap. If a future symphony hits this exact fetch-failure-at-EOD scenario, the frozen dashboard will now correctly render its shadow-basis Held value (assuming the marker was `True` and a shadow row exists) rather than silently misrendering the reconstructed value with no possibility of ever being right — the render layer can only be as honest as the marker it's given, and F4/F5 make it maximally honest given that input. The underlying `symphony_data_cache`-vs-`bot_state` scope asymmetry in `alpha_bot_execution.py` itself is NOT touched by this cycle (would require an engine-layer fix, out of scope, AC-7).

**F2 (HIGH-MED) / F7 (LOW) — `guard_delta_vw`'s coverage-scaling formula corrected.** The paragraph above ("pairwise delta, full-membership floor preserved") describes `guard_delta_vw` as the paired-subset MEAN divergence (`dry_run_wsum / paired_weight − paired_if_held_wsum / paired_weight`), scaled afterward by `invested_frac` (a FULL-membership fraction) at the account-basis layer. This extrapolates the covered symphonies' average divergence onto uncovered capital. Reviewer's worked example, verified: 3 × $1,000 symphonies ($3,000 account), two covered with +1.0pp divergence, one with no shadow row today — the shipped-then-corrected formula: paired mean = +1.0pp, `invested_frac` = 1.0 → rendered account guard effect **+1.0pp**; the honest value (uncovered divergence unknown, conservatively treated as 0) is **+0.667pp** (= 1.0 × 2000/3000) — a 1.5x overstatement, unbounded as coverage shrinks toward the `_PBO_MIN_CONFIGS`-style floor, always in the inflating direction, and exact only under full coverage (which is why the original cycle's own 11/11-covered live capture never exposed it). **Fix:** `guard_delta_vw` is now the paired-subset divergence SUM divided by TOTAL weight in one division — `(dry_run_wsum − paired_if_held_wsum) / total_weight` — computing the coverage-scaled value directly and implicitly treating an uncovered symphony's unknown divergence as exactly 0, matching the reviewer's honest-value derivation. F7 folds into the same change: the redundant `paired_weight` counter (a second accumulator incremented in lockstep with `dry_run_weight`, with no assertion guarding the two never desync — precisely the desync-hazard class this whole PR exists to fix) is deleted; `dry_run_weight` alone gates both the `dry_run` average and the new formula. `get_portfolio_today_change_account_basis`'s docstring is corrected to describe both the paired (preferred) and legacy-fallback branches explicitly, replacing the now-false "dry_run and if_held share the same symphony-value denominator" invariant claim.

**F6 (MED) — the internal `guard_delta_vw` intermediate no longer leaks by default.** `include_paired_guard_delta` on `get_portfolio_today_change`/`_value_weighted_portfolio` is now keyword-only-default `False` (was hardcoded `True`) — the shape of `today_change` in every `/api/strip` response and the engine's persisted EOD snapshot (`alpha_bot_execution.py:1136`, reached with zero diff to that file since it now passes no kwarg and inherits the new default) is restored to a clean 2-key `{if_held, dry_run}` dict; callers that genuinely need the coverage-scaled intermediate opt in explicitly. **Interaction trap, closed:** `app.py`'s `_compute_portfolio_strip` has THREE separate `get_portfolio_today_change(...)` call sites (Tier-0 warm-cache, Tier-1 last-good, Tier-2 floor) plus the frozen branch's `_snap_vw_tc` call — ALL FOUR now pass `include_paired_guard_delta=True` explicitly, or F2's fix would silently regress at whichever tier is live production's most common case (Tier-0, warm cache). A genuine mutation-check gap surfaced mid-cycle: held-imp's own GREEN report (commit `f35b3de7`) disclosed that mutation-testing (disable each opt-in, confirm a test goes RED, restore) caught Tier-2 and the frozen floor as load-bearing but found NO test caught Tier-0 or Tier-1 disabled, because `test_account_basis_tc.py`'s F9-updated seam mocks patch `analytics.get_portfolio_today_change` wholesale and never exercise real kwarg-passing at those two sites. held-tw closed this gap in a dedicated follow-up (commit `50742343`) — 2 new route-level tests forcing Tier-0/Tier-1 respectively via direct cache seeding (never mocking `analytics`), each independently mutation-verified the same way held-imp verified the other two sites. All 4 opt-in sites now have dedicated mutation-sensitive coverage.

**F5(a)/(b) — frozen-branch parity, the pieces F4 doesn't cover for free.** (a) The frozen Tier-2 floor (`_snap_tc_final = _snap_vw_tc`, pre-revise) surfaced the raw VW dict directly with no account-basis conversion and no paired re-derivation — worse than F2's live-branch bug, since it produced a SIGN-FLIPPED artifact (rendering `-0.3333pp` against the worked example above, vs. the live branch's pre-fix `+1.0pp` overstatement) rather than merely an overstated one. Fixed to re-derive `dry_run` from `if_held + guard_delta_vw`, matching the live path's own Tier-2 fix. (b) `_snap_bot_state` (the frozen Tier-2 aggregate's hand-built 4-key dict — `current_value`/`current_return`/`name`/`account`) is the ONE site F4's `bot_state_entry`-primary pivot does not cover for free, since it is not the real `bot_state` entry — it gains the marker key explicitly.

**F8/F9 (test integrity, MED) — sufficiency gaps in the original cycle's own test suite.** F8: the AC-3 route-level aggregate assertion (`if_held is not None`) was VACUOUS — it passed identically against both the pre-fix (`+0.192476`) and post-fix (`+0.209465`) aggregates, so the headline end-to-end portfolio-convergence claim was untested at the aggregate level; rewritten to compute an independently-derived expected value from the fixture and assert it via `pytest.approx`. F9: two seam mocks in `tests/analytics/test_account_basis_tc.py` patched `get_portfolio_today_change` with bare 2-key dicts, so — post-F6 — these pre-existing phantom-alpha regression guards were exercising only the legacy fallback branch production no longer reaches at those call sites (production always supplies `guard_delta_vw` there); both mocks updated to 3-key dicts.

**F13/F14 (test hygiene, LOW).** F13: the 11-column `shadow_history` CREATE TABLE DDL, pasted 3 times in `test_held_basis_convergence.py` with the 3rd copy silently dropping `NOT NULL` on `current_return` (an intentional relaxation indistinguishable from a typo), is now one `_create_shadow_schema(conn, *, current_return_nullable=False)` helper naming the relaxation explicitly. F14: `test_golden_fixture_weighted_average_helper_is_self_consistent` was a tautology (compared the helper against the identical expression re-typed inline); rewritten to assert against an independently hand-computed literal from the fixture — the test-writer's own first hand-typed literal was itself arithmetically wrong and caught only by independently running the computation in Bash before committing, a self-demonstration of exactly the failure mode this fix exists to prevent.

**F10/F11/F12 — TRACKED, not resolved, not lost.**
- **F10 (MED, design gap):** under partial shadow coverage on a multi-trigger day, the portfolio VW `if_held` can silently mix shadow-basis (a triggered+marked symphony with a same-day row) and reconstructed-basis (a triggered+marked symphony WITHOUT one, hitting the AC-4 fallback) contributions in one weighted mean, with no basis-disclosure marker on the rendered value. Needs a basis-disclosure design decision, not a patch — future cycle.
- **F11 (LOW-MED, design gap):** the marker-gated override checks same-day row EXISTENCE and non-NULL, never RECENCY — during a DB-lock storm the day's latest shadow row could be materially stale (minutes old) and still get used as Held against fresher account-basis figures, presenting staleness as divergence with no signal. Mitigated today only by the fact that Bot and Held share the same row (no cross-row staleness skew between the two columns) — genuine recency signaling is new scope, tracked.
- **F12 (LOW, refactor):** the same 8-key analytics `sym_dict` literal is hand-built at six `app.py` sites; a `_build_analytics_sym_dict` helper would deliver any future field everywhere by construction. PARTIALLY absorbed by F4 this cycle — the 2 marker-threading additions the original cycle made to two of those six sites became removable, reducing (not closing) the duplication this finding describes.

### F6 follow-up — `guard_delta_vw` leak closed on both Tier-2-floor else branches (2026-08-25)

**Trigger.** F6 (above) restored `today_change` to a clean 2-key `{if_held, dry_run}` shape at all 4 real `include_paired_guard_delta=True` call sites and added `test_api_state_tier2_floor_today_change_is_exactly_two_keys` — but that test only exercised the Tier-2 floor's IF branch (paired coverage present). It never reached the Tier-2 floor's ELSE branch (zero paired coverage — no symphony has a same-trading-day `shadow_history` row, so `_value_weighted_portfolio` sets `dry_run_weight == 0.0` and `guard_delta_vw` resolves `None`, `analytics.py` ~1178/1188-1190). Two of F6's four opt-in sites build their `today_change`/`_snap_tc_final` from a Tier-2 "floor" that has this shape, and BOTH had the same else-branch bug:

- **Site 1 — live path.** `app.py`'s `_compute_portfolio_strip` (`else: today_change = _vw_tc_floor`, ~line 1664 pre-fix) assigned the raw 3-key `_vw_tc_floor` dict verbatim — still carrying the internal `guard_delta_vw` key — straight into the public `/api/state` `portfolio_strip.today_change` JSON.
- **Site 2 — frozen/EOD-snapshot path.** `app.py`'s `get_state()` frozen branch (`else: _snap_tc_final = _snap_vw_tc`, `app.py:2412` pre-fix) had the structurally identical bug on its own independent code path, reachable via the routine after-hours `market_state == "closed_frozen"` branch. Found by gdvw-reviewer during review of Site 1's fix.

Exactly the leak class F6 exists to prevent, on the two branches F6's own regression test didn't cover.

**The fix (`app.py` only, both sites).** Each else branch now builds an explicit fresh 2-key dict instead of passing its raw VW dict through: Site 1 — `today_change = {"if_held": _vw_tc_floor.get("if_held"), "dry_run": _vw_tc_floor.get("dry_run")}`; Site 2 — `_snap_tc_final = {"if_held": _snap_vw_tc.get("if_held"), "dry_run": _snap_vw_tc.get("dry_run")}`. Both mirror their own branch's IF-branch construction style immediately above them. `analytics.py`, `math_engine.py`, `alpha_bot_execution.py`, `synthetic_history.py` carry zero diff — the leak was purely the route's failure to strip the internal key before assignment at 2 call sites, not a computation defect.

**Test gap closed.** Two new tests in `tests/app/test_held_basis_route_convergence.py`: `test_api_state_tier2_floor_zero_paired_coverage_strips_guard_delta_vw_key` (Site 1) and `test_frozen_tier2_floor_zero_paired_coverage_strips_guard_delta_vw_key` (Site 2), each fixtured with one `bot_state` symphony carrying valid weight+if_held but no `shadow_history` row for the trading day (forcing the respective else branch). Both confirmed non-vacuous: FAIL pre-fix with actual keys `{'dry_run', 'guard_delta_vw', 'if_held'}`; the pre-existing sibling tests PASS unchanged in the same run — each leak was isolated to its own branch, no broader regression. Site 2's test was authored inside `TestF5FrozenBranchConvergence` (that class's existing home for frozen-branch tests) at RED, then relocated into `TestF6NoInternalKeyLeakage` per team-lead's review — that class already held the live IF/else leak guards, so consolidating the frozen-else guard there completes the full live/frozen × IF/else internal-key-leak matrix in one discoverable place. Confirmed via `git diff bc85e33f^..bc85e33f`: setup/assertions are byte-identical across the move, only the docstring gained one paragraph explaining the co-location rationale. A same-day `ruff format` pass (`35340d62`) then wrapped 2 long lines the move introduced — cosmetic only, re-verified 21/21 passing after. Both tests now live in `TestF6NoInternalKeyLeakage` (verified directly against the file at current HEAD — no class boundary between them).

**Reviewer's completeness proof — these two else branches are the COMPLETE `guard_delta_vw` leak surface, not merely "two spots found so far."** Independently verified by gdvw-doc against the source (not relaying the claim):
1. **Only 2 of the 4 real `include_paired_guard_delta=True` call sites can leak.** All 4 sites live in `app.py`: Tier-0 warm-cache (`~1613-1619`), Tier-1 last-good (`~1630-1636`), Tier-2 floor live (`~1643-1649`, Site 1 above), and the frozen branch's `_snap_vw_tc` call (`~2370-2373`, feeding Site 2 above). Tier-0 and Tier-1 route their `_vw_tc` result through `analytics.get_portfolio_today_change_account_basis(...)` before it ever reaches `today_change` — every one of that function's return statements (`analytics.py:1403/1407/1410/1412/1414/1437`) is a fresh `{"if_held": ..., "dry_run": ...}` literal, never the input dict passed through. Only the two Tier-2 floors (live + frozen) assign their outward-facing field directly from the raw VW dict on any branch — and only their ELSE branch (zero paired coverage; the IF branch already builds a clean literal) had the bug.
2. **The engine's own EOD-persisted snapshot can't carry the key either.** `alpha_bot_execution.py`'s `get_portfolio_today_change(...)` call (`~line 1136`) passes no `include_paired_guard_delta` kwarg at all — inherits F6's default `False`, so `_value_weighted_portfolio` never computes or attaches `guard_delta_vw` to that dict in the first place. Nothing to leak; not just nothing that leaks today.
3. **The account-totals cache stores a scalar, not the dict.** `_account_totals_cache.get("portfolio_tc")` / `_account_totals_last_good.get("portfolio_tc")` (the `_cached_tc`/`_lg_tc` values feeding Tier-0/Tier-1 above) are Composer's `todays_percent_change` — a bare float passed as `account_if_held_tc`, never the `_vw_tc` dict itself. No cache-write path exists for the raw VW dict to persist and re-leak from later.

**Verified independently (gdvw-doc, not relaying a prior self-report).** Fresh `python -m pytest tests/app/test_held_basis_route_convergence.py -n0 -q` at HEAD `35340d62` — 21/21 PASSED (whole file, both new tests included, zero regression to the other 19). `git diff cc221a9a..35340d62 --stat` — `app.py` (+10/-2, exactly the 2 else branches identified above) + the test file only; zero diff to `analytics.py`/`math_engine.py`/`alpha_bot_execution.py`/`synthetic_history.py`.

**Reviewer.** gdvw-reviewer combined APPROVE at HEAD `35340d62`: fix correctness on both sites, RED non-vacuity on both, the test-relocation + ruff-format commits confirmed behavior-neutral, `analytics.py`/engine zero-diff confirmed, and an independent completeness sweep re-confirmed no third leak site exists (matching the proof above). No blocking findings.

**Accepted follow-up (not this cycle), `/code-review`.** The `/code-review` pass on this cycle returned no correctness bug, plus one accepted structural observation: the internal-key strip is now enforced by CONVENTION at each of the four `today_change`-shaped direct-assign sites (live IF, live else, frozen IF, frozen else) — each site independently builds its own `{if_held, dry_run}` literal — rather than by shared infrastructure. A future 5th call site opting into `include_paired_guard_delta=True` and assigning its result directly (mirroring any of these four) could reintroduce the same leak with no compile-time or test-level guard forcing it to strip the key. **Recommended hardening (own future cycle):** collapse the four projections into one leak-proof projection point — either a shared `today_change`-projection helper all four sites call, or renaming/marking the internal field so the JSON serializer structurally cannot emit it regardless of call-site discipline. **Deferred, not fixed, deliberately:** the current fix is both correct and PROVEN COMPLETE for all four existing sites (the completeness sweep above) — this is future-proofing against a hypothetical 5th site, not a gap in today's fix, and the hardening would deliberately refactor the two already-correct IF branches alongside the two else branches this cycle exists to fix. Scoping that refactor into this cycle would have mixed a proven-complete bug fix with a speculative structural change; it deserves its own scoped cycle instead.

**Files changed.** `app.py` (2 Tier-2-floor else branches, 4 lines each); `tests/app/test_held_basis_route_convergence.py` (+2 tests, relocated into `TestF6NoInternalKeyLeakage`, ruff-formatted); `docs/generated/app.md` (Tier-2 floor re-derivation, frozen-branch F5(a) parity note, and header history all updated for both sites); `DECISIONS.md` (this addendum).

## DE-FR-PROPOSAL-IDENTITY-001 — Frontrunner Proposal Identity: honest Composer draft naming + overlay-delta provenance (2026-08-20)

### The defect

Frontrunner Builder proposals are, by design, FULL standalone copies of the incumbent symphony with one generated frontrunner overlay spliced over one detected cascade (`splice_candidate_into_symphony`, migration `034`'s own comment: "the full spliced candidate symphony"). Every operator-facing surface, however, named a proposal as if it were a bare frontrunner fragment: the Composer draft uploaded on approval was named the generic `"Frontrunner Candidate — <hash>"` with a static one-line description, and the dashboard cards never stated that the artifact was a complete copy of the operator's symphony or what Approve actually creates. The operator (2026-08-20) ruled this misleading, verified directly against the 3 live droplet rows at the time -- all `proposal_source='frontrunner_builder'`, all incumbent `8FAXAnQmYi1INDubazeC`, each `candidate_tree` ~186KB, all status `uploaded`, two created 2 minutes apart in the same weekly run (confirming names must be unique per proposal, not per symphony/day).

### What shipped

**Three new pure helpers** in `advisors/frontrunner_builder.py` (no I/O, unit-tested in isolation):
- `build_proposal_symphony_name(display_name, proposal_id, source)` -- the Composer draft `name`, bounded to `MAX_PROPOSAL_NAME_CHARS=100` (only `display_name` is ever truncated; the `#{proposal_id})` suffix always survives, guaranteeing uniqueness for same-run duplicates).
- `build_proposal_symphony_description(...)` -- the Composer draft `description`, bounded to `MAX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS=1000`, carrying full provenance (incumbent name+hash, replaced-node id, overlay summary, proposal id, creation date) plus the operator-mandated sentences "Full standalone copy — the original symphony is not modified." and "Undeployed candidate — review before investing."
- `summarize_overlay(overlay_tree)` -- a short, specific, human-readable one-liner (e.g. "relative-strength-index(SPY,10) gt 30 rotates into VIXY"), operating on the raw PRE-compile/pre-graft build-plan-DSL overlay node (never the post-splice tree, whose `else` branch embeds the entire incumbent core), degrading to the exact literal "compound condition overlay" on any underivable shape -- never a fabricated guess.

**Persist-site wiring.** `_run_build_for_symphony`'s existing persist site additively stamps `metrics_json["overlay_tree"]` (= `result.candidate`, the pre-graft node -- adversarially guarded in tests against the post-splice `spliced` object, which would recreate the exact misleading-identity problem this feature fixes), `["replaced_node_id"]`, and `["overlay_summary"]` -- no schema migration (the column is already free-form JSON), existing keys byte-unchanged.

**Approve-path wiring.** `approve_frontrunner_proposal` resolves the incumbent's display name (hash-to-name via `database.load_state()`, honest hash fallback when the symphony is gone from `bot_state`) and calls the two builders in place of the old hardcoded name/description literals -- the bare-hash format no longer occurs on any approval, including legacy proposals predating this cycle (AC-6 degrade: missing overlay metrics render "overlay not recorded for this proposal" in the description, never a crash, never a fabricated summary).

**Dashboard render (`app.py` `ai_advisor_tab()` + `templates/ai_advisor.html`).** The `frontrunner_proposals` prefetch loop gains: incumbent display-name resolution (one `database.load_state()` call per request, not per row), `metrics_json` non-dict normalization to `{}` (AC-6), and a bounded `overlay_tree_preview` mirroring the existing `candidate_tree_preview` transform (`overlay_tree` is NOT popped, since the template still needs `replaced_node_id`/`overlay_summary` from the same dict). `frontrunner_builder`-source cards gain an identity line ("Full standalone copy of {incumbent} with one new frontrunner overlay"), an explainer line ("Approve creates a NEW undeployed Composer symphony — the incumbent is never modified."), an overlay-summary line (honest empty-state fallback), and a second collapsed overlay-preview `<details>` distinct from the existing raw-candidate preview. `strategy_builder_retrofit`-source cards gain their own from-scratch identity line ("does not contain the incumbent's logic"). The raw-preview `<details>` label now branches by source: "Full spliced symphony (preview)" for `frontrunner_builder`, "Proposed symphony (preview)" for `strategy_builder_retrofit` -- a retrofit candidate is from-scratch, so calling its preview "spliced" would itself be dishonest (team-lead ruling, mid-cycle finding, `f8350672`).

**Zero change to detection, splice, gating, or acceptance math (AC-8).** `composer_draft_client.save_symphony`'s payload changes ONLY in the `name`/`description` string arguments; no new write routes; `LIVE_EXECUTION` untouched; the approve route's request/response contract unchanged.

### Deviation from the plan, locked at implementation (`65738df0`)

The plan's Architecture section implied the "Full standalone copy — the original symphony is not modified." description sentence should gate on the overlay-identity metrics (`replaced_node_id`/`overlay_summary`) being present. The shipped behavior makes this sentence **unconditional** for `source="frontrunner_builder"` -- a genuine improvement over the original spec, ruled at implementation: the full-copy property is a fact about the SPLICE itself, not about whether AC-3's metrics were recorded at persist time, so a legacy row predating this feature is still a genuine full spliced copy and gating the sentence on the metrics would have incorrectly implied otherwise for exactly the rows most in need of the disclosure. A dedicated regression test locks this against a future "fix" making it conditional again.

### A latent crash found and fixed mid-cycle (not in the original plan)

Wiring AC-6's `metrics_json` non-dict-to-`{}` normalization exposed a **pre-existing** latent defect in the dashboard card template: six stats-table cells (Calmar/CAGR/MDD x incumbent/candidate) used an `is not none` guard. Once `metrics_json` degrades to `{}`, the referenced field is Jinja `Undefined` -- not literal `None` -- which passes `is not none` and then crashes the subsequent `format()` filter. This was the actual root cause of the AC-6 non-dict-`metrics_json` 500, not merely the missing normalization the plan anticipated. Fixed with `is defined and` guards on all 7 same-shaped cells; the 7th (`fr-node-count-delta`, a bare expression that silently rendered blank rather than crashing, so it was missed in the first pass) was caught by a dedicated sufficiency-review RED test (`ebe4bbb0`) and closed in Revise 1 (`02f86e51`).

Two unrelated defects surfaced during this cycle's investigation of the Frontrunner Builder cluster and are explicitly NOT addressed here:

- **SIMPLIFY acceptance path structurally unreachable.** ~~RESOLVED — see `DE-FR-SIMPLIFY-001` (2026-08-24) below.~~ `frontrunner_acceptance.py`'s `MATERIAL_SIMPLIFICATION_MAX_RATIO=0.50` is compared against whole-symphony node counts (incumbent-copy-plus-overlay vs. incumbent-copy-plus-overlay), not the overlay delta alone -- since a splice replaces one cascade inside an otherwise-identical full copy, the ratio can essentially never clear 0.50 in practice, meaning the PRESERVE+SIMPLIFY acceptance path (one of the two documented acceptance routes alongside IMPROVE) is effectively dead. A future cycle should re-scope the ratio to the overlay subtree specifically.
- **`asset_class` hardcoded to `EQUITIES`.** ~~RESOLVED — see `DE-FR-ASSET-CLASS-001` (2026-08-24/25) below.~~ `composer_draft_client.py`'s `_DEFAULT_ASSET_CLASS` is a fixed constant on every `save_symphony` call, including approved Frontrunner Builder proposals for a non-equities incumbent (if one ever exists) -- a future cycle should thread the incumbent's real asset class through instead of assuming equities universally.

Both are named explicitly here per the operator's plan-time ruling that they be tracked, not silently dropped or bundled into this cycle's diff.

**F1 (`advisors/frontrunner_builder.py`) -- `summarize_overlay` degraded every nested scale-in overlay to the generic fallback.** The generation prompt's own flagship worked example (HARD REQUIREMENT #4) nests an `if`/`if_compound` node inside the outer overlay's `"then"` branch -- a genuine 2-tier scale-in structure. `_find_first_asset_ticker` had no case for a nested node with neither `"children"` nor `"node"`, so it returned `None` for every real scale-in overlay, and `summarize_overlay` silently fell through to `"compound condition overlay"` -- the specific-summary path was unreachable for the exact shape the system is designed to generate. Fixed: both builders now omit the name-slot segment/clause entirely when `display_name` is falsy.

**F3 (`advisors/frontrunner_builder.py`) -- `approve_frontrunner_proposal`'s `metrics_json` guard silently swallowed a distinguishable failure mode.** `proposal.get("metrics_json") or {}` does not fire on a TRUTHY non-`dict` value (e.g. a stored JSON array) -- the subsequent `.get()` calls then raised `AttributeError`, caught by the function's own outer `except`, but WITHOUT persisting an `error_message` first, unlike every other documented failure branch. Fixed to an explicit `isinstance(dict)` check, mirroring `app.py`'s own equivalent AC-6 guard.

**F4 (`advisors/frontrunner_builder.py`) -- the retrofit description's first sentence claimed a relationship it doesn't have.** `build_proposal_symphony_description`'s first sentence was shared verbatim across both `source` branches ("Frontrunner Builder candidate for {name} (incumbent {hash})...") -- false for `strategy_builder_retrofit`, whose whole point is that it does NOT contain the incumbent's logic. Fixed: both are now required (non-`None`) before the specific-summary path is taken.

**F7 (`advisors/frontrunner_builder.py`) -- the universal safety sentence could be truncated off a long description.** The old assembly appended `"Undeployed candidate — review before investing."` FIRST in the parts list, then truncated the fully-assembled string from the tail with a bare slice -- a sufficiently long `display_name` or `overlay_summary` could chop the safety sentence off entirely. Fixed: `display_name` is now independently bounded (`_MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_CHARS_IN_DESCRIPTION=200`) before embedding, everything else is assembled and truncated to fit within `MAX_PROPOSAL_DESCRIPTION_CHARS − len(_SAFETY_SENTENCE) − 1`, and the safety sentence is appended LAST -- guaranteeing `description.endswith(_SAFETY_SENTENCE)` for every proposal regardless of field lengths.

## DE-FR-SIMPLIFY-001 — Frontrunner SIMPLIFY-Path Delta-Scoping (2026-08-24)

### Defect

`advisors/frontrunner_acceptance.py`'s Calmar acceptance gate (`evaluate_calmar_acceptance`) has two admission paths: IMPROVE, or PRESERVE+SIMPLIFY. The SIMPLIFY path requires `candidate_node_count <= incumbent_node_count * MATERIAL_SIMPLIFICATION_MAX_RATIO` (0.50) — a 2x-or-better size reduction. Both operands were the WHOLE-SYMPHONY node counts. Since every Frontrunner Builder candidate is, by construction, a full standalone copy of the incumbent symphony with exactly one detected cascade replaced by a small generated overlay (`frontrunner_builder.splice_candidate_into_symphony`), `candidate_node_count` is always ~98-100% of `incumbent_node_count` — empirically measured across all 11 of the operator's real trees, 2026-08-20. The ratio could essentially never clear 0.50 in practice: SIMPLIFY was structurally unreachable, and IMPROVE was the only path any candidate could ever admit through.

Found by PR #126's independent `/code-review` pass (the mandatory review gate on `DE-FR-PROPOSAL-IDENTITY-001`), deferred at the time as explicitly out of scope for that cycle (see that entry's "Deferred — explicitly OUT of scope" section, now annotated RESOLVED, pointing here). This cycle fixes it.

### The fix

Re-scopes the SIMPLIFY-clause comparison to the honest delta: the generated overlay's node count vs. the node count of the incumbent cascade subtree it replaces — both already computable at the real call site (`frontrunner_builder._run_build_for_symphony`), since the builder holds the compiled overlay (`GenerationResult.compiled_tree`/`.candidate`) and the detected cascade (`Cascade.overlay_tree` — `advisors.frontrunner_detector.Cascade`, not `FrontrunnerCascade`, no such class exists in this codebase) in the same loop iteration.

`evaluate_calmar_acceptance` gains two additive, keyword-only params — `overlay_node_count`/`replaced_cascade_node_count` (default `None`) — consumed by a new pure helper, `_is_delta_scoped_material_simplification`, which fails closed on either operand being `None`/non-numeric/`<=0`/the overlay being bigger than the cascade. The pre-existing `incumbent_node_count`/`candidate_node_count` whole-tree params are retained on the signature UNCHANGED, but now serve only the unrelated `node_count_delta` display metric (AC-6) — the SIMPLIFY clause never reads them again. A caller that omits the two new kwargs (an un-migrated legacy call site) makes SIMPLIFY structurally unreachable at that call site, never a silent fallback to the old broken whole-tree comparison.

`advisors/frontrunner_builder.py` gains `_count_overlay_node_count(candidate, compiled_tree=None)` (a three-tier resolution: reuse `GenerationResult.compiled_tree` when present, else an already-step-shaped candidate, else a fresh pure-compile with no `backtest_fn` — never network, never a fabricated `0`) and a shared `_unwrap_single_compiled_child` helper. `_run_build_for_symphony`'s loop computes `replaced_cascade_node_count = _count_tree_nodes(cascade.overlay_tree)` directly (already raw_value-shaped, no compile needed) and threads both counts through `_gate_and_accept_candidate`'s new additive keyword-only params into the acceptance call.

### `[PM-ASSUMED]` design ruling

Delta-scoped ratio (overlay node count vs. replaced-cascade node count) is the semantically correct reading of "materially simplifies" for a single-cascade splice — a whole-tree ratio is mathematically incapable of expressing it (98-100% measured on all 11 real trees), and both operands were already in scope at the real call site (the `DE-FR-PROPOSAL-IDENTITY-001` cycle's own `replaced_node_id` plumbing had already established the cascade-identification precedent this reuses). The `0.50` constant VALUE is unchanged — it was always calibrated against overlay-vs-cascade scale (the grounding note's "collapsing hundreds of flat RSI-gt rungs" framing describes an overlay-scale reduction, not a whole-symphony one); the COMPARISON was the bug, not the threshold. Undisputed at implementation — no team-lead pushback, no revision needed.

### Fail-closed hardening beyond the plan

The plan's AC-5 specified declining on `None`/absent and overlay-bigger-than-cascade. Mid-cycle, team-lead additionally required an `overlay_node_count=0` case to decline (not just `None`) — a real compiled overlay always has ≥1 node, so a `0` could only mean an upstream count failure masquerading as a legitimately tiny (and therefore trivially-passing) value; `_is_delta_scoped_material_simplification`'s guard is `<= 0`, not `< 0` or `is None` alone, closing this gap for both operands.

### A reviewer finding folded in mid-cycle (not scope creep — a genuine correctness/efficiency gap in the new code)

fps-reviewer's first-round pass returned APPROVE with one non-blocking INFO finding: `_count_overlay_node_count`'s first GREEN draft always re-compiled `candidate` from scratch via `plan_tree_compiler.compile_plan`, even on the successful-generation happy path where `generate_candidate_overlay` had already produced `GenerationResult.compiled_tree` moments earlier — a redundant second compile-plus-validate pass, plus a landmine for a future edit that might assume the count reflects a fresh compile when it may not. Team-lead's ruling: fold the fix in now since it's small — consume the already-compiled tree at the call site, keep the pure-compile as a fallback only. Landed as `_count_overlay_node_count`'s three-tier signature (`compiled_tree: dict | None = None`), verified by a dedicated regression test confirming `compile_plan` is called exactly ONCE per real build-loop iteration for the candidate (not 2, not 3) and two additional fallback-path unit tests (compiled-tree-absent → fresh-compile; fresh-compile-fails → `None`, never a fabricated `0`). **[Corrected, Revise 3]** this "2, not 3" framing was accurate only as of this fold-in's own HEAD (`f2611ee1`/`62366d3c`) — Revise 3's F7 fix additionally threaded `compiled_tree` into `splice_candidate_into_symphony`, eliminating what had been a second/third redundant compile there too. The current, correct invariant — `compile_plan` called exactly once per candidate across the WHOLE `_run_build_for_symphony` → `_gate_and_accept_candidate` → `splice_candidate_into_symphony` chain — is proven directly by `tests/advisors/test_frontrunner_simplify_path_wiring.py::test_no_redundant_compile_anywhere_in_the_flow_including_splice`, which wraps the real `compile_plan` and counts calls; see this entry's "Revise 3" section below.

### Scope boundaries held

Zero diff to `frontrunner_detector.py`, splice mechanics (`splice_candidate_into_symphony`), `backtest_gate_engine.py`, or Calmar math itself (AC-7) — independently confirmed via `git diff` scoped to only `advisors/frontrunner_acceptance.py` + `advisors/frontrunner_builder.py` (+ test files). The IMPROVE path is byte-unchanged (AC-4) — it reads neither new keyword param. ### Revise 3 (PR #128 independent `/code-review`, 2026-08-24)

**Trigger.** The mandatory `/review` gate on PR #128 (this cycle's PR, opened after the original `DE-FR-SIMPLIFY-001` cycle above) found the shipped delta-scoped fix STILL had a load-bearing defect: `frontrunner_detector.Cascade.overlay_tree` (the operand the builder was counting as `replaced_cascade_node_count`) is the detector's STUB-PADDED COMPACT CASCADE, not honest signal logic. The prior cycle's own AC-3 reachability fixture certified this asymmetry because it hand-built a synthetic `Cascade` object bypassing the real detector path entirely — it never exercised the stub-padding behavior it was supposed to be testing against. 15 total findings (1 CRITICAL merge-blocking, 14 others), consolidated across an interim ruling round plus an addendum round.

**RULING 1 (CRITICAL, F1) — both SIMPLIFY operands must count SIGNAL LOGIC ONLY.** `frontrunner_detector._build_cascade_overlay`/`_compact_if_node` splits an if-node's two branches into "fire" (the smaller-by-node-count side, copied verbatim — real content) and "continuation" (the larger side, REPLACED with synthetic `_STUBBED_CORE_CONTINUATION` leaf placeholders sized `max(count(continuation), fire_count+1)` — deliberately kept larger than fire so downstream fire/continuation size comparisons stay internally consistent). `fire_child`/`continuation_child` is picked by SIZE, not position or `is-else-condition?` — either original branch can end up on either side. `cascade.overlay_tree` is the compacted if-node with BOTH branches — real fire content + stub-padded continuation. Counting the WHOLE thing (as the original fix did) counts core-sized stub padding as "replaced logic," which could INFLATE the denominator ARBITRARILY (see A4 evidence below) — inverting SIMPLIFY a second time, not back to unreachable but to admitting overlays LARGER than the signal logic they genuinely replace. Fixed: new `frontrunner_builder._count_signal_logic_nodes(if_node)` returns `1 + count(fire_child)`, excluding the continuation/else entirely, identifying the excluded child via (1) a `_contains_stub_marker` search (reliable on detector output, where fire/continuation is size-picked) or (2) falling back to `is-else-condition? is True` (reliable on a freshly-generated overlay candidate, never detector-compacted, mirroring the existing production `_find_terminal_else_child`'s identical logic). Returns `None` — never a whole-tree fallback — when `if_node` isn't shaped as exactly two dict if-children (team-lead ruling: a whole-tree fallback would be ANTI-conservative, inflating exactly the denominator this fix exists to deflate, on exactly the inputs the function understands least). `MATERIAL_SIMPLIFICATION_MAX_RATIO=0.50` stays unchanged — the calibration basis was always overlay-scale, per the original `DE-FR-SIMPLIFY-001` design note.

**RULING 2 (F2) — SIMPLIFY additionally requires whole-tree no-growth.** `frontrunner_acceptance.evaluate_calmar_acceptance`'s SIMPLIFY clause gains a third, independent gate: `node_count_delta <= 0` (the pre-existing whole-tree `candidate_node_count - incumbent_node_count` computation, already carried on `AcceptanceResult`). Restores an invariant the delta-scoped ratio alone structurally cannot see — `frontrunner_builder._graft_incumbent_core` re-inserting the incumbent's full core into the candidate's else branch can make the OVERALL spliced tree bigger even though the signal logic genuinely shrank; tagging "simplification" on a tree that grew would be an absurdity the ratio alone cannot catch. Never traded off against the ratio or the Calmar check — all three gates required.

**RULING 3 (F3+F10) — `_count_tree_nodes` must descend compound-condition clauses.** `advisors/frontrunner_builder.py`'s `_count_tree_nodes` previously only walked `.get("children")`; a compound condition's clause list (`make_compound_condition`'s `"conditions"` field, a DATA field on an if-child, not under `"children"`) was invisible to the walk — a 2-clause and a 12-clause compound condition with identical then/else content both counted as 7 nodes (empirically verified). Fixed: also descends into a `condition` dict field and a `conditions` list clause when present, making clause count genuinely load-bearing on every count this function feeds (`node_count_delta` AND, via `_count_signal_logic_nodes`, both SIMPLIFY operands). **[SUPERSEDED, Revise 4, 2026-08-24 — corrected by this doc pass, 2026-08-25]** `_count_tree_nodes` itself was REVERTED to a children-only walk in Revise 4 (R4-2) — this RULING's own compound-condition-clause descent was superseded, not kept: `_count_signal_logic_nodes` (this RULING's SIMPLIFY-operand consumer, named above) was itself DELETED in Revise 4, replaced by the detector-stamped `Cascade.signal_logic_node_count`; clause-aware counting for the SIMPLIFY operands now lives exclusively in the new, dedicated `frontrunner_detector._count_clause_aware_signal_logic` (imported by the builder, never duplicated). `_count_tree_nodes`'s only remaining consumer is RULING 2's whole-symphony `node_count_delta` gate, which never needed clause-awareness in the first place (a coarse did-it-grow-at-all check). This historical bullet's own body is left unedited per the project's non-destructive-annotation convention — see this entry's "Revise 4" section (R4-2) for the full current-truth account, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s frontrunner-cluster key-files row (corrected by this same doc pass) for the current-state summary.

**F7 — thread `compiled_tree` into `splice_candidate_into_symphony` too.** Same invariant as the original cycle's already-shipped `_count_overlay_node_count` fix (fps-reviewer's earlier INFO finding, folded in at `f2611ee1`) — `splice_candidate_into_symphony` did its OWN separate `plan_tree_compiler.compile_plan` call on `result.candidate`, a THIRD redundant compile on the happy path. Gains a keyword-only `compiled_tree: dict | None = None` param, threaded from `_run_build_for_symphony` (`compiled_tree=result.compiled_tree`); falls back to its pre-existing compile/accept-as-is paths only when absent. Closes the loop opened by the original cycle's own "2, not 3" claim (see the correction on this entry's main section above) — `compile_plan` is now called exactly ONCE per candidate across the whole `_run_build_for_symphony` → `_gate_and_accept_candidate` → `splice_candidate_into_symphony` chain, proven by `test_no_redundant_compile_anywhere_in_the_flow_including_splice`.

**F8 — harden + share `_unwrap_single_compiled_child`.** Strict dict-or-None contract for any input shape (never raises); `children` must genuinely be a `list` of length 1 with a `dict` sole entry, never a truthy-fallback coercion of a malformed shape. `splice_candidate_into_symphony` now calls this SAME shared helper instead of a duplicated inline unwrap.

**F9/A3 — `_safe_node_count_float` node-count-operand hardening.** A dedicated stricter coercion, used ONLY for the SIMPLIFY-clause operands (never the general-purpose `_safe_float`): declines on `bool` (Python's `bool` is an `int` subtype — `float(True)==1.0` would coerce a caller bug into a plausible tiny count), a numeric string, and non-finite values (`inf` trivially satisfies any finite ratio comparison; `nan` comparisons are always `False`, an ambiguous fall-through). A3 (empirically probed): `float(10**400)` raises `OverflowError`, which pre-fix escaped `_safe_float` entirely and was caught by `evaluate_calmar_acceptance`'s own outer catch-all — nulling `candidate_sharpe`/`candidate_volatility`/both Calmar values/`node_count_delta` even though they were fully computable from otherwise-valid metrics. Fixed by catching `OverflowError` inside `_safe_node_count_float` itself, letting the rest of the function complete normally with a real, populated reject. The fabrication-risk asymmetry between the overlay (numerator, genuinely dangerous on a bool/string) and cascade (denominator, self-defeating except for `inf`) sides is documented in-source; symmetric checking is applied to both anyway as defense-in-depth.

**F11 (accepted) — `_count_overlay_node_count`'s tier-2 labeled, not dropped.** The already-`step`-shaped candidate shortcut is labeled "unreachable under current call graph, second-layer defense" (this project's established `_resolve_admission_mdd_baseline` convention) rather than removed — the sole production caller always populates `compiled_tree` alongside a non-`None` candidate, so tier 2 cannot fire today, but is kept as defense-in-depth.

**F12 (accepted, ride-along, not a dedicated item per team-lead) — the overlay>cascade guard's framing.** `_is_delta_scoped_material_simplification`'s explicit "overlay bigger than cascade" check is reframed in its docstring as a "ratio >= 1 tripwire," not a co-equal condition alongside the `<=0` checks — the ratio comparison would already reject this case on its own; the explicit guard is a self-documenting aid, not load-bearing on its own. No behavior change.

**F13 — `plan_id` constant extraction.** Three inline `plan_id` literals (`"frontrunner-candidate"`/`"frontrunner-overlay-node-count"`/`"frontrunner-splice-candidate"`, each duplicated at its own call site) promoted to module-level `_PLAN_ID_GENERATION`/`_PLAN_ID_OVERLAY_NODE_COUNT`/`_PLAN_ID_SPLICE_CANDIDATE` constants — a single source of truth per marker; test-writer's existing tests assert against the literal string values, which are unchanged, so no test churn was required.

**F5/F6 (production-only, doc/comment work, this doc-writer's job per the handoff) — stale constant-comment + module header.** `advisors/frontrunner_acceptance.py`'s `MATERIAL_SIMPLIFICATION_MAX_RATIO` comment and module docstring, and `advisors/frontrunner_builder.py`'s SIMPLIFY-threading comments, now state the signal-logic-only/three-gate semantic — see the diff at HEAD `70f832b3` and this doc pass's `docs/generated/` updates.

## DE-FR-ASSET-CLASS-001 — Frontrunner Draft Asset-Class Propagation (2026-08-24/25)

### Defect

`advisors/composer_draft_client.py` hardcodes `_DEFAULT_ASSET_CLASS="EQUITIES"` as `save_symphony`'s `asset_class` default. The one production caller — `advisors/frontrunner_builder.approve_frontrunner_proposal` (the operator-approval → real-Composer-draft-create seam) — passed `raw_value=candidate_tree` but never `asset_class`, so every Frontrunner/Strategy-Builder-retrofit draft was stamped `EQUITIES` regardless of the incumbent symphony's real asset class. Found and deferred as explicitly OUT of scope by `DE-FR-PROPOSAL-IDENTITY-001` (2026-08-20), then again by `DE-FR-SIMPLIFY-001`'s "Scope boundaries held" section (2026-08-24, same day this cycle shipped) — this entry is where it is FIXED, not merely tracked.

### The fix

New pure D-1 helper `advisors/frontrunner_builder._resolve_draft_asset_class(candidate_tree: dict | None) -> str`, called at `approve_frontrunner_proposal`'s existing `save_symphony` call site (`asset_class = _resolve_draft_asset_class(candidate_tree); ... save_symphony(..., asset_class=asset_class)`). `candidate_tree` is `proposal["candidate_tree"]` — the persisted, DB-JSON-round-tripped candidate tree already in scope at that call site (no new read).

**Precedence (final, post-Revise-3):**
1. A present, non-empty top-level `asset_class` string is DECISIVE — a case-exact member of the new module constant `_COMPOSER_ASSET_CLASSES = ("EQUITIES", "CRYPTO", "OPTIONS")` (sourced from `docs/research/composer/baseline__2026-05-12.md:86`'s holdings-response schema, `"asset_class": "EQUITIES|CRYPTO|OPTIONS"`) is returned verbatim; an out-of-enum string still decides the outcome (falls back to `"EQUITIES"`) — **either way the `asset_classes` array is never consulted once a present string is found.**
2. The `asset_classes` array is consulted ONLY when the top-level value is absent/empty/non-string: a non-empty list whose elements are ALL the same in-enum string is used; a mixed, out-of-enum, empty, non-list array, or an array containing any non-string element (a shape malformation, not a discarded value) falls back to `"EQUITIES"`.
3. `candidate_tree` not a dict, or any internal read error → `"EQUITIES"` (D-1 never-raises).

**Observability:** `logger.warning` fires (a) when a present, in-shape value is discarded to the `EQUITIES` fallback (an out-of-enum top-level string, or a mixed/out-of-enum `asset_classes` array of strings), and (b) whenever the final derived result is non-`EQUITIES` (`CRYPTO`/`OPTIONS`) — flagging that live Composer acceptance of that value is unverified. Normal absence (no key, empty array/string) and shape malformations stay silent — those are absence/malformation, not a discarded value.

### `[PM-ASSUMED]` design ruling

Derive the asset class at the CALL SITE (`approve_frontrunner_proposal`), not inside `save_symphony`. `composer_draft_client.py`'s deliberate "pass `raw_value` through UNCHANGED, never inspect it" transport contract stays intact — the domain derivation belongs in the builder module, which understands symphony trees; the client stays a dumb transport. `_DEFAULT_ASSET_CLASS` remains `save_symphony`'s param default for any other/future caller that omits `asset_class` explicitly. Undisputed at implementation — no team-lead pushback.

### Cycle history (base → Revise 2 → Revise 3 → comment cleanup)

**Base cycle (`a601a679`):** derive+thread `asset_class` into `save_symphony`, EQUITIES fallback on absence.

**Revise 2 (`c5035fb2`), per `/code-review` round 1 findings F1/F2/F4:** added the two WARNING log call sites (discard-warning + non-EQUITIES-forwarded-warning) described above — additive logging only, zero change to return values/precedence/the enum/the D-1 contract.

**Revise 3 (`7bc103c4`), per `/code-review` round 2 findings F1/F2/F4:**
- **F1 (real bug, CRITICAL for correctness):** a present, out-of-enum top-level `asset_class` string was correctly logged as a discard-warning but then FELL THROUGH to also inspect the `asset_classes` array — missing the `return "EQUITIES"` that should have followed. This violated the function's own precedence rule ("array consulted ONLY when top-level absent") — an out-of-enum top-level string could, if the array happened to hold a valid in-enum value, have silently produced that array-derived value instead of the documented EQUITIES fallback. Fixed: the top-level-string branch now always returns before the array is ever read.
- **F2 (semantics correction + robustness):** an `asset_classes` array containing any non-string element (e.g. `[1, 1]`, or unhashable dict elements) is now classified a SHAPE MALFORMATION — same category as a non-list `asset_classes` or non-string top-level `asset_class` — and degrades to EQUITIES silently (no warning), reversing part of Revise 2's logic. `all(isinstance(x, str) for x in array)` is checked explicitly BEFORE the `set()`-based dedup, making a `TypeError` from an unhashable element structurally unreachable rather than merely caught by the outer `except`.
- **F4:** added the cross-reference comment on `_COMPOSER_ASSET_CLASSES` noting it must stay consistent with `composer_draft_client._DEFAULT_ASSET_CLASS`, which independently hardcodes the same `"EQUITIES"` default with no shared source-of-truth link between the two (see Limitation (c) below).
- F5 (round-2 finding) required no production change — test-only.

**Comment-cleanup pass (`fa251747`), per `/code-review` round 3 finding F2 (hygiene):** `_resolve_draft_asset_class`'s docstring and two inline comments had drifted into narrating the REVIEW TIMELINE ("Revise 2/3" labels, finding numbers F1/F2, a commit SHA, "/code-review round 1" citations) instead of describing runtime behavior. Rewritten to describe WHAT the function does and WHY the non-obvious branches exist, with zero change-history references left in the source — that incident history belongs in THIS DECISIONS.md entry, not in the code comments. Pure comment/docstring diff, independently confirmed via `git show fa251747` (every changed line is inside a docstring or a `#` comment) — zero logic change.

### Limitations (documented honestly, not swept under)

**(a) Absent-top-level-key population.** ~6 of the 11 real droplet-captured trees (`tests/fixtures/advisors/frontrunner/real_tree_*.json`) lack a top-level `asset_class` key entirely and fall back to `EQUITIES` via precedence rule 3 above — accepted per the feature plan's own AC-2/fallback design; the fix only changes behavior for the tree-carrying population (~5/11).

**(b) Premise caveat — byte-identical on today's real data.** Composer's own research doc (`docs/research/composer/baseline__2026-05-12.md`, lines 86/169/205) flags that Composer's spec still enumerates `CRYPTO` in `asset_class` but a "What's New" search-summary paraphrase (Tier 4, Medium confidence, unconfirmed by direct citation) claims crypto assets/indicators are "no longer supported" on the platform. All 11 of the operator's current real trees resolve to `EQUITIES` either way (via the top-level key or the fallback) — this fix is a **latent-correctness improvement**: it is byte-identical to the pre-fix behavior against today's real symphonies, and only diverges for a hypothetical non-equity incumbent. Live Composer acceptance of a derived non-`EQUITIES` `asset_class` value (whether `CRYPTO` really is rejected platform-side, or `OPTIONS`) remains UNVERIFIED, deferred to the existing operator-gated task-zero live-create test (`advisors/composer_draft_client.py`'s own pending item) — the Revise-2 WARNING log is the loud signal that will surface the first time this path actually fires against real data.

**(c) F4-accepted — no shared source-of-truth constant.** The 4 `"EQUITIES"` fallback-return literals inside `_resolve_draft_asset_class` (and the enum tuple's own first element) are linked to `composer_draft_client._DEFAULT_ASSET_CLASS` only by a cross-reference COMMENT (F4, Revise 3) — not a shared module constant. Both hardcode `"EQUITIES"` independently. ### Revise 4 (PR #128 round-4 `/code-review`, 7 findings against the hardened Revise-3 GREEN, 2026-08-24)

**Trigger.** A fourth independent `/code-review` pass (after the Revise-3 rider above) returned 7 findings (R4-1 through R4-6, plus B1-B3 sub-items) against the shipped Revise-3 state. The core finding: Revise 3's cascade-side stub-marker search (`_contains_stub_marker`, living in `frontrunner_builder.py`) is **disprovable on multi-tier cascades** — both if-children of a multi-tier cascade's root can carry a stub marker when the fire branch itself contains an already-compacted nested tier (the nested tier's OWN compaction step stamps `STUBBED_CORE_CONTINUATION_TICKER` onto ITS continuation, which then sits inside the outer fire branch too) — making the marker-search's "which side is the placeholder" identification genuinely ambiguous on real multi-tier shapes, not just a hypothetical.

**R4-1 — architectural fix: stamp the count at DETECTION time, on the detector, not re-derive it at the builder.** `frontrunner_detector.Cascade` gains two new fields, `signal_logic_node_count: int | None` and `fire_is_else_branch: bool`, computed ONCE inside `detect_frontrunner_cascades` on the PRE-STUB original `root_node` (never the padded compact overlay) via two new detector-level functions:
- `_compute_signal_logic_node_count(if_node) -> int | None` — the if-node itself, plus its fire branch counted for real; a NESTED qualifying if-node (a further scale-in tier, or an internal hedge subgate, identified via `_qualifies_as_cascade_rung(..., is_nested_tier=True)` or `_is_internal_hedge_subgate`) has its OWN continuation excluded via the SAME selection rule applied inline — never a stub-marker search. Returns `None` (never fabricates) when `if_node` isn't a valid 2-child if-node.
- `_compute_fire_is_else_branch(if_node) -> bool` — `True` when the ROOT cascade if-node's fire (signal) side lands on the `is-else-condition?==True` child (inverted polarity). Reads the SAME selection the node-count walk uses (never a second, independent derivation). Root-level only.

`frontrunner_builder._count_signal_logic_nodes`/`_contains_stub_marker` (Revise 3's fix) are **DELETED entirely** — the builder now reads `cascade.signal_logic_node_count` VERBATIM off the detector, never re-deriving it. This is an architectural fix, not a patch: the ambiguity Revise-3's marker-search fallback had to guess around cannot arise at all when the count is computed once, at detection time, directly on the honest pre-stub subtree.

**Shared selection helper.** `_compact_if_node`'s existing fire/continuation size-based split (the smaller-by-node-count direct child is "fire") is extracted into a new `frontrunner_detector._select_fire_and_continuation(node, *, pair=None) -> tuple[dict, dict] | None` — the single source of truth for this selection. `_compact_if_node` itself is refactored to call it (behavior-preserving, verified against all 11 real fixtures unchanged). The new signal-logic walker (`_compute_signal_logic_node_count`) and the dedicated clause-aware counter (`_count_clause_aware_signal_logic`, R4-2/B3) both consume this helper one-directionally — no direct or mutual recursion between any of the new functions (structurally enforced by an AST-based cycle-detection test).

**New `frontrunner_detector._count_clause_aware_signal_logic(node) -> int`** — a general-purpose, non-exclusion node counter that descends `children` AND a compound condition's `condition`/`conditions` DATA fields (this is the ONLY place clause-aware counting lives after Revise 4 — see R4-2). Imported verbatim by `frontrunner_builder` for the overlay-side SIMPLIFY operand (B3), never reimplemented there.

**R4-2 — RULING 3 REVERTED.** `frontrunner_builder._count_tree_nodes` is reverted to a children-only walk. Revise 3's RULING 3 (compound-condition-clause descent) is **superseded**, not merely relocated-with-identical-effect: `_count_tree_nodes`'s ONLY remaining consumer is the whole-symphony `node_count_delta` gate (RULING 2's coarse did-it-grow-at-all check) — clause-aware counting for the SIMPLIFY-path operands that actually need it now lives exclusively in the new, dedicated `frontrunner_detector._count_clause_aware_signal_logic` (imported, never duplicated). **Both `DECISIONS.md`'s Revise-3 RULING-3 section above and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s frontrunner-cluster key-files row (pre this doc pass) incorrectly implied this reversion never happened — corrected by this doc pass; see the `[SUPERSEDED, Revise 4]` annotation appended to the RULING-3 bullet above.**

**R4-3/R4-6 — `_count_overlay_node_count` simplified to a single tier.** `compiled_tree` absent is now an UNCONDITIONAL `None` (the fresh-compile and already-compiled-candidate fallback tiers from the original cycle and Revise 3 are deleted as unreachable dead code under the real call graph — the sole caller, `_run_build_for_symphony`, always has `compiled_tree` populated). Overlay-side fire/continuation identification now reuses the EXISTING production `_find_terminal_else_child` instead of a bespoke stub-marker search (a compiled overlay candidate is never detector-compacted, so its else slot is always identifiable via `is-else-condition?==True` alone — no stub-marker ambiguity can arise on this side, ever). The fire-child lookup is an explicit `next((c for c in node.get("children") or [] if c is not else_child), None)` (B1) — never a bare `next()` that could raise `StopIteration` on an aliased-duplicate-children shape and silently fall through to the outer except-all at DEBUG level; an aliased-duplicate shape now DECLINES with a WARNING instead.

**R4-5/B2 — node-count-operand hardening in `frontrunner_acceptance.py`.** `_safe_node_count_float` gains an `is_integer()` check (a node count is never legitimately a non-whole float — `3.7` nodes is meaningless; a genuinely whole-number float like `20.0` is still accepted). New `_safe_node_count_int(value) -> int | None` hardens RULING 2's own operands (`incumbent_node_count`/`candidate_node_count`, feeding `node_count_delta`) — `bool` rejected explicitly, `None`/non-numeric-string degrades via the natural `int()` `TypeError`/`ValueError`, caught here rather than escaping to `evaluate_calmar_acceptance`'s outer catch-all (which would null every OTHER reporting field, not just `node_count_delta`). A genuinely numeric string (e.g. `"50"`) is still accepted.

**Final pin — `fire_is_else_branch` gates SIMPLIFY.** `evaluate_calmar_acceptance` gains a `fire_is_else_branch: bool = False` keyword-only param, threaded verbatim from `cascade.fire_is_else_branch` through `_gate_and_accept_candidate`'s matching new kwarg. When `True` (the cascade's fire content sits on the untrustworthy `is-else-condition?==True` side), SIMPLIFY declines unconditionally with a WARNING, regardless of what the ratio/whole-tree-no-growth gates alone would say — since `_graft_incumbent_core`'s core-preservation logic assumes normal polarity and would silently drop the real core for this shape. **This scope (SIMPLIFY only) is exactly what Revise 5's F1 finding below corrects** — Revise 4 left the IMPROVE/performance path reachable unconditionally, regardless of polarity.

**Scope boundaries.** Endpoints touched: none (advisory-only, off-execution-path, no HTTP/API surface). Fixture provenance: n/a — pure logic-layer fix over synthetic/real-fixture detector trees already in `tests/fixtures/advisors/frontrunner/`. `MATERIAL_SIMPLIFICATION_MAX_RATIO=0.50` unchanged (as in every prior revision of this cycle).

### Revise 5 (PR #128 round-4 `/code-review`, 7 findings against Revise-4 GREEN `d9983434`, 2026-08-25)

**Trigger.** The SAME round-4 `/code-review` pass, re-run against the Revise-4 GREEN, returned 7 further findings (F1-F7) — dispatched directly via `SendMessage` (no separate `feature-plans/` doc; the full RED-plan approval transcript, including the required F2/F4 first-principles derivation, lives in the team-lead/fps-test-writer session message history and is reproduced in `.claude/tdd-handoff.md`).

**F1 (real behavior change) — inverted-polarity fail-closed must cover BOTH acceptance paths, not just SIMPLIFY.** Root cause (confirmed): `if candidate_calmar > incumbent_calmar: tags.add("performance")` ran UNCONDITIONALLY, before the `fire_is_else_branch` check Revise 4 added — which only gated SIMPLIFY. An inverted-polarity candidate (fire content on the untrustworthy `is-else-condition?==True` side — `_graft_incumbent_core` silently drops the real core for this polarity) with a merely-BETTER Calmar still got `accepted=True`, tagged `{"performance"}`, and queued for operator approval on a REAL Composer draft creation. **Fix (team-lead ruling, binding):** when `fire_is_else_branch=True`, decline the WHOLE acceptance fail-closed — `accepted=False`, `tags=set()` (neither "performance" nor "simplification") — with a `logger.warning(...)`, WITHOUT nulling the other reporting fields (`candidate_sharpe`, `candidate_volatility`, `incumbent_calmar`, `candidate_calmar`, `node_count_delta` all stay genuinely computed — no early return; the final `AcceptanceResult(...)` construction is still reached with every field populated). Landed by restructuring `evaluate_calmar_acceptance` to `if fire_is_else_branch: <warning> else: <IMPROVE check>; <SIMPLIFY check>` — moving the previously-unconditional `if candidate_calmar > incumbent_calmar` block inside the new `else`.

**F2/F4 (BINDING — DO NOT UNIFY, docstring-only, zero counting-logic change) — the two SIMPLIFY operand counters are two intentionally-asymmetric, correct-by-design policies, not a bug.** The cascade-side counter (`frontrunner_detector._compute_signal_logic_node_count`, stamping `Cascade.signal_logic_node_count`) EXCLUDES a nested qualifying tier's OWN continuation ENTIRELY, at EVERY nesting level — never counted at all, regardless of size. The overlay-side counter (`frontrunner_builder._count_overlay_node_count` → `frontrunner_detector._count_clause_aware_signal_logic`) counts EVERYTHING under the fire child, EXCLUDING ONLY the OUTERMOST placeholder-else — a nested tier's own else IS counted. **This is a genuine trust asymmetry, not an oversight:** the overlay (candidate) side is MANUFACTURED by us (Fable → our compiler) — `_find_terminal_else_child`'s own docstring documents a manufacturing-time guarantee: tiers nest ONLY inside `'then'`; a nested tier's own `'else'` is real lower-intensity hedge content, NEVER a placeholder — verified against real fixtures and the module's own flagship 2-tier worked example, so counting it is structurally safe (no core-content smuggling is possible on a self-generated candidate). The cascade (incumbent) side is DETECTED and untrusted — `_is_internal_hedge_subgate`'s own docstring documents a REAL core-leak risk: a nested continuation can genuinely be unrelated core-strategy bulk (thousands of nodes) — the exact defect class `DE-FR-SIMPLIFY-001` exists to prevent (Revise 3's stub-padding-bulk regression: "admitting oversized overlays"). Excluding at every qualifying nesting level is the conservative, fail-closed choice. **Risk-asymmetry rationale for why conservative wins on this side specifically:** over-excluding a genuine small nested-tier continuation on the cascade side costs a few nodes (bounded, small); under-excluding (counting it) risks unboundedly inflating the denominator with real core bulk if the documented leak risk materializes (unbounded, large) — bounded-small-cost beats unbounded-large-risk for untrusted input, a different risk profile than the candidate side's structural guarantee. **Unifying the two counters would REINTRODUCE the Revise-3 CRITICAL fail-open regression** (untrusted core bulk inflating the "replaced logic" denominator → admits oversized overlays) — explicitly NOT done. Both fixtures pinning the asymmetry use IDENTICAL tier structure/tickers/wrappers so the diff isolates cleanly to the one structural difference: cascade-side count `6` (excludes a nested tier's own else, 4 nodes, plus the outer's 202-node real core); overlay-side count `10` (includes the same 4 nodes) — diff exactly 4, the nested tier's own else subtree. **F4's `condition`/`conditions` fold-in confirmed NOT a real gap:** `_compute_signal_logic_node_count`'s general branch reads only `current.get("condition")` (singular); grepping all 6 real fixtures under `tests/fixtures/advisors/frontrunner/` for the literal string `"conditions"` confirmed every occurrence is reached exclusively via a wrapping `"condition"` key (matching `symphony_schema.make_compound_condition`'s own construction) — since the walk delegates the ENTIRE subtree to `_count_clause_aware_signal_logic` as soon as it finds ANY `.get("condition")` dict, and `"conditions"` never appears without that wrapper, this is dead code under the real schema, not a functional undercount; pinned positively (not just negatively) by a nested-tier-compound-condition test with a hand-derived `7 + n_clauses` formula. Landed as 3 verbatim docstring insertions (`frontrunner_acceptance.py`'s module docstring inside the "2. PRESERVE + SIMPLIFY" bullet; `evaluate_calmar_acceptance`'s own "Public surface" description; `frontrunner_builder.py`'s `_count_overlay_node_count` docstring) — zero diff to `_compute_signal_logic_node_count`, `_compute_fire_is_else_branch`, `_count_overlay_node_count`'s counting logic, or `_count_clause_aware_signal_logic` (confirmed by grepping the diff for all 4 names: every hit lands inside an added comment/docstring line, never a code line).

**F3 — `OverflowError` escapes `_safe_node_count_int`, nulls every other reporting field.** Confirmed directly against the interpreter: `int(float("inf"))` raises `OverflowError`, not caught by the prior `except (TypeError, ValueError)` — escaped to `evaluate_calmar_acceptance`'s outer catch-all → bare `_rejected()` → nulled `candidate_sharpe`/`candidate_volatility`/both Calmars AND fabricated `node_count_delta=0` (the `_rejected()` default, not an honest `None`). Identical for `numpy.float64("inf")` and `decimal.Decimal("Infinity")`. ### Revise 7 — SPLICE POLARITY DEFECT: `_graft_incumbent_core` sourced from the detector's own fire/continuation selection (separate branch, Toxic-Pair TDD cycle, 2026-08-25)

**Trigger.** Not a `/code-review` finding — PM-driven reconnaissance (pre-cycle) on the already-shipped `DE-FR-SIMPLIFY-001` construction path found a LIVE bug in `_graft_incumbent_core` (`frontrunner_builder.py`, unrelated to any Revise 1-6 change, present since the original wave-2 splice code): it selects the incumbent's "real core" to preserve during a splice by hardcoding a search for the `is-else-condition?==True` child — i.e. it assumes the else side is always core. But fire/continuation selection (`frontrunner_detector._select_fire_and_continuation`) is purely SIZE-based (fire = the smaller of the two direct children), independent of which side carries the `is-else-condition?` marker. On an INVERTED-polarity cascade — the `real_tree_09`/`n2oo` class, the same shape `fire_is_else_branch` (Revise 4/5, above) exists to flag — fire content genuinely lands on the `is-else==True` side because it happens to be the smaller branch. The old graft read "is-else==True" as "the real core" and grafted the FIRE content in as if it were core, silently dropping the actual (larger) real core on the other side. `symphony_schema.validate_tree` never caught it — the corrupted tree is still structurally well-formed, just semantically wrong — so a real Composer backtest could run on the corrupted tree. This was firewalled from shipping only by Revise 5's F1 `fire_is_else_branch` fail-closed acceptance decline (documented there as covering the acceptance-policy symptom; the construction-level root cause was left unfixed and untracked as its own item until this cycle).

**Fix (Option C — single source of truth, per this feature's established no-duplication ruling, Revise 6).** `_graft_incumbent_core` now sources the incumbent's real core from `frontrunner_detector._select_fire_and_continuation(original_node)`'s `continuation_child` — the SAME size-based selection the detector itself uses — instead of an independent `is-else-condition?==True` search. No size comparison is reimplemented in the builder; it delegates entirely to the detector's one existing implementation. On a normal-polarity cascade the continuation child IS the `is-else==True` child, so output is byte-unchanged there. Never-raises contract preserved: a `None` selection (a node shaped unexpectedly, or one `_select_fire_and_continuation` can't resolve to a fire/continuation pair) degrades to the existing unchanged-`compiled_node` fallback path, unchanged from before.

**Scope held.** `advisors/frontrunner_builder.py` only (28 insertions / 20 deletions, docstring + one selection call) — zero diff to `frontrunner_detector.py`, `frontrunner_acceptance.py`, or any engine/analytics module. `_graft_incumbent_core`'s 2-arg signature and `splice_candidate_into_symphony`'s call site are unchanged.

**Explicitly NOT touched — the acceptance-side firewall stays exactly as Revise 5 left it.** `frontrunner_acceptance.evaluate_calmar_acceptance`'s `fire_is_else_branch=True` fail-closed decline (Revise 4's SIMPLIFY-only gate, widened to the whole acceptance decision by Revise 5's F1) is UNCHANGED — inverted-polarity candidates STILL decline unconditionally (`accepted=False`, `tags=set()`). This cycle fixes CONSTRUCTION correctness (the splice itself no longer drops core content, on any polarity), not acceptance policy — the two are now independent, both-required safeguards rather than correctness depending entirely on the acceptance-side decline catching every inverted-polarity case.

**Tests.** `tests/advisors/test_frontrunner_graft_polarity.py` (new, 4 tests, RED `00756c6f` -> GREEN `2d957f2e`): unit-level (`test_graft_incumbent_core_preserves_real_core_on_inverted_polarity_cascade`) and wiring-level (`test_splice_candidate_into_symphony_preserves_real_core_on_inverted_polarity_incumbent`) RED pins against a local, oracle-independent inverted-polarity fixture (`is-else==False` side = 21-leaf real core `{SVXY, HEDGEPAD00..19}`; `is-else==True` side = 2-leaf fire `{VXX, UVIX}`) — pre-fix confirmed grafting `{VXX, UVIX}` instead of the real core; both now PASS. Matching normal-polarity no-regression pins (`test_graft_incumbent_core_normal_polarity_unchanged`, `test_splice_candidate_into_symphony_normal_polarity_unchanged`) PASS unmodified both before and after the fix, confirming the detector's `continuation_child` and the old is-else search agree on that shape. Fixture builders are LOCAL to the test file (not imported from `test_frontrunner_detector_r4_signal_logic.py`), each returning `(if_node, real_core_tickers)` so every assertion compares against the actual asset tickers used to build the fixture, never a re-typed literal.

**Verified.** sp-test-writer + sp-reviewer independently: `tests/advisors/test_frontrunner_graft_polarity.py` 4/4 passed; wider suite (`test_frontrunner_builder.py` + `test_frontrunner_real_boundary_contract.py` + `test_frontrunner_detector_r4_signal_logic.py` + `test_frontrunner_detector.py` + `test_frontrunner_acceptance.py`, `-n0`): 152 passed, 1 xfail (pre-existing, unrelated, `DE-FR-SIGNALS-001`). **doc-writer independent re-verification (2026-08-25, not relaying test-writer's own reported counts):** fresh `python -m pytest tests/advisors/test_frontrunner_graft_polarity.py -n0 -q` at HEAD `64f1fa90` — **4 passed, 0 failed**.
