## DE-CLOSED-BOUNCE-001 — Closed-market cumulative-return bounce: guard-alpha fallback's unguarded side effect on the lifetime row (2026-08-25)

Branch: `fix/closed-market-cumulative-bounce` | Base: `82657b96` (pre-cycle main) | HEAD: `8b0ad603`

### Problem

On the closed_frozen `/api/state` route (market closed, serving the EOD snapshot), the "Cumulative · lifetime" comparison row on the dashboard bounced between the correct account-basis lifetime value (~63.95%, matching Composer) and an incorrect VW-windowed value (~27.56%) on every ~30 s poll cycle.

### Root cause — two legs, both required to produce the bounce

**Leg 1 (server, structural trigger):** the closed_frozen branch's inline `_portfolio_strip` dict (`app.py`, built directly from `analytics.get_portfolio_cumulative_return_account_basis()` etc., never via `_compute_portfolio_strip()`/`compute_windowed_portfolio_strip()`) never set `guard_alpha` or `window` at all. This differs from the live-poll path, which has always populated a default-window `guard_alpha`/`window` pair (`app.py:1859-1881`) alongside its own account-basis `cumulative_return`.

**Leg 2 (client, the race):** `renderGuardAlpha()` (`static/index.js`) falls back to `fetchWindowedStrip('30d')` whenever `ps.guard_alpha` isn't a number — which, per Leg 1, was true on EVERY closed-market poll, not just an edge case. `fetchWindowedStrip()` wraps `/api/strip/<window>`'s response (whose `cumulative_return` field is windowed VW-basis, from `analytics.compute_windowed_portfolio_strip`) and calls BOTH `renderGuardAlpha()` (intended) AND `updateComparisonRows()` (unintended side effect) with it. `updateComparisonRows()` sourced the lifetime-labeled row from `ps.cumulative_return` with no discriminator between a genuine `/api/state` poll payload (account-basis, correct) and the windowed-strip wrapped payload (VW-basis, wrong for a "lifetime" label) — so on every closed-market poll cycle, two writers raced to the same DOM row, and whichever of `/api/state` / `/api/strip/30d` resolved last on that tick won.

This is a DIFFERENT bug from F-014 (`DE-DISPLAY-TRUTH-001`, 2026-07-21, shipped and still in effect): F-014 was `updateComparisonRows()` itself explicitly preferring a `windowed_cumulative_return` field over `cumulative_return` — that preference is gone from current code and F-014's fix is not implicated here. This bug is a *different* function's fallback (`renderGuardAlpha`) reaching into `updateComparisonRows()` as an unguarded side effect, structurally triggered on every closed-market poll by Leg 1.

**A misleading comment made the bug harder to spot.** The pre-fix comment at `static/index.js:161-166` claimed fetching the windowed strip populated the cumulative row "with correct windowed VW values" — the exact wrong mental model that produced the bounce; a windowed value is never correct under a row SSR-labeled "Cumulative · lifetime" (`templates/index.html:961`).

### Fix — both legs closed

**Leg 1 (`app.py`, +33 lines):** the closed_frozen branch's happy-path `_portfolio_strip` construction gains its own `try`/`except` block (deliberately separate from the surrounding try, so a failure here can't discard the already-computed `today_change`/`cumulative_return`/`max_drawdown`) that mirrors the live path's own default-window strip computation (`app.py:1859-1881`): calls `analytics.compute_windowed_portfolio_strip(_snap_symphonies_list, _snap_bot_state, window=_DEFAULT_HERO_WINDOW, conn=_frozen_shadow_conn)` and, on success, sets `guard_alpha` (float or `None`), `window` (string), and — for shape parity with the live path, not currently consumed client-side (see `docs/generated/static_index_js.md`) — `windowed_cumulative_return`. `guard_alpha` can still legitimately be `None` here (e.g. `weight_sum==0`, or this new block's own `except` firing) — the Leg-2 fallback path remains necessary for that genuine edge case, it's just no longer the every-poll default.

**Leg 2 (`static/index.js`):** `updateComparisonRows()` no longer includes the `cumulative` row in its `rows` array unconditionally. `rows` starts as `[today, mdd]`; the `cumulative` row entry is spliced in at index 1 ONLY when `'data_as_of' in ps` — reusing the exact discriminator `DE-AUDIT-BL4-001` established for the account-basis chip/freshness helpers in this same function (`data_as_of` is set by every genuine `/api/state` producer, never by the windowed-strip producer). On a `fetchWindowedStrip` wrapped payload, the cumulative row is skipped entirely by `rows.forEach` — its DOM elements are left untouched rather than being overwritten with a windowed value (or flickered to an honest-empty state and back). This applies uniformly to EVERY caller of `updateComparisonRows`, including the window-picker click handler — a windowed value is wrong under a "lifetime" label regardless of who triggered the windowed-strip fetch. The misleading `renderGuardAlpha` comment (`:161-166`) is rewritten to describe the corrected behavior and why `guard_alpha` can still be null.

**Live visual gate (bounce-ux) — APPROVED, 4/4 scenarios PASS** (reported by bounce-ux via team-lead, not independently re-run by this doc-writer):
1. **Happy path:** `guard_alpha` populates from the server leg → `/api/strip/30d` never auto-fires → Cumulative row stable at the account-basis figure (~63.95% class), zero console errors.
2. **Sparse-shadow-history / `guard_alpha=None`:** `/api/strip/30d` DOES still fire (the genuine edge case) — 200+ high-frequency samples + a `MutationObserver` confirm the Cumulative row never flips and never blanks to an empty state. This is the decisive proof that the CLIENT leg (the `data_as_of` row-gate), not just the server leg, is the actual bounce guarantee — the server fix alone doesn't cover every case (see "Why both legs matter" below).
3. Blank/`"--"` flicker explicitly ruled out — zero occurrences across both scenarios above.
4. **Window-picker click (60d):** `/api/strip/60d` fires; Cumulative row records zero DOM mutations — the row-gate holds uniformly for every caller, not just the passive fallback.

**Why both legs matter (not redundant):** `guard_alpha` can legitimately resolve `None` in production even with the server fix in place — a new symphony, or a window with fewer than 2 recorded `shadow_history` days (the AC-8b "insufficient data, not zero" floor; see `TestClosedFrozenNullGuardAlphaIsLegitimate`, commit `8b0ad603`). In that case the client fallback DOES fire (scenario 2 above), and the client-side row-gate is what actually prevents the bounce, not the server leg — the server leg only makes the fallback rare instead of universal.

**Scope note [SUPERSEDED, Revise round — see below]:** this doc-pass originally claimed only the "Cumulative · lifetime" row needed the `data_as_of` gate, with Today/MDD safely ungated because their values were "not window-parameterized." That claim was WRONG and is corrected by the Revise round below: `PR #136`'s `/code-review` (finding #1) traced a real divergence on `today_change` too (it genuinely IS account-basis on a real poll vs. always-VW on the windowed strip, when the account cache is warm), and a real scope-mismatch risk on `max_drawdown`. All three rows are now gated uniformly. Left in place, struck through in spirit rather than deleted, so a reader following this entry's history sees the correction rather than a silently vanished (and wrong) claim.

**Window-picker behavior, explicit (bounce-impl) [SUPERSEDED, Revise round — see below]:** clicking a time-window button still re-windows the Today/MDD rows and the guard-alpha headline; it intentionally does NOT re-window the Cumulative row (structural correction, not a regression) — that row's SSR label is hard-coded "Cumulative · lifetime" (`templates/index.html:958-961`), and a windowed value would misrepresent it regardless of what triggered the fetch. **Correction (Revise round, finding #3):** this was accurate for HEAD `8b0ad603` only. As of `faebc986`, the picker click re-windows ONLY the guard-alpha headline — none of the three comparison rows (Today/Cumulative/MDD) re-window on a picker click any more, not just Cumulative.

### Revise round — gate all 3 comparison rows, drop dead field (PR #136 `/code-review` findings #1/#2/#3, 2026-08-25)

**Trigger.** `/code-review` on PR #136 found the original cycle's client-side fix incomplete (finding #1, "most serious"): only the `cumulative` row was gated on the `data_as_of` discriminator. Reviewer traced that when `guard_alpha` is genuinely `null` even with the server leg fixed (sparse `shadow_history` / new symphony / an except-fallback — a real, non-hypothetical case), `renderGuardAlpha`'s fallback still fires and rewrites the `today` and `mdd` rows from the windowed strip too — the identical bounce class the original cycle left unguarded on those two rows. Confirmed mechanism: `today_change` genuinely IS account-basis on a real closed-market poll when the account cache is warm (via `analytics.get_portfolio_today_change_account_basis`), vs. always-VW on `compute_windowed_portfolio_strip` — the same divergence class as the original cumulative-row bug. `max_drawdown` has no account-basis blend function anywhere in `analytics.py` (independently confirmed by this doc-writer: `grep -n "^def get_portfolio_" analytics.py` finds `get_portfolio_cumulative_return_account_basis`/`get_portfolio_today_change_account_basis` but no `get_portfolio_max_drawdown_account_basis`), so its divergence risk is a trading-day/snapshot-vs-picker-window scope mismatch rather than a basis-blend one — but the same `data_as_of` gate protects it regardless of which mechanism would produce the mismatch.

**Fix.** `static/index.js`'s `updateComparisonRows` now builds `rows` ALL-OR-NOTHING: `var rows = [];` by default, replaced with the full `[today, cumulative, mdd]` array only inside `if ('data_as_of' in ps)` (previously: `rows` unconditionally held `[today, mdd]`, with only `cumulative` conditionally spliced in). A windowed-strip wrapped payload therefore now leaves ALL THREE rows' DOM untouched, not just Cumulative's. `app.py`'s closed_frozen default-window block (finding #2) drops its `windowed_cumulative_return` assignment — genuinely dead now that no comparison row is ever sourced from a windowed-strip payload at all; the pre-existing live-path assignment of the same field (`_compute_portfolio_strip`, `app.py:1877-1879`) is untouched code-wise (out of this cycle's scope; only its stale comment corrected) — see `docs/generated/app.md` for why this is deliberately asymmetric, including a doc-writer correction to the "shape parity with `/api/strip/<window>`" framing (that route's own response has never carried a `windowed_cumulative_return` key at all — it's `compute_windowed_portfolio_strip`'s raw 8-key dict). Finding #3 corrects the window-picker click handler's stale "re-windows the three vs-rows" comments in `static/index.js` (now false after finding #1) to state plainly that none of the three rows re-window on a picker click, only the guard-alpha headline does.

**Test-file robustness (finding #4, #5 — not production code).** `tests/app/test_closed_market_cumulative_bounce.py`: `app_module._account_totals_cache`/`_account_totals_last_good` are module-global dicts two tests mutate with no teardown, an order-dependent flake risk (finding #4) — fixed with a `_clean_account_totals_cache` fixture (clears before AND after every test) composed into both `frozen_client`/`open_client`. `tests/dashboard/test_closed_market_bounce_js.py`: the single-row discriminator test is generalized to `@pytest.mark.parametrize(row_id=["today", "cumulative", "mdd"])`; its `_slice_row_entry` helper is rewritten from a naive `body.find('},', row_anchor)` forward scan to proper bidirectional brace-matching (finding #5) — the naive scan could stop early at an empty-object `|| {}` fallback inside the row entry, or over-span past the entry's real boundary into trailing code if the entry's shape ever changed, either way letting a stray `data_as_of`/`basis` token spuriously satisfy the discriminator check.
